CMC Ludhiana is definitely among the leading private medical colleges in the country. As a final-year MBBS student here, I'll break down my experience to help you understand better.

Teaching/Lectures: In my experience, the quality of lectures tends to dip as you move from first year to the final year, though there are exceptions. During my first year, I found every lecture to be engaging and educational, with teachers actively encouraging us to study and helping us with doubts during tutorials and discussions. Regular weekly and monthly tests were also a part of the routine, which kept me focused during the first two years. By the third year, when clinical subjects start, professors are often busy with their patients, so sometimes PG residents take over the classes. However, whenever professors do teach, it's always valuable. In the last two years, written tests become less frequent, and there is less personal attention, which in a way, helps us become more independent.

Teaching/Clinical Postings: We start clinical postings in the second year, initially focusing more on theory, which makes sense since we are just beginning. By the third year, things start to click, and professors are patient and eager to teach. With a large number of patients, we get to experience both outpatient and inpatient care across various departments. CMC graduates are known for their excellent clinical skills due to the strong focus on hands-on experience, especially in the final year.

Student-Teacher Relationship: The college has a unique student-teacher relationship, thanks to foster families that link us with faculty, as well as juniors and seniors. You can rely on your teachers for support during personal crises and guidance whenever needed. The open communication and approachable faculty were a pleasant surprise for me when I started.

Infrastructure: There's room for improvement here. While some hospital departments are well-equipped, the classrooms need upgrading. However, some new hostel rooms are quite nice. Recently, the institute subscribed to UpToDate and Clinical Key for all students, which have been incredibly valuable resources.

Extracurricular Activities: While not as extensive as some other colleges, we do have an annual musical, which MBBS students completely produce, from writing the script to composing the music. The administration is also very supportive, allowing us to attend conferences or participate in academic exchanges through groups like AMSA-India.

Research: One of the major benefits of CMC is the chance for undergraduates to engage in meaningful research projects, either through ICMR STS or independently. It's all about discovering your passion and finding a great mentor to guide you.

It sounds like you're asking about your NEET All India Rank. If that's the case, then with a rank of 257, you've got a good shot at getting into CMC Ludhiana. However, it really depends on how many candidates show up for the counseling sessions.

Both CMC campuses have a limited number of seats, with 100 available in Vellore and 75 in Ludhiana. After the reservation process, Vellore offers 16 seats for the All India Quota, while Ludhiana has 13. Keep in mind, this information is specifically for non-Christian applicants without any reservations.

KMC Manipal is the better option in my opinion. It offers more opportunities for research compared to CMC Ludhiana. Many students from KMC Manipal have successfully entered residency programs in the USA, and have become outstanding doctors in countries like the USA, Canada, and the UK.

A great example is Dr. Ranjit Varghese, a pediatric orthopedic specialist. He graduated from Kasturba Medical College at Manipal University in Mangalore, India, and did his residency there too. He then completed a fellowship in orthopedic oncology at Harvard Medical School. It's impressive because getting into Harvard is a big deal, and not even students from AIIMS, New Delhi, often achieve this. Dr. Varghese now works at Johns Hopkins.

Similarly, Dr. Devi Prasad Shetty, a renowned cardiac surgeon and the founder of Narayana Health, also studied at KMC Mangalore. He's performed over 15,000 heart surgeries and received prestigious awards like the Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan for his contributions to affordable healthcare.

On the other hand, CMC Ludhiana focuses on preparing students for mission work and serving in rural areas, which is very noble. However, it offers fewer research opportunities. There’s also a mandatory two-year service bond in rural areas after graduation, which can delay further studies like an MD.

In terms of ranking, KMC is 5th among Indian medical colleges, while CMC Ludhiana is 18th. The fee at CMC Ludhiana is around 50 lakhs for the full MBBS course, with a 10% increase annually, plus the bond requirement. KMC's fee is about 58 lakhs in total, with no yearly increment.

Ultimately, choose the college that aligns with your goals. If your passion is social service, CMC Ludhiana is ideal. If you're aiming for further studies abroad, consider AIIMS, KMC Manipal, or their Mangalore campus. Both colleges have their strengths, so choose wisely without letting the cost be the main factor. After all, once you're a doctor, you can repay your parents for their support.

I'm currently doing my MD at AIIMS, New Delhi, and my brother, who just took the NEET, is considering CMC Ludhiana but prefers AIIMS or KMC Manipal to pursue USMLE and residency in the USA. Both colleges have their merits, but your choice should reflect your future aspirations.

Christian Dental College, located on the CMC Ludhiana campus, ranks among India's top ten dental schools. It's been around for 26 years, building on the 130-year tradition of CMC. There are 40 spots available, with only eight open for the General Category. Baba Farid University Of Health Sciences Faridkot oversees the admission counseling process. The college is known for its outstanding faculty, great facilities, and plenty of clinical opportunities. Plus, unlike many other dental schools, it has a dedicated medical team due to its connection with a medical college. If you're thinking about pursuing a BDS and get a chance here, it's definitely worth considering.
I'm in my second year at CMC Ludhiana now, and I can say it's a fun place to be. The first year can be pretty busy because there's a lot to cover in the syllabus in a short time.
Our classes run from 8 AM to 4 PM, and we study Anatomy, Physiology, Biochemistry, and Ethics. We have a diverse group of 75 students in our class.
The hostels are really nice, much better than those at government colleges, and the students manage the mess. The food is decent.
The professors here are very knowledgeable and experienced. They might seem a bit strict, but it's to help us do well academically. Thanks to their efforts, I even got a university rank.
The one downside is the campus isn't very green. I have to walk through a busy road with a lot of traffic every morning from the hostel to the college.
Despite that, life is exciting with things like socializing in the anatomy dissection hall, practicals, and going out with friends. We have crazy hostel parties, too. It's a great experience!

VIIT Vishakhapatnam is ranked 201-300 in B.Tech by NIRF in 2024 out of 300 colleges in India.

VIIT offers a range of programs, including a B.Tech and M.Tech degree with eleven and eight specializations. Apart from that, the college also offers an MBA and an MCA degree course. Candidates can seek admission to B.Tech and M.Tech after appearing in the EAMCET and PGECET entrance exams, respectively. For MBA and MCA, admissions will be conducted through the Integrated Common Entrance Test (ICET). VIIT's flagship course is B.Tech, with a first-year fee of INR 68,700. The library and computer lab are well-equipped, but there's no auditorium, so students head into town for larger gatherings. Hostel rooms are basic, not luxury but not bad either. The food in the mess is hit or miss, with some quality issues—once, over 100 students got sick from spoiled daal. Mess charges aren't in the fees, and buying from different vendors can get pricey.

Sports facilities are just okay. There's a cricket field, but it often floods because of the heavy rains in Manipal. Overall, the infrastructure is solid, and classes are split into two shifts to fit everyone in.
Faculty: The teaching staff is pretty average. A few stand out as excellent, but some don't handle criticism well. The administration is strict and not too student-friendly.

Rules and Regulations: Rules are a big deal here. TAPMI is firm with them. Getting permission to go home or for a night out involves a lot of paperwork, making you rethink the whole idea. Curfew is strict, holidays are few, dress codes can be annoying, and missing out on placements is a real threat they follow through on.

Campus Life: You can hang out with friends on campus for as long as you want. There are some festivals and activities, but they're not as exciting compared to other colleges. Joining inter-college competitions is tough because faculty prioritize attendance.
City Life: Manipal is a small town with a few pubs and bars, nothing extravagant. There are some nearby eateries, but not much else going on. That doesn't bother me much though.
Crowd: Most students are GEM, with many from the South; not as many from the North. It's quite a diverse mix.

Placements: Here's the big topic. There's a 100% placement rate, but the average figures, especially for summer placements, are a bit exaggerated. Everyone gets internships, though not all are paid. Job profiles are average, and the location is a downside during placements. However, the placement committee works really hard. The large batch size is a challenge for placements.

Ranking: Don't rely too much on rankings; they can be misleading. Competitors are FORE and GIM. FORE has an edge due to its location, which helps during placements. TAPMI is a tier-two school, with location and batch size as major challenges. Schools like IMT, XIMB, IMI, and IRMA are a step above.
Alumni: TAPMI has some notable alumni, including CFOs and CMOs, and a strong alumni network.

Overall, TAPMI has decent infrastructure, reasonable fees (though mess and electricity charges are extra), and good placements given its location and ranking—but keep your expectations realistic. The faculty is just okay, and some societies are more about boosting your resume than actual involvement. The quizzing culture isn't strong, and metro cities do better in that regard. Management can be overly strict, which can be a problem if it becomes counterproductive. The location is a bit remote, with the nearest airport in Mangalore, requiring a taxi to Manipal that costs over 1300. In my opinion, location and batch size are key factors for tier-two colleges, and TAPMI falls short in these areas.

I wouldn't recommend going for a tier-two college if you're taking out a loan; it might be better to try the CAT exam again. If you have a high CAT score, you might qualify for a scholarship at TAPMI, but I'm not sure if that would be your top choice.
I hope this gives you a clear and fair picture.

I would say TAPMI has its own charm, especially in the MBA program. The faculty here are well-qualified, and the learning experience is great. The placement rate is 100%, and they have good companies visiting, like Deloitte and ITC. The average package is around 14.6 lakh, which is decent. I haven’t been to IIM, but from what I hear, they have their own advantages. TAPMI might not have the same brand recognition as IIM, but it’s definitely competitive in its own right.

1. If you're deciding based on financial returns after a PGDM, staying in your current job might be better unless you get into an IIM. As an engineer with 3-4 years of experience, you can earn around 8-10 lakh per year. Spending 12-14 lakh on an MBA for an average package of 9-10 lakh annually might not be the best financial move.
2. Many graduates end up in IT roles like business analysts or consultants, which are also available to engineering grads.

3. TAPMI isn't as recognized in the corporate world as some other schools like IMT, XIMB, or GIM. Even people in your office or locals in Karnataka might not know much about it, despite it being around for 30 years.
4. Indian MBA programs need to update their courses to include current trends like mobility, data science, and digital marketing.

5. A bachelor's degree often suffices to show your skills and succeed. If you're really interested in marketing or finance, you can learn from books. Many MBA students seem more focused on getting a job and a degree than on actual learning.
6. An MS from a foreign university might be a better choice if you're looking at ROI and degree value, as they're often more respected by Indian companies.

With 2-5 years of IT experience, pursuing an MBA at TAPMI could be beneficial. The course is intensive, with a mix of practical and theoretical learning. Companies like Deloitte and ITC come for placements, with the highest package reported at 25 lakhs. The fees are around 21.6 lakhs, including hostel costs, which is quite a bit, but the 100% placement rate makes it an appealing option. So, if you're ready for a challenge and want to grow, TAPMI could be a great fit.

TAPMI was truly a place where I experienced "Learning for Life". There were tons of options to get involved in, like sports, committee activities, college competitions, and industry meetups. Personally, I focused on taking full advantage of these opportunities.

Being there made me tougher and taught me how to handle tough situations effectively. The infrastructure is quite impressive, with well-equipped hostel rooms, classrooms, a library, wi-fi, computer labs, and a finance lab.
In the past year, the management has made some great improvements. I'm really pleased with my decision to choose TAPMI over other schools I considered after the entrance exams.

For the PGDM program, TAPMI is a solid choice among Tier-3 colleges. It has a steady track record in the job market. If you're into marketing, it shines in that area, offering good profiles. It's a reliable choice, but you should also weigh it against any other offers you have.

I can't list all 50, but I can mention some top colleges in AP that accept EAMCET scores. If you've got a good rank and are anywhere in the state, VIT-AP and SRM-AP come highly recommended. For those located in Krishna or Guntur districts, VRSEC, RVRJC, VVIT, Vignan, and LBRCE are solid choices. Beyond these, I'm not too familiar with others, but some well-known ones are AU, JNTUK, SRKR in Bhimavaram, MITS, SVU in Tirupati, Gayatri in Vizag, and VIT Bhimavaram. Hope this helps, and good luck!

LHMC: The institute is famous for its prime location, brand name, and its safe all-girls environment. Its infrastructure has been renovated recently and its DU tag is very helpful. Atal Bihari Vajpayee Institute of Medical Sciences (ABVIMS), New Delhi, is a government medical institute established in 2008 for postgraduate courses. It started the MBBS program in 2019. Located in Connaught Place, it is part of Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital. The institute offers undergraduate, postgraduate, and super-specialty programs in medicine. It is affiliated with Guru Gobind Singh Indraprastha University and approved by the National Medical Commission (NMC). ABVIMS provides courses like MBBS, MD, MS, DM, M.Ch, and DNB.

The most popular course today is MBBS, with no specific specializations at the undergraduate level. The first-year fee for MBBS is INR 53,000. Admission to MBBS requires passing 10+2 with 50% in Physics, Chemistry, Biology, and English, and qualifying in the NEET-UG exam, followed by MCC Counseling. The institute has 100 MBBS seats. For postgraduate courses like MD and MS (166 seats), admission is through NEET-PG, and for super-specialty courses like DM and M.Ch (41 seats), it is through NEET-SS.

Students at ABVIMS Delhi become job-eligible after completing the 5.5-year MBBS course, which includes a 1-year compulsory internship with a monthly stipend of INR 24,000 to INR 30,000. After the internship, most students are placed in government or private hospitals, with a starting salary of around INR 1,00,000 per month.

The flagship course of Atal Bihari Vajpayee Institute of Medical Sciences (ABVIMS) New Delhi is MBBS. The second most popular course is MD, offering 10 different specialisations.

“"The course curriculum is good but needs some improvement. There are 3 subjects in the 1st year, 3 subjects in the 2nd year, only 2 subjects in the 3rd year, and 11 subjects in the final (4th) year, which makes the last year very tough. We need more subjects to be added in the 3rd year, and even in the 1st and 2nd years, so that we have less burden in the final year." A student shared in a review posted to Collegedunia in 2025. Read the full review

ABVIMS Delhi offers admission to MBBS and various postgraduate (PG) medical courses for 2025. To get into the MBBS program, students must pass Class 12 with 50% marks and qualify the NEET-UG exam. For PG courses like MD and MS, candidates need an MBBS degree, a 1-year internship, and must pass NEET-PG. For super-specialty courses like DM, M.Ch, and DNB, a postgraduate degree and NEET-SS score are required.

The admission process is done online through the MCC Counselling Website. Students fill in their choices, and based on rank and preference, they are allotted seats. ABVIMS has 100 seats for MBBS, 166 seats for MD/MS, and 41 seats for super-specialty courses.

As per information from student reviews on ABVIMS Placements, Students at ABVIMS Delhi become eligible for jobs after completing the 5.5-year MBBS course, which includes 4.5 years of study and a 1-year internship. The internship is compulsory and includes training in departments like Medicine, Surgery, Obstetrics & Gynaecology, Psychiatry, Anesthesia, Orthopedics, and more.

During the internship, students receive a monthly stipend of INR 24,000 to INR 30,000, depending on government rules. After the internship, most students get placed in private or government hospitals or choose to study further through postgraduate courses.

The starting salary after MBBS is around INR 1,00,000 per month. Placement is common for those who complete the course and internship successfully. Students are not given extra projects or tasks during internship to earn more, but they gain hands-on hospital experience.
There is no specific mention of top recruiters, but government hospitals are a major placement option for students.
Atal Bihari Vajpayee Institute of Medical Sciences (ABVIMS) New Delhi is compared here with two of its major competitors offering similar MBBS course options on key metrics.

The campus of Atal Bihari Vajpayee Institute of Medical Sciences (ABVIMS) is located in Connaught Place, New Delhi, and is part of Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital. It covers about 30 acres and provides a large space for learning and medical training.

ABVIMS has well-equipped lecture halls for teaching, with tools like projectors. There is a new dissection hall for anatomy classes and labs for subjects like physiology, biochemistry, and microbiology. These labs help students practice and learn science. The campus also has a big library with many books, journals, and online resources for study and research.

The attached Dr. RML Hospital has over 1,500 beds and serves 185,000 outpatients and 67,000 inpatients yearly. It has advanced machines like CT scans, MRI, and X-ray for medical tests. The hospital also has special units like heart labs and emergency rooms, giving students real-world training.

Students live in Dhanwantri Chhatrawas, a hostel with basic facilities. There is a canteen for food and open areas for rest and activities. The campus hosts REVELS, a big medical festival, for student events. Public transport connects the campus, but reliability varies.

“Right now, we have proper lecture theatres, labs, hostels, and campus facilities. A new campus is also being planned for UG students. We have reading rooms and library facilities as well. All the labs are well-equipped, and classrooms have projectors and digital screening facilities." a student shared in a review posted to Collegedunia in 2024, rating the campus 5 stars. Read the full review
Ques. How are the hostel facilities at ABVIMS?

Ans. The hostel facilities at ABVIMS are provided through Dhanwantri Chhatrawas. They offer rooms for students with basic needs like beds, study tables, and storage. The hostel has a canteen for meals and common areas for relaxation. It is clean and safe, located within the campus near Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital. Students can stay comfortably, and the hostel supports their studies with a quiet environment. Both male and female students have separate accommodations.
Ques. How is the student-faculty ratio at ABVIMS?

Ans. The exact student-faculty ratio at ABVIMS is not publicly shared. However, as a government medical institute, it maintains a balanced ratio to ensure good teaching. With 100 MBBS seats and experienced faculty from Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital, students get proper guidance. Faculty teach in small groups during lectures, labs, and hospital training, helping students learn better.
Ques. Does ABVIMS offer any scholarships or fee waivers to students?

Ans. ABVIMS offers Merit-Based Scholarships for students with high academic performance and Minority Scholarships for students from SC, ST, OBC, or religious minority groups. These scholarships help cover educational costs like tuition or books. The institute also supports access to government scholarships through portals like the National Scholarship Portal. For exact eligibility and application details, students should contact ABVIMS or check the official website.
Ques. Is the library at ABVIMS useful for medical research?

Ans. The library at ABVIMS is large and well-equipped for medical research. It has many books, journals, and online resources on medicine and related subjects. Students can access study materials for MBBS, MD, and super-specialty courses. The library provides a quiet space for reading and research, with computers for online access. It supports students and faculty in their academic and research work. For more details, visit the ABVIMS official website.
Ques. Can students participate in sports or cultural activities easily at ABVIMS?

Ans. ABVIMS offers opportunities for sports and cultural activities. The campus has open areas for sports like cricket or football. Students can join REVELS, a large medical festival, for cultural events like dance, music, and competitions. These activities are organized to help students relax and connect. The campus supports easy participation, with facilities available for practice and events. For more information, check the ABVIMS official website.

The best college for you depends on your priorities and goals. First, you need to figure out what exactly you are expecting from your degree and college. IDEKU (Institute of Distance Education, University of Kerala) is in the Kariavattom Campus, Thiruvananthapuram. The institute was founded in 1976, and it is a leading distance learning centre in the state of Kerala dedicated to ensuring that disadvantaged groups of people, women, senior citizens and lifelong learners receive quality education.

Library: One of the oldest and largest university libraries in Kerala is the Kerala University Library, which serves students of IDEKU, too. It contains a large storage of books, journals, theses, and other reference materials of various disciplines, as well as contemporary digital resources for remote learners. The university provides students with access to OPAC (Online Public Access Catalogue), inter-library loan facilities, and an increased number of e-journals and databases through the digital portal. The library also offers current awareness services so as to keep the learners abreast with the latest research. In the case of IDEKU students, this mixture of offline and online resources provides an opportunity to get academic assistance both locally and remotely.

Sports Facilities: The athletics available to IDEKU students are the sports amenities of the University of Kerala, which comprise an artificial athletics track, a football and basketball court, cricket practice nets, as well as a multipurpose events stadium. There is also the fitness and weight training centre and indoor games in the university. Through these resources, students get a lot of room to remain active, participate in tournaments, and reconcile academics with physical health.

Health Centre: The University of Kerala has a Health Centre at a campus called Kariavattom Campus, which is available to the IDEKU students, staff, and their dependents and provides consultation services between 8.00 AM and 2.00 PM on working days. It has a team of staff such as a Resident Medical Officer, Nurse, Lab Technician, Radiographer, Clinical Psychologist and other support staff who are involved in routine health checks, counselling and treatments. Aesthetics and sensitization campaigns on contagious and water-related diseases are also held regularly, which support preventive measures among students. In the case of hostel students, they have access to special health-related programs and counselling that are provided even outside the clinic hours.
Ques. Where is IDEKU located?

Ans. The Institute of Distance Education of the University of Kerala is called IDEKU and is situated in the Kariavattom Campus of Thiruvananthapuram. The campus is also well linked to the city and accessible by road and rail. It is situated in a serene, scholarly place with vegetation. The location is near the capital city and, therefore, easy to reach for the students. The central location of IDEKU makes it available to learners within Kerala.
Ques. What facilities does IDEKU offer to students?

Ans. IDEKU has a variety of student facilities, among them academic counselling, online study facilities, and regional study facilities. The institute helps the learners utilise online platforms to access the lessons and hand in their assignments. It also schedules contact classes for a few courses to facilitate interaction. Both online and campus administrative assistance is offered. All these facilities together ensure IDEKU becomes student-friendly and flexible.
Ques. How does the IDEKU library help distance learners?

Ans. Students of IDEKU have access to the Kerala University Library, which is one of the largest libraries in the state. The library contains thousands of books and research materials in various fields and journals. The remote access is provided in digital services such as OPAC, e-journals, and databases. Inter-library loans and current awareness updates are the other support that aids learners. This renders the library of IDEKU as a major academic support of distance learning.
Ques. Does IDEKU provide hostel facilities?

Ans. IDEKU fails to offer hostel services to its distance education students. Since the majority of the students have a part-time or off-campus status, the institute anticipates them to make their own accommodation. There are, however, numerous PGs, rentals and lodges around the area, being in Thiruvananthapuram. There is easy access to a short-term stay for students who come to take exams or talk to counsellors. IDEKU is college-oriented as opposed to residential services.
Ques. What is the admission process at IDEKU in 2025?

Ans. Applications at IDEKU in 2025 are completely online via the official portal. The students will be required to enrol, complete academic forms, submit documents, and pay necessary fees. Choosing is normally based on merit, which is based on qualifying exam scores. In some cases, coursework is required in the postgraduate program, and shortlisted candidates are the only ones paying the entire admission fee. IDEKU makes the process easy, transparent, and available to the learners in Kerala.

Master's Union is a modern business school that differs significantly from traditional business schools. The institute was established in 2020 and is situated in Gurugram, Haryana. It has been ranked 36th for MBA by Collegedunia in 2025.

It offers various courses at UG and PG levels, with PGP (Technology & Business Management) being the flagship course. Admission to PGP is based on the score in CAT/GMAT, followed by a Personal Interview. Applicants without CAT/GMAT scores need to appear for the Master’s Union Business Aptitude and Assessment Test (MU-BAAT).

As per Masters’ Union Placement Report 2025, the highest package stood at INR 1.28 Crore per annum, and the average package stood at INR 33.39 LPA. The top recruiters during the placement drive 2025 are Kearney, Accenture, KPMG, PwC, EY, Oliver Wyman, etc.

After a valid score in the entrance exam, candidates will be invited for a Personal Interview. The final admission is based on Entrance exam scores, Personal Interview, and Candidate's Profile. Ques. What is the eligibility criteria for admission to PGP course at Masters’ Union?
Ans. Masters’ Union offers admission to PGP courses in two cohorts. One cohort is only for experienced professionals with more than 1 year of post MBA work experience.

The other cohort offers admission to freshers candidates as well having internship experience. The duration of PGP TBM (Experienced Professionals) is 16 months and PGP YLM (Freshers+ Work Experience) is 24 months.
Ques. How do I apply to Masters’ Union PGP programs?

Ans. For admission to various courses at Masters’ Union, interested candidates need to apply through the official website. The admission is based on a Video Essay, followed by a Personal Interview. The college accepts CAT/GMAT entrance exam scores for shortlisting of candidates. Masters’ Union also conducts its own entrance exam MU BAAT, for candidates who haven’t appeared or haven’t performed well in CAT/GMAT.
Ques. Does the Masters’ Union offer scholarships for undergraduate students?

Ans. Yes, you can get scholarships based on your grades and financial need. Your score on the Masters’ Union entrance test (above 35 out of 45) or scores from other tests like JEE, IPMAT, MUSAT, or CUET will determine if you qualify.
Ques. How is the Masters’ Union curriculum structured?

Ans. The course curriculum at Masters’ Union combines core business fundamentals, technology skilling, and real-world projects. Students learn through case studies, simulations, internships, and industry challenges.
Ques. What is the MU-BAAT, and when should candidates appear for the test?

Ans. MU-BAAT (Masters’ Union Business Aptitude and Assessment Test) is a 60-minute experiential test for applicants without CAT/GMAT/Focus scores. It evaluates business aptitude, analytical thinking, and problem-solving and must be taken within 7 days post-application deadline.
Ques. How does a typical day look like for a PGP-TBM student?
Ans. Students usually attend 2–3 daily classes, each lasting around 120 minutes, complemented by CXO sessions, practicums, and career counseling.
Ques. Is Masters’ Union UGC recognized?

Ans. Masters’ Union is a private business school and its PGP-TBM program is a certificate, not a UGC-recognized degree. However, its Undergraduate Programme is offered in collaboration with Delhi University, which awards a recognized BMS or B.Com degree.

When people ask if doing an MBA from the Masters Union School of Business is worth it, they usually want to know about the quality of education, job prospects, and return on investment. If you're considering these factors, Masters Union in Gurgaon offers a distinctive value that makes it stand out from typical MBA programs like those at IIMs or ISB.

1. About the Institution Masters Union (MU) began its first batch in 2020 and has quickly become one of India's most talked-about business schools. Unlike traditional MBA courses that focus heavily on theory, MU’s PGP in Technology and Business Management (PGP-TBM) emphasizes learning from industry practitioners, hands-on startup experiences, and real industry immersion. The faculty includes over 200 industry experts, including top professionals from companies like McKinsey, Microsoft, Google, and Mastercard. Advisors from prestigious institutions like Stanford, ISB, IIT, and Wharton support the program. The campus is located in DLF Cyber City, Gurgaon, placing students at the heart of India's corporate action.

With many students landing roles with CTCs over ?25–30 LPA, the return on investment is among the best in India, especially considering international exposure and startup mentorship.

The Directorate of Distance Education (DDE) at Alagappa University, located in Karaikudi, Tamil Nadu, and a part of Alagappa University, was formed in 1992. Alagappa University is a Government of Tamil Nadu institution, and is UGC and DEB approved, and has NAAC accreditation at 'A+' grade, indicating the high levels of both academic quality and institutional strength.

Alagappa University’s Directorate of Distance Education (DDE) flagship course is a two-year MBA programme with the approval of UGC-DEB in distance education mode. The programme in MBA has specializations in General Management, Financial Management, Human Resource Management, Marketing, International Business, and Systems Management. The MBA programme is for graduates only, and there will be no entrance exam for applicants. The estimated cost of the MBA through DDE is estimated at INR 80,600.

The Directorate of Distance Education (DDE) at Alagappa University offers placement assistance services to its students. Although the placement procedure is not centralized as with conventional B-Schools, some students reported average salaries of INR 2.5 LPA and the highest salary package of INR 8 LPA. The university also provides internship opportunities with Wipro, TCS, and Sharekhan so that students have some level of industry exposure.
Here are the key highlights
Alagappa University, Directorate of Distance is now accepting applications for its undergraduate programs for the 2025 admission cycle. Given below are the key dates for College Admission 2025

Alagappa University’s Directorate of Distance Education (DDE), Karaikudi, Tamil Nadu, has announced admission for a two-year MBA programme for the session 2025 on the basis of direct admission/merit admission. Candidates with a bachelor’s degree programme from a university recognized by the Government of India in any discipline are eligible. Entrance examinations or a minimum percentage qualification are not required, thereby making the programme available for any learners (in any discipline), including working professionals and graduates, as well as a second degree.

The DDE offers two sets of admissions: for the academic year, i.e., July – December, and the Calendar year, i.e., January - June. Admission processes are conducted through an interactive online portal on the Alagappa University official website or at its authorized Learning centers. Once the application is received with the relevant documentation, eligibility is assessed, and students will be notified of their admission in just two or three weeks.

Once selected, participants in the MBA must pay the prescribed course fees or the first installment payment to secure their place. After confirming payment, students will receive the printed or electronic study materials and may begin their studies through a self-paced distance learning approach.

The Directorate of Distance Education (DDE) at Alagappa University, Karaikudi, provides placement support to its students, with salary packages reported to be between INR 2.5 and 8 lakhs per annum. The university also provides internship opportunities with leading companies like Wipro, TCS, and Sharekhan for the students to have exposure in the industry. It also provides support to students interested in entrepreneurship through startup/incubation cells, particularly for students to start their ventures.

Management Development Institute (MDI) is a private business school in Murshidabad, West Bengal, established in 2014. It is part of the same MDI society that also governs MDI Gurgaon.
Collegedunia in 2025 ranked MDI Murshidabad as 64 best B-school in India out of 372.

MDI Murshidabad offers PGDM as its flagship course, approved by AICTE and accredited by NBA and AIU, with a total fee of INR 16.45 lakh. Candidates need to take the CAT/XAT/GMAT for shortlisting, where 65 percentile in 2025 was the closing score for both CAT and XAT.

In the 2025 placement drive, the highest package offered was INR 20 LPA, the average package was INR 12.75 LPA, and the median package was INR 11 LPA, with participation from over 90 companies. The top recruiters at MDI Murshidabad are Aditya Birla, Airtel, Axis Bank, Infosys, Flipkart, Cognizant, etc.
Admission for the PGDM program at MDI Murshidabad is ongoing for the 2026-28 batch.
Below are some important entrance exams and dates for admission.

MDI’s academic curriculum involves a doctoral-level fellow management program and a PGDM online course. But the cornerstone of MDI Murshidabad’s academic offerings is the 2-year AICTE and NBA-approved PGDM course.

Ques. What specialisations can PGDM students at MDI Murshidabad choose?
Ans. PGDM students at MDI Murshidabad, in the second year, can opt for elective/ optional courses to specialise in a maximum of two functional areas.
Students can opt for a range of 14 to 17 electives. However, CGPA is calculated based on the best 14 electives out of the total.
MDI’s residential PGDM program is offered to candidates with a minimum of 50% marks in graduation via CAT/XAT/GMAT.

Ques. How is the personal interview at MDI Murshidabad?

Ans. As per multiple inputs from students, during the interview, candidates are mainly asked to describe themselves and their area of interest. Then the panel would ask questions specific to the domain of interest to gauge the level of knowledge the candidate has. Some candidates were asked generic questions associated with student life, including depression and anxiety, and some basic questions about personal life and family.

Need-based scholarships are made available to students belonging to economically disadvantaged families, and provide a particular scholarship to students from India's northeastern states to pursue a management degree. Each year, MDI Murshidabad provides free tuition (worth INR 8,92,000 for two years) to five students.

Additionally, 10 students will receive a scholarship worth INR 8,500 each month for up to 21 months. MDI Murshidabad Scholarship is dependent on the students' exam results; the better they perform, the more they receive. This assistance is provided to students enrolled in the AICTE-approved 2-year PGDM (Post Graduate Diploma in Management) program.

MDI Murshidabad campus is spread across 10 acres of land. The classrooms of this institute are well-equipped with all the modern facilities. The campus at MDI Murshidabad comprises hostels, a library, a canteen, a health club (gymnasium), an ATM, a swimming pool, and a cafeteria.

Apart from this, the institute provides certification and fellowship programs, and BBA was introduced as a new UG course this year.

Ans. MDI Murshidabad is spread over almost 10 acres. Facilities include hostels, a library, an auditorium, classrooms with AV equipment, a gym, a cafeteria and a playground.

The PGDM in Business Administration Executive program at MDI Gurgaon is a 24-month course designed for busy professionals in the NCR who haven't had formal management training before. It's perfect for those looking to boost their careers significantly.

The program is open to professionals with over 3 years of experience, and it's a non-residential course that fits well with their schedules. If you're aiming for that next big career step, this could be a great option to consider.

MDI Gurgaon ranks among the top MBA schools in India, alongside IIMs, XLRI, FMS, and SPJIMR. However, before deciding, you should think about what you want from your MBA. It's important to match your career goals with what the school offers to see if it's the right fit for you.

I'll keep this short and straightforward based on what I've experienced. The faculty at MDI Gurgaon is truly impressive, no question there. The opportunities for exposure are also very good. However, the student experience, especially in terms of student committees, has been a major downside for me.

It feels like there's a lot of power struggles both within and between committees, which can have a negative effect on your mindset. The culture here seems to lean towards an authoritarian style of leadership, which isn't what you'd ideally expect from a business school. People often find themselves having to either keep quiet or adapt to this environment. If you're comfortable with that kind of politics, then you might be fine. But I strongly suggest looking into the real situation at any college you get into before you decide.

MDI Gurgaon ranks among the top 15 MBA schools in India and is on par with the top 10 when it comes to both reputation and job placements. Companies that visit MDI for placements are the same ones that go to the leading institutes. The average salary package offered is around ?26.2 lakh per annum, with promising job profiles.

If you're aiming for positions in Private Equity or Front End Investment Banking, which are typically reserved for the very top schools, MDI might not be the ideal choice. However, it does attract a variety of other roles, including consulting, banking, and FMCG.
Patrick Dsouza has achieved a 100% score on the CAT six times.

If you're a doctor looking to pursue an MBA, especially at MDI Gurgaon, you're in a pretty good spot. Here's why: First, the program won't be too hard for you. Since medicine is already a tough field, you're familiar with hard work and you'll likely excel here. Second, business schools usually appreciate having students like you because you can offer unique perspectives in class discussions. Finally, when it comes to job placements, you'll find plenty of opportunities. Companies in the pharmaceutical, medical devices, consulting sectors, and hospitals will be interested in your skills, and there aren't many candidates like you around. It's a win-win situation for you. Best of luck, VK

I had a fantastic time at MDI Gurgaon. It's less hectic compared to other top IIMs, which means you get lots of time to hang out with friends and enjoy life alongside your studies. I also participated in an exchange program in Europe, and let me tell you, exploring Europe at such a low cost is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity. If you're studying at MDI and have the chance to go on an exchange program, definitely go for it. The extra 2-3 lakh rupees you'll spend on living and traveling there is totally worth it.

GMCH Chandigarh, also known as Government Medical College & Hospital Chandigarh, was established in 1991. GMCH Chandigarh is situated in Sector 32 on a 32-acre urban campus and ranked 34 among medical colleges in the NIRF 2025 rankings.

GMCH Chandigarh offers flagship programmes, such as MBBS, which includes 150 seats for students and admissions are done through the NEET UG Entrance exam. GMCH also offers undergraduate courses, including B.Sc. Nursing, B.Sc. Radiotherapy, BMLS, and B.Sc. Optometry, along with several postgraduate courses, such as M.Sc., MD, and MS programmes. Admissions in these UG and PG courses are based on the GMCH Combined Entrance Test. The average fees for flagship programs, such as MBBS, at the institute are INR 25,000 per year.

SP Jain requires one entrance test score: GMAT, GRE, CAT (for Indian applicants), or SPJAT. The minimum expected scores are 650 in GMAT, 320 in GRE, 80 percentile in CAT, or 50% in SPJAT. SPJIMR PGPFMB (Post Graduate Programme in Family Managed Business) is a better and clear choice between the two.

This program was launched by SPJIMR in the year 1997, so it is quite a renowned program. This program has a network of 4000+ alumni to take guidance from. This program offers a classroom learning experience, and it last for 18 months.
The fee for the program is 16 lac for 18 months. While the GFMB program was launched recently by SP Jain Global, so if you have a choice, then I would recommend you to go for PGPFMB.

There is a major difference between the 2 B Schools, SPJIMR and SP Jain. The former is an Australian B School with 4 campuses in Dubai, Mumbai, Singapore, and Sydney whereas the latter is a Management Institute offering Management courses at its only campus in Mumbai.

Although Mumbai has a variety of decent B Schools to choose from, my brother chose SP Jain for EMBA. He had a list of criteria he looked for in his dream B School and according to him, SP Jain fulfilled it all. Some of his major requisites were

He found all these features in SP Jain and was very glad he chose it. In fact, through his Executive MBA, he claimed to have got an insight into the business world and see how businesses in other sectors survive. He believes to have developed a more holistic view post this program. Professionally too, he is doing pretty well and the program has helped him gain success.

Many people choose to enroll in the Indian School of Business (ISB) Hyderabad due to its reputation and the success of its alumni. However, it is important to note that the SP Jain Global MBA program is also a highly regarded option. In fact, it has been recognized by Forbes and The Economist as a top MBA program in the world, an accomplishment that ISB has not yet achieved. Additionally, SP Jain Global has a long history of providing quality education and producing talented professionals. This is particularly true for the Family Managed Business course, which is taught by a faculty that includes a large number of international university doctorates.

Given its reputation, the experience of its professors, and the specific offerings of the Family Managed Business course, SP Jain Global is a strong choice for those looking to inherit and expand a family-run business.

The major drawback of ABM is that you are deprived of the PGP electives and can cover ABM electives only. These electives cover strategy marketing and operations.

Both colleges are among India’s prestigious institutions, but they differ in academics, campus culture, fees, and student exposure. St Xaviers Mumbai is generally preferred for media, economics, commerce, and corporate exposure, while St Xaviers Kolkata is known for science, research, and traditional academic excellence.

St Xavier’s College Mumbai offers a heritage campus in South Mumbai with modern academic infrastructure, research facilities, sports amenities, and student support services. The college focuses on holistic student development through advanced learning resources, extracurricular opportunities, wellness support, and inclusive campus facilities.

As per student discussions, St Xaviers Mumbai offers a vibrant and culturally diverse college life with exposure through festivals, societies, and extracurricular activities. Students frequently highlight Malhar and other department fests, active student-run clubs, supportive faculty, and excellent peer networking opportunities. The heritage campus, library, sports facilities, and central South Mumbai location are also appreciated, although some students mention high academic pressure and expensive living costs in Mumbai for outstation students.
Ques. Is St Xaviers Mumbai strict regarding discipline and attendance?

Ans. St Xaviers Mumbai is considered quite strict regarding discipline and attendance. The college enforces a mandatory attendance requirement (around 75%), and students who fail to meet it may be barred from exams. Overall, the environment is disciplined and rule-oriented, though manageable if students maintain regular attendance.
Ques. What is campus life like at St Xaviers Mumbai?

Ans. Campus life at St Xaviers Mumbai is very vibrant and active. Students frequently highlight the college’s famous festivals like Malhar, student-run societies, cultural events, sports activities, and an overall energetic campus environment. The college offers great exposure, networking opportunities, and a diverse student crowd, making campus life engaging and eventful.
Ques. Does St Xaviers Mumbai provide scholarships?

Ans. Yes, St Xaviers Mumbai provides scholarships and financial aid, which include government scholarships for SC, ST, OBC, EWS, and minority students, merit-based scholarships, sports scholarships, disability support, and the Student Beneficiary Fund (SBF) for financial assistance. Under the government scheme structure, benefits typically cover eligible students across reserved categories, while institutional aid is granted based on merit and financial need. Students note that although the college is academically strict, eligible applicants can receive fee concessions or aid if they apply with proper documentation within deadlines.
Ques. How competitive is admission at St Xaviers Mumbai?

Ans. Admission to St Xaviers Mumbai is considered highly competitive. Students mention that the college receives a large number of applications from across India for limited seats, especially for popular courses like BMS, BAMCJ, BA Economics, and B.Sc programs. Selection is based on a combination of Class 12 marks and XET entrance test for selected courses, which increases competition further. High percentages (90%+) may not guarantee admission due to cut-offs and category-wise seat allocation, making the process quite selective overall.
Ques. Is St Xavier’s College Mumbai good for placements and internships?

Ans. St Xaviers Mumbai is considered good for internships and moderate for placements, rather than a fully placement-driven institute. The college attracts recruiters like Deloitte, EY, KPMG, and JP Morgan, with reported packages generally ranging from INR 6 LPA to INR 24 LPA (occasionally higher in select cases). However, placements are not uniform for all students, and many rely on off-campus opportunities. Overall ROI is considered strong due to the relatively low annual fees (around INR 30K - INR 2.7 lakh depending on course) combined with good exposure, internships, and brand value, but final outcomes depend heavily on individual skills and networking.

Loyola College Chennai is an autonomous institution founded in 1925. The institute has been awarded the status of “College of Excellence” by UGC and is accredited with an 'A++' grade by NAAC. It is affiliated with University of Madras. Loyola College Chennai is ranked 14th in the College category by NIRF 2025, and placed 5th in Commerce and 6th in Science by Collegedunia.

It offers popular B.Sc and M.Sc programs under a two-shift system. UG admissions are based on 10+2 marks, while PG admissions require a relevant bachelor’s degree followed by GD/PI. Loyola College fees are category-based: UG fees vary by board (HSC, CBSE/ISC, others), and PG fees differ for University of Madras graduates and students from other universities.
For Shift I, M.Sc (Madras University students) costs about INR 13,740-INR 15,150 for the 1st semester, while B.Sc (HSC board) costs INR 14,910-INR 21,040, depending on the specialisation.
Loyola College Chennai reported strong placement outcomes, with the highest package of INR 22.5 LPA and an average package of INR 6.34 LPA, according to the Placement Brochure 2024.
Online application portal for admission to UG programs (2026-27) will open on the day the Tamil Nadu 12th board results are announced. Here is a likely timeline based on the latest available dates.

Note: Students must complete the online registration within 10 days of the Tamil Nadu 10+2 result announcement. For other boards, registration should be done within 3 days of their result announcement.

Loyola College admits undergraduates solely on a merit basis, while PG candidates must take an additional entrance exam consisting of GD and/or PI, administered by the university. The curriculum of the popular Data Science (M.Sc) program is well-rounded with intensive laboratory work, industry talks, and case studies. The other popular courses, such as BCA and BBA, have updated curriculum, aligned with the academics as well as industrial developments in the relevant fields.
For SHIFT 2 Courses and Fees, check: Loyola College Courses & Fees

The college also offers PhD in Economics, Commerce, History, English, Zoology, Physics and Chemistry. There are two active Diploma and PG Diploma programs as well, in the School of Film Studies and Management, respectively.

Loyola College Chennai conducts admissions for UG, PG, and doctoral programs through a fully online process, with the application portal typically opening after the release of Tamil Nadu 10+2 results for UG courses.

Admissions are primarily merit-based. UG candidates are shortlisted based on their Class 12 (10+2) marks, while PG admissions are based on graduation scores and may include entrance tests, group discussions and / or PI for select programs.

To apply, candidates must register on the official portal, choose their course, fill in personal and academic details, upload required documents, and pay the application fee. A unique application number is generated to track the admission status online.

Shortlisted candidates are offered provisional admission, which becomes final after document verification and payment of the admission fee. Applicants required to appear for entrance tests are notified separately after submitting their application.

The Reddit discussion presents mixed opinions about Loyola College Chennai. Some users describe it as a decent and affordable college with good ranking, especially for arts and commerce, while others feel it is slightly overrated compared to expectations. A detailed student review highlights serious dissatisfaction with the B.Sc Physics department, mentioning poor teaching quality, strict evaluation, and outdated labs, while also noting that arts and media courses offer better exposure and opportunities. Overall, the consensus is that Loyola is a good option depending on the course, but the experience can vary significantly by department.

Loyola College campus provides an academic ambience of international standard.

It offers facilities such as spacious classrooms, well-equipped laboratories, sports complex, library with a reading room and digital database, separate hostel accommodations for boys and girls, and a canteen.
Hostel accommodations at the institutions provide a home-like environment to its residents. The presence of nature surrounding the living quarters makes them quite comfortable.
The vast college sports ground is the heart of the sports facilities that provide students with opportunities to engage in outdoor sports such as cricket, football, etc.
Loyola College has a health centre on campus equipped to provide optimal health care services. The facility houses a medical officer for consultation.

Ques. Are mobile phones allowed inside Loyola College Chennai ?

Ans. No. Electronic gadgets such as mobile phone, ipad, ipod,smart watches are prohibited inside Loyola College campus. Students are also discouraged to travel around the camous in their personal vehicles. Any such vehicle, if used to commute by a student, is to be parked at the parking area inside the campus.
Ques. Is there any dress code / uniform at Loyola College Chennai ?

Ans. While Loyola College Chennai doesn’t require students to wear uniforms, they are needed to dress in a way that’s suitable to the academic environment of the college. Girls are required to wear decenly cut salwaar kameez while boys should sport formals. Neat and tidy appearance is also mandated by the college.
Ques. What are the attendance regulations at Loyola College Chennai?

Ans. Loyola College Chennai mandates an attendance of 75% in each subject in a semester to be eligible for the final examination. Barring special cases such as health issue related absence, absence of a differently abled student caused by any difficulty, no consideration is extented to any defaulter.
Ques. What are the shift timings at Loyola College?

Ans. Loyola College conducts classes in two shifts : Morning Shift (8:15 AM – 1:15 PM) for students working part time after college hours and Afternoon Shift (1:30 PM – 6:30 PM) for students capable of financing their education without any assistance from the college.
Ques. Is Loyola College co-ed?

Ans. Loyola College is a partially co - educational instituition. Some of its courses are co-ed, while others admit male candidates only. For instance, the UG courses at the department of Commerce admit only male students. However, the college has separate hostels for boys and girls to accomodate students belonging to both genders.
Ques. Does Loyola College provide scholarships to differently abled students?
Ans. Yes. Loyola College alumni base lends financial aid to differently abled students under the college’s Student Support Service program.

In my opinion, Loyola College in Chennai is one of India's top Jesuit institutions. It's consistently ranked among the top 10 colleges in India by NIRF and offers a wide range of courses in Humanities, Science, and Management. It mainly caters to men, though some courses are open to women.

St Joseph’s University, also a Jesuit institution in Bangalore, has a strong reputation here. It's known for its rich legacy of over 120 years and a strong alumni network. As a co-ed college, it has a balanced mix of male and female students. The university is highly regarded for its Humanities, Science, and B.Voc programs, among other courses. While it may not be as famous outside Bangalore, it remains a prestigious institution in the city and across India.

When it comes to placements, both colleges provide good opportunities. Loyola College, Chennai tends to have a higher placement rate due to its nationwide recognition. St Joseph’s also offers solid placements, although slightly less compared to Loyola, but much depends on individual student performance.

To sum up, both institutions are well-respected Jesuit colleges in India with excellent faculty. Whether you choose Loyola or St Joseph’s, you'll receive not only academic excellence but also holistic development and character building. Both colleges have strong placement records and send their students to top companies.

Loyola College is quite well-known outside Tamil Nadu, especially in major cities like Mumbai and Delhi. Many people regard it as one of the top colleges in India. As a student of the Bachelor of Commerce (B.Com), I've experienced a lot of pride in my college's reputation.

The placement opportunities here are impressive, with companies like Deloitte and TCS recruiting students, which adds to its recognition beyond Tamil Nadu. The college has a strong alumni network that contributes positively to its reputation in other states.

It really comes down to your perspective. Loyola College offers a fair amount of freedom, but they do have a bit of an annoying rule against using camera phones. If you're aiming for courses like chartered accountancy, you might want to consider somewhere else, like Vivekananda, which offers better support for that field. The student community is great, and the faculty is pretty decent too. There are tons of opportunities for club activities and other Co curriculars if that's what you're into. The attendance policy is more relaxed compared to other colleges. Plus, having Loyola on your resume is a nice perk. Hope this helps!

Loyola College is known for its strict environment, particularly concerning academics. In my Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) course, we have a rigorous exam structure where attendance is closely monitored. You need to maintain a certain percentage to sit for exams, and they are pretty serious about ensuring students follow these rules.
It can be challenging, especially if you're juggling extracurriculars and studies, but it helps instill a sense of discipline.

I got 87% in the Tamil Nadu State Board exams and was really eager to study mathematics at Loyola College, even though my math score wasn't the best. I decided to apply for physics, mathematics, and chemistry, hoping to get into at least one of them. To my surprise, I got shortlisted for both physics and mathematics. I was over the moon and joined Loyola in 2016, and I stayed happy throughout my time there. Loyola isn't just a college; it's so much more.
Sure thing! Just include a self-signed copy of your parent's bank passbook when you apply, and you'll be good to go.

Loyola College is particularly notable for its Bachelor of Commerce (B.Com) program, which is designed to prepare students for real-world challenges. The faculty are mostly experienced professionals, and the teaching methods include using modern digital tools. The internship opportunities are robust, with students required to complete internships in their third year, which greatly enhances employability.

The fee structure is also quite affordable, especially for the government-aided shift, making it accessible for many students. Overall, the college provides a holistic experience that balances academics with cultural events and personal development.

If you're all about diving deep into your studies, Loyola College is the place to be. But if you're looking to grow personally and become more well-rounded, Madras Christian College offers that transformation. You might start at MCC as a kid, but you'll walk out as a true Gentleman.

I chose Loyola College for my Bachelor of Commerce (B.Com) degree mainly because of its reputation. The course is rigorous, with a good mix of theory and practical applications, but the faculty is very supportive, which makes it manageable. Regular exams and internal assessments keep us engaged and motivated.

The campus life is vibrant, with plenty of clubs and activities, and the annual fest is a highlight of the year. I've also noticed good placement opportunities, which is a big plus for me as I prepare for my career ahead.

Some negative aspects of Loyola College Chennai, particularly in the Bachelor of Commerce [B.Com] program, include the outdated curriculum. The syllabus often lacks relevance to modern business practices, especially in areas like digital marketing and advanced accounting software. This can hinder students' preparedness for the job market, making it difficult for them to compete with peers from other institutions. Additionally, while the faculty is generally well-qualified, some professors may not effectively engage students, leading to a less interactive learning environment.

Another concern is the high fee structure for the Bachelor of Commerce [B.Com] program. While the college has a reputation for excellence, the financial burden can be significant for many students. Despite the availability of scholarships, the criteria can be stringent, and not all students benefit from them. This can create a financial strain, especially for those from lower-income families.

Lastly, campus life has its downsides too. While events like "Ovations" are engaging, some students feel that there could be more inclusivity in extracurricular activities. The pressure to participate in various clubs and events can sometimes feel overwhelming, detracting from the overall college experience. The infrastructure, although extensive, may not always meet students' expectations in terms of maintenance and facilities, which can affect their daily life on campus.

15 May, 2026 CUET UG 2026 examination is currently ongoing till May 31, 2026.

Department of Business Economics, also known as DBE DU was established in 1973. DBE DU is a constituent department of the University of Delhi and functions under DU regulation approved by UGC. As a department within the University of Delhi, the DBE is accredited with an A++ grade by NAAC.

Note: The primary application window for the MBA(Business Economics) and MBA (Finance) programs for the 2026-27 session is currently closed. The GD & Personal Interview (PI) is scheduled in March and April 2026, and the final result will be published in May 2026.

MBA admission generally begins between January and March, following CAT results, while CUET-UG-based admission takes place between May and July. Some of the important admission dates for the 2026 session of DBE DU are given below in the table:

At the UG level, it offers BMS, BBA FIA, and BA (Hons). At the PG level, DBE DU offers an MBA program in Business Economics and Finance. The total MBA fee at DBE DU is approximately INR 1.01 Lakh for the complete program, excluding hostel and miscellaneous charges. DBE DU also offers PhD programs in business economics and finance. The details for the DBE DU courses and fees are mentioned below in the table.
Image Source: DBE DU Official Website
Ques: Is DBE DU more costly than other MBA programs?

Ans: No, DBE DU is one of the most affordable MBA options in India. When considering total fees versus placement outcomes, it offers a good return on investment due to its affordable tuition and respectable placement packages.
Ques: Do all categories have the same fees at DBE DU Fees?

Ans: No, under the DU financial support scheme, reserved categories and economically disadvantaged sections qualify for fee waivers and concessions, just like other DU programs; however, the base fee structure across categories remains similar unless a waiver is granted.

DBE DU admission for the MBA program is based on the Common Admission Test (CAT), followed by group discussion and personal interview. For undergraduate programs like BMS, BBA FIA, BA (Hons), and B.Voc, admission is entirely based on CUET UG scores. For PhD admission, candidates require a postgraduate degree and a valid UGC-NET score, followed by a departmental selection process. Applicants must apply online via the DU admission portal within the stipulated dates.
Entrance exams: DBE DU accepts the CUET UG exam for UG programs, CAT (for MBA), and UGC NET (PhD).
Eligibility Criteria: for UG admission, candidates must have passed 10 + 2 from a recognised board, and for MBA admission, candidates must have held a bachelor's degree from a recognized university.
Mode of selection: For the UG program, candidates must have appeared for the CUET UG, and for MBA admission, candidates must have appeared for the CAT examination.
Ques: How does DBE DU differ from other colleges or departments within Delhi University?

Ans: DBE DU's robust pre-win business education sets it apart from other DU colleges. DBE incorporates economics, statistics, and policy analysis in two programs, like BBE, preparing students for consulting, analytics, and public policy rules, in contrast to commerce colleges like SRCC or Hindu College, which primarily focus on accounting, finance, and taxation. DBE DU provides a balanced industry-academic approach with practical exposure in business analytics, sustainability, and market forecasting, in contrast to the Delhi School of Economics, which is primarily theoretical and research-oriented. Additionally, DBE offers one of the best ROIs in DU. MBA total fees are about INR 2 Lakhs. The average packages with recruiters like Deloitte, KPMG, and EY are between INR 10 and INR 15 LPA, competing with much more expensive private B-schools.
Ques: Does DBE DU accept CUET PG scores for MBA in Business Economics?

Ans: No, DBE DU does not accept the CUET PG score for its MBA in business economics program, even though many Delhi University postgraduate programs have switched to CUET PG. It is a component of the Department of Financial Studies joint admission process. Meanwhile, the MBA admission process is based on the CAT examination.
DBE DU was ranked 57th for MBA and 21st for BBA/ BMS in the Collegedunia rankings 2025, based on placement outcomes, fees, and academic reputation. Given below is the DBE DU Ranking for 2026.

The expected CAT Cutoff for MBA admission at DBE DU is around the 90 percentile, varying by category. Candidates can check the official cutoff scores for different categories and MBA specializations to assess their admission chances.
Tabulated below are the DBE DU CAT cutoffs for 2026:

DBE DU Placement Report 2025 has not been released. For the MBA batch of 2023-2025, DBE DU recorded highest package of INR 30.25 LPA, with a mean package of INR 15.12 LPA across the participating students. Top recruiters regularly visiting DBE DU include Cognizant, Deloitte, KPMG, EY, Infosys, Axis Bank, and among others.
Tabulated below are the DBE DU placement highlights for 2025:

As per DBE, DU MBA Students review on collegedunia, DBE DU offers a strong MBA program with an excellent return on investment, combining relevant theory with practical exposure through case studies, projects, and market-focused discussions. The course structure is well planned, with core subjects in the first year and electives later, supported by knowledgeable faculty. Internship opportunities are plentiful, including roles from reputed companies, and placements are consistently improving with a high average package. Campus life is engaging, driven by an active student body and networking events. While infrastructure needs upgrades, affordable fees, solid placements, and industry exposure make DBE a highly attractive choice. Click for More Details
Ques: Which sectors dominated the 2025 recruitment drive?

Ans: The placements were primarily led by the BFSI (Banking, Financial Services, and Insurance), IT, and Analytics sectors. Major names like Barclays, American Express, Citibank, and ICICI Bank were among the largest recruiters.
​Ques: What kind of stipends can I expect for a summer internship?

Ans: The summer placement process for the batch of 2025-26 saw a highest stipend of ₹1.5 lakh for the two-month duration, with a mean stipend of ₹51,470. Companies like Arcesium and Citibank often recruit interns as early as the first semester.

This table highlights a structured, side-by-side comparison of three colleges: Department of Business Economics, Delhi School of Economics (DU), and DFS, Department of Financial Studies (DU). The following highlights key aspects, including courses offered, admission criteria, accepted exams, top recruiters, and the application process, to help students choose the right college.
Department of Business Economics (DBE), DU:

DBE DU offers an MBA in Business Economics with a strong blend of economics, analytics, and managerial decision-making. It is known for excellent return on investment due to low fees and consistently good placements. The program suits students seeking versatile corporate roles in consulting, analytics, strategy, and general management with a solid economic foundation.
Delhi School of Economics (DSE), DU:

DSE DU is one of India’s most academically prestigious management institutions, offering MBA specializations such as HRD, International Business, and Business Analytics. It emphasizes analytical thinking, research orientation, and conceptual clarity, making it ideal for students interested in intellectually rigorous management careers with diverse specialization options.
Department of Financial Studies (DFS), DU:

DFS DU is a finance-focused management school offering an MBA in Financial Studies, with strong industry alignment in banking, investment, and corporate finance. It consistently records the highest finance placements among DU management colleges and is best suited for students targeting specialized finance and BFSI sector careers.

DBE DU offers merit-based and need-based scholarships through DU schemes. Scholarship amount and eligibility are subject to university notifications each academic year. Below are some of the DBE DU scholarships offered:
Ques: Does the "EXIM Bank Scholarship" still apply to DBE students?

Ans: Historically, the EXIM Bank has offered a scholarship specifically for top-performing MBA students in international business or economics-related disciplines. At DBE, this is usually a cash award given to the three top performers (two from the general category and one from a reserved category) based on their academic ranking within the batch.
​Ques: Can I apply for the "All India Postgraduate Scholarship"?

Ans: Yes. If you joined the MBA (BE) program after completing an honors degree (B.A./B.Sc./B.Com.) with a first-class result, you are eligible to compete for this university-wide merit scholarship. It provides a monthly stipend (currently around INR 400 per month) for the duration of the course.
DBE DU students can apply for DU hostels. Annual hostel charges typically range between INR 14,000- INR 20,000, excluding mess charges.
Given below is the Aravali hostel fee structure of DBE DU:
Tabulated below are the following one-time charges payable by the residents at the time of admission:
​Ques: What happens if I don't get a hostel?

Ans: Most DBE students who don't secure a hostel stay in Satya Niketan, a vibrant student hub located directly across the road from South Campus. It offers a massive range of PGs and flats. Living here is more expensive but provides the "Satya Vibe" with unlimited cafes, 24/7 food joints, and no university curfews.

As part of the dynamic University of Delhi ecosystem, the DBE DU campus offers a fusion of academic tradition and contemporary learning resources. High-speed Wi-Fi, a rich library system, well-equipped lecture halls, and specialized computer and analytics labs are all beneficial to students. In addition, the campus offers sports and cultural facilities and clubs, seminars, workshops, and student societies to promote holistic development. Cafeterias, common areas, and access to DU's wider services, like health centers and counseling, are examples of on-site amenities. In general, the setting encourages intellectual development, peer interaction, and industry engagement. Hostel accommodations are available through DU hostels on a merit basis.
DBE DU Cricket Ground
Ques: Which academic and technology resources are available for DBE students?

Ans: DBE DU offers interactive sessions on econometrics, analytics, and finance modelling in smart classrooms with projectors and contemporary AV systems. The department offers access to well-equipped computer labs with statistics software necessary for business economics research, as well as books, journals, resources, and a digital database for easy access to international journals and economic research papers. The South Campus library is one of DU's nine major libraries. Being close to interdisciplinary resources such as the SP Jain centre which facilitates cross-department learning in management and applied sciences, is a special benefit.
Ques: What are the sports facilities like for a small department?

Ans: DBE students have access to the larger South Campus sports infrastructure, including a cricket ground, football field, and volleyball courts. Specifically for quick breaks between classes, there is a popular badminton court right near the department building that is a favorite for friendly matches and de-stressing.

The Ashoka Institute of Technology and Management is located in the Uttar Pradesh city of Varanasi. The Institute offers 15 degree courses. Ashoka Institute of Technology and Management is a well-known institution that offers 14 UG and PG courses taught by highly qualified faculty. Ashoka Institute of Technology and Management is the answer for individuals seeking a high-quality education. The Institute is Affiliated with Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Technical University (AKTU).

The Institute provides courses like B.Pharma, B.E. / B.Tech, MBA/PGDM in fields such as Medicine & Health Sciences, Engineering, and Business and management Studies. Through its trained and experienced faculty, Ashoka Institute of Technology and Management provides opportunities to gain knowledge and expertise in the fields of Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science Engineering, Electronics & Communication Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Civil Engineering, and Biotechnology Engineering. Trinity Institute of Professional Studies (TIPS) New Delhi is a private institute established in 2007. It is affiliated with Guru Gobind Singh Indraprashtha University. It is approved by the Bar Council of India (BCI), AICTE, and recognised by UGC. The Institute is accredited with an “A” Grade by NAAC. As per India Collegedunia Ranking 2025, it has been ranked 210 under the BBA/BMS Category. It offers undergraduate programs in Commerce, Journalism, Computers and Law.

BCA is a popular program at Trinity Institute of Professional Studies. For admission to the BCA Program, candidates must have completed 10+2 in Mathematics or Computer Science from any recognised board. Students also need to appear for the IPU-CET Entrance Examination conducted by the Guru Gobind Singh Indraprastha University. The total fees for the BCA program is INR 4.55 Lakhs.

Trinity Institute of Professional Studies Reports shows 95% placement Record in the core Program. The highest package offered is INR 13 LPA, while the average package is INR 4.5 LPA in 3 years. Myntra, Bajaj Allianz, Concentrix, Asia Sky News and many more were the top recruiters at Trinity Institute of Professional Studies 2025 Placement Drive.

Mithibai College of Arts, Chauhan Institute of Science, and Amrutben Jivanlal College of Commerce and Economics is a private autonomous institute in Mumbai also commonly known as Mithibai College. The college was established in 1961 and is affiliated with Mumbai University. It is approved by UGC and accredited by NAAC with Grade A++. The college has been ranked 22nd for journalism by IIRF and 23rd for Art by Collegedunia in 2025.

Mithibai College offers UG, PG, & PhD programs with various specializations. The popular courses offered at Mithibai College are B.Sc. & M.Sc. Mithibai College offers B.Sc. as its flagship course. The 1st-year tuition fee for B.Sc ranges from INR 18,000 to INR 1.01 Lakhs. Meanwhile, the 1st-year tuition fee for M.Sc. ranges from INR 30,000 to INR 1.1 Lakhs. The college offers students with weak financial backgrounds Merit-Based scholarships for the UG courses.

Mithibai College Admission is based on merit for UG and PG courses. For admission to the B.Sc. program, a candidate must have passed the 10+2 examination conducted by the Maharashtra State Board or any recognised Board.

Mithibai College of Arts Placement 2025 report has not been released yet. The top recruiters included Morgan Stanley, JP Morgan Chase, Deloitte, and many more.
