Mithibai College has spacious classrooms, libraries, a cafeteria, and computer centers. The campus also offers various other amenities, including sports facilities, well-equipped laboratories, and a spacious auditorium for events and seminars.

Library: Mithibai College Library (Jitendra Library) has a collection of books, encyclopedias, journals, and other resource materials. It is centrally air-conditioned and supported with modern technology like Wi-Fi and digital cameras. The Library holds more than 60,000 books on different fields of learning. These also include journals, periodicals, encyclopedias, handbooks, and books on general knowledge.
Health Services: The College has a provision of a Doctor on Campus to attend to staff and students.
Canteen: The canteen is very spacious and offers hygienic food at affordable and student-friendly rates.
Gymkhana: The College has a very good sports facility, which is ideal for indoor games such as TT, Chess, and Carrom.
Classrooms: The College has an effective method of teaching in the high-tech classrooms, which are centrally air-conditioned and have good seating and lighting.

Auditoriums: Juhu Jagruti Hall and Mithibai Seminar Hall are excellent, centrally air-conditioned halls, technically well-equipped with lights and sound facilities. It has a seating capacity of approximately 114.
Laboratories: The laboratories at Mithibai College are spacious and well-equipped with the latest apparatus and modern equipment. Most of the labs are High-Tech labs and used for Research work.
Lifts/Ramps/Washrooms/Water Coolers: These facilities are available on a common floor to suit everyone's needs.

Security and Safety: Mithibai College offers a very safe and secure environment with Cameras installed in all the important places and with round-the-clock security. The college also has fire hydrant equipment in place.

Ques. Which academic programs are offered at Mithibai College?

Ans. Mithibai College offers undergraduate, postgraduate, and PhD programs in fields like management, science, computer applications, & education. Mithibai College offers 10 specializations in its PhD program, which include English, Commerce, Microbiology, Botany, Zoology, Mathematics, Biotechnology, Physics, Physical Chemistry, and Analytical Chemistry.
Ques. How is campus life at Mithibai College?

Ans. Mithibai College campus life is vibrant and student-driven. The college hosts multiple cultural events, academic seminars, and student-run clubs throughout the year. The annual fest, Mithibai Kshitij, is one of Mumbai’s largest intercollegiate festivals.
Ques. Does Mithibai College provide hostel facilities?
Ans. Yes, Mithiba College offers separate hostels for boys and girls, with limited seating available. Facilities include Wi-Fi, mess, laundry, and basic furnishings.
Ques. Does Mithibai College offer scholarships?
Ans. Yes, Mithibai College offers merit-based scholarships, government scholarships for reserved categories (SC/ST/OBC), and financial assistance for economically weaker students.

The Oxford College of Science (TOCS) is a private science college in Bangalore, established in 1994 and affiliated with the University of Bangalore. TOCS Bangalore is an AICTE-approved institution, accredited with an ‘A’ grade by NAAC, and recognised by UGC. Collegedunia ranked The Oxford College of Science as the 7th best science college in Bangalore, and 105th out of 280 in India in 2025.

The Oxford College of Science offers B.Sc., BCA, M.Sc, MCA, and MA English programs. Popular courses at the college are B.Sc. and M.Sc., and students can pursue them in any of the 12 and 11 specializations offered, respectively. The B.Sc. program at TOCS Bangalore costs INR 1.8 lakh for the entire duration, while the total cost for M.Sc. is INR 1.5 lakh.

Admissions to B.Sc, BCA, and MA programs at TOCS Bangalore are merit-based, purely on the previous qualifying examination. Admission to the M.Sc., MCA, and PG diploma programs is entrance-based. The college accepts KMAT and PGCET exam scores for admission through the government quota for MCA, whereas admission through the management quota does not require an entrance test.
The Oxford College of Science has an average placement package of INR 5 LPA. Some of the top recruiters are TCS, Wipro, Capgemini, etc.

The Oxford College of Science is ranked among the top colleges in Bangalore. Reputed agencies like Collegedunia and India Today have ranked TOCS Bangalore as the 7th best science college in Bangalore in 2025. The college in 2025 is ranked among the top 10 in Bangalore for both Fashion Design and Computer Applications.
The table below presents The Oxford College of Science Ranking, in a detailed manner:

The Oxford College of Science offers B.Sc. and BCA at the UG level and M.Sc., MCA, and MA as PG study. In affiliation with Bangalore University, the curriculum at the college follows the NEP, under which the UG programmes extend over four academic years (eight semesters) with multiple entry and exit options. UG students can exit with a certificate after the completion of one academic year; a diploma after completion of two academic years; a regular bachelor’s degree after three academic years; with an option to extend another year for an honours degree.
Presented below are The Oxford College of Science Courses and Fees:
Based on the latest information available, here are the admission dates for all programs at The Oxford College of Science, Bangalore:

The Oxford College of Science admits students to the UG programs entirely based on the scores on the 10+2 qualifying exam. Admission to both the B.Sc. and BCA programs doesn’t require an entrance exam. Similarly, TOCS Bangalore evaluates candidates for the M.Sc. and MA programs on their graduation scores and an interview round. The Oxford College of Science Admission to the MCA program is through PGCET.
The Oxford College of Science accepts PGCET rank for the MCA program. The table below presents the PGCET 2024 Cutoff for the GM category.

The Oxford College of Science has a placement cell that trains the final-year students of each course for placements. It organizes workshops for students to bridge the gap between industries and academia.

The college has not released the placement statistics. According to research, and as per student testimonials on Collegedunia, the lowest salary package secured is INR 2 LPA and highest placement package is INR 9 LPA.
Some of the top recruiters at The Oxford College of Science Placement drive are TCS, Capgemini, Amazon, Wipro, etc.

Sparsha S Reddy, a former BCA student at TOCS Bangalore, reviews on Collegedunia that “Many companies come for campus interviews, and most of them are non-IT companies. The package offered to students is between INR 2 LPA and INR 9 LPA. The Placement cell in our college facilitates all the placement activities.”
The Oxford College of Science has a well-equipped campus with all the necessary facilities. The campus is a 6-storeyed building spread over 2.85 lakh sq. ft. area in HSR layout, Sector 4.

Library: The library houses 34,888 books, 40+ scientific journals, 11000+ online national and international journals and over 2,00,000 online resources. It is equipped with PCs, printers, and an internet facility.
Transport: The college operates a fleet of buses for students, within the city limits.
Classrooms: Classrooms are equipped with ICT tools such as audio-visual facilities, smart boards and interactive display panels to enable comprehensive curriculum delivery.

Laboratories: State-of-the-art Scientific laboratories equipped with high-end equipment and new generation computer systems are available for curriculum delivery, research, training programs and in-house projects. An English Lab with Wordsworth software is provided to enhance the communication skills of the students to enable them to compete globally.

Auditorium: The auditorium has a good seating capacity to enable the students and faculty to organise symposia, conferences and other academic and cultural programs. The auditorium is well designed with video conferencing facilities to interact with well-known personalities in related fields all over the world.

Sports & Yoga: The institution has a well-equipped Sports & Yoga Centre for Indoor games and Yoga programs. A fully equipped Gymnasium is available. A health Centre with a first aid facility and a basic health monitoring facility is also present within the campus.

The Oxford College of Science provides separate residential areas for boys and girls with adequate facilities to make the stay comfortable and memorable. The hostel is equipped with about 500 rooms and a spacious dining area. The Oxford College of Science hostel has facilities like hygienic and nutritious food, a sports centre and reading rooms ensuring the overall well-being of the hostelites. The annual hostel fee, according to student reviews, is 2400 INR, including food, with a monthly breakdown of 1000 INR for room and 1000 INR for meals, covering breakfast, lunch, snacks, and dinner.

Ques. What is the PG diploma program at The Oxford College of Science?

Ans. The Oxford College of Science offers the PG diploma in Cellular and Molecular Diagnostics, which is a 12-month duration including 6 months of training and an internship for 6 months. The maximum intake for the program is 20. Selected students through the Karnataka-Biotechnology Aptitude Test (KBAT) conducted online by the Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (K-tech) are eligible for a monthly stipend of INR 10,000 for 12 months supported by K-tech BITS, Government of Karnataka and the Department of Biotechnology, New Delhi.
Ques. What is the Skill Enhancement Centre at The Oxford College of Science?

Ans. The Oxford Science Skill Enhancement Centre is an initiative to enhance the technical skills of students in order to create greater opportunities for them in the industry. Under TOSSEC, skill enhancement activities are organised such as Hands-on Workshops, Lecture workshop series, MOOCs, Long-term and short-term projects. Skillathon, an annual event, is also organised to stimulate students to learn new skill sets.
Ques. Does the Oxford College of Science offer certificate courses?

Ans. The Oxford College of Science, through its different departments, presents numerous new-age programs, for both UG & PG students. Several new age courses offered by the college are: Do on stream processing (protein), Insect-host plant selection, nano material, PCB designing, Android app development, Web design, mushroom cultivation, and more.
Ques. How is the campus life at The Oxford College of Science?

Ans. The campus life at TOCS Bangalore is labelled as dynamic, offering a balance between academics and extracurricular activities. Multiple students, former and current of the college have praised the environment which encourages interaction among students from various backgrounds. Annual festivals are held such as Freshers' Day, Farewell Days and other cultural programs with varying themes. Though the college doesn't have its own playground, sports competitions are held every year. The college has a sexual harassment cell, a no ragging cell, a sports cell, and a placement cell. NCC and NSS are given importance at the college, where students can be part of leadership training, trekking campus, and other fun outdoor activities.

Jyothi Engineering College Cheruthuruthy (JECC) is a Kerala-based and NAAC-accredited private college that was established in 2002 under the aegis of Trichur Educational Trust and offers courses like B.Tech, M.Tech and PhD at Undergraduate, Postgraduate and Doctorate levels respectively. The institute is affiliated to APJ Abdul Kalam Technological University, approved by AICTE and 5 of its undergraduate programs have NBA accreditation. Admission to college courses is granted to students based on their merit in the previous year’s exam and score in entrance exams like GATE or KEAM and JECC has collaborated with Tata Technologies to bridge the gaps between student’s skills and industry demands under the auspicious initiative called TATA-JYOTHI IIIC.

In addition to this, JECC offers Management Merit Scholarship worth 3 crore/year to deserving and meritorious KEAM Rank Holders and has established a Technology Business Incubator for the purpose of transforming students into job creators, future leaders and fostering a spirit of R & D and Entrepreneurship in ambitious youths. Last but not the least, for its amazing contribution in education and making it affordable for even weaker sections of society, JECC was awarded 4th rank among all Engineering Colleges in Kerala by DTE Kerala, South Asia Best Preparation Center Award for higher education from Cambridge English Assessment and Academic Excellence award in 2013 & 2014 instituted by University of Calicut.

JECC provides 100% assistance to the students during the placement drive. The institute conducts training programs and seminars for knowledge and skill development among the students. Some of the companies that visited during the placements were Cognizant, Mindtree, South Indian Bank, Dell, TCS, Hexaware Technologies and many more.

The Jyothi Engineering College Cheruthuruthy of Kerala offers a full-time and 4 years duration B.Tech Degree course along with a 2-year M.Tech program PhD course. Cited below are the details for the same.
Check: JECC Kerala Courses and Fees
The admission process of Jyothi Engineering College Cheruthuruthy is through online mode, and given below is the detailed procedure for the same.

The JECC of Kerala has a dedicated Placement and Training Cell composed of experienced academic and industry professionals, for the purpose of developing the overall personality of students, enhancing their industry readiness and providing them suitable job opportunities. Another objective of this PAT cell is to provide career related guidance and assistance to students, conduct training programs for them and teachers and organize industrial visits to make them aware about things that work at ground level. Also, numerous reputed MNCs and Banks regularly visit the college campus during recruitment drives to hire JECC students for various profiles. and a host of other companies visit the Campus. Cited below are the details of top recruiters of the institution.

The JECC Kerala is situated in an amazing area and has a comprehensive infrastructure to ensure overall personal and professional development of students. Cited below are some of the wonderful amenities college has for its ambitious students and teachers.

TATA-JYOTHI IIIC: As becoming a top-class innovation center is one of the most important objectives of JECC Kerala, the college has established an Integrated Industrial Incubation Centre in collaboration with TATA Technologies to make students industry ready by offering them a diversified hi-tech course. And students will gain knowledge of Product Design and Development, Design Engineering, PLM Application Engineering, Product Verification Analysis, Electric Vehicle and Connected Autonomous Vehicle, Electric Vehicle Repair and Maintenance, IIoT Engineering, Advanced Industrial Robotics, Advanced Manufacturing Engineering and Machine Tool Operator / CNC Operator. Last, but not the least, these futuristic courses will be helpful in offering internships and wonderful job opportunities to students and inculcating all the essential skills in students need to have before joining the corporate world.

Fablab: With the support of APJ Abdul Kalam Technological University and Kerala Startup Mission, Jyothi Engineering College has established a mini fabrication laboratory in the campus and these labs are well equipped with essential machinery, tools and consumables of worth INR 50 Lakhs, all of which are imported from USA Fablab.

Computer Center: College has also established Computer Labs to make its students digitally proficient and competent and help faculty members complete their work. And these labs are well-resourced with 210 desktop computers, printers, scanners, LCD projectors and all the systems are connected with two 300 Mbps leased line internet connections and a 20Mbps NMEICT connection. And visiting time of these labs is from 9 AM to 7.30 PM on all weekdays. Apart from this, students and staff members can request for any services via mail and these labs are primarily used for practical and technical training sessions, short-term courses, and national-level workshops for students as well as for online placement and other exams. It is worth to be noted that JECC is authorized to conduct online entrance exams of GATE, JIPMER, CAT COMEDK, Cambridge, RRB, NABARD, ESIC, CUET, Bank Exams and NSEIT etc.

Transportation: As JECC campus is located 30 Kms away from the Thrissur town, hence the college provides transport facility to both students and staff and 20 buses are there to pick up and drop 600 students and staff members from their home to the college and vice-versa.

Canteen: With the intention of serving delicious and hygienic South Indian snacks and food items to students and staff members at an affordable price range, the college has an aesthetically developed canteen where one can find students after classes or during lunch. And this canteen remains open from 8 AM to 5 PM on all working days including Saturdays. Also, 2 coffee shops operate inside the campus to serve coffee and other refreshments drinks to both staff and students.

Auditorium and Seminar Halls: JECC Kerala has established an Auditorium too in 725 sq.m of area and a seating capacity of 1000+ students in the western academic block, to conduct special programs and events. Along with this, the college has fully air-conditioned seminar halls which they call as 'Decennial Hall and Insight Hall' and these halls are fully resourced with modern digital sound systems, LCD projectors and podiums, etc. These halls are primarily used for events and activities like seminars, guest lectures, cultural activities and staff meetings, etc.

Technology Business Incubator: For the purpose of fostering the environment of innovation and entrepreneurship in college, JECC has started a wonderful initiative called TBI whose main objective is to transform students and faculties’ Science and Engineering related ideas into products, processes and services for commercial exploitation and for the benefit of society. And at present, through TBI students and teachers are exploring areas such as Information and Communication Technologies, VLSI, embedded systems, Instrumentation, energy, mechatronics and robotics.

Fitness Center: JECC also has a fitness center and gym with all the modern equipment including bench press, pec deck, bicep curl, lateral pulley and body twister machines and expert trainers to train students and staff members and keep them physically fit and healthy because college believes in the fact that a healthy mind resides in a healthy body. Girls and boys can visit this gym from 6-7:30 AM in the morning and 4:45 -6:30 PM in the evening.

Chapel: For the purpose of satisfying the spiritual and prayer-related needs of students, JECC has a cathedral on the 3rd floor of the administrative block and the college regularly motivates students to spend some time here. In addition to this, Mass is celebrated every day in this Chapel for hostlers and for the catholic students and staff on the first Friday of the month in the College Auditorium.

Sports Facilities: JECC Kerala has big playgrounds for students to play outdoor games like Volleyball and Basketball and Table Tennis is also there for them. Additionally, the college has a 200m track for running events and standard long jump pit for jumps and enough area for conducting Throws.

Language Lab: Last but not the least, JECC has a language lab with all the required audio-visual facilities to expose the students to the language of the native english speaker by using the software ORELL. And using this software, students can even enhance their interview skills, vocabulary and communication skills.

15 May, 2026 CUET UG 2026 examination is currently ongoing till May 31, 2026.

Deen Dayal Upadhyaya College (DDUC) is a government college that was established in 1990. The college is approved by the University Grants Commission (UGC) and has received a ‘B’ grade accreditation from NAAC.
According to the Collegedunia Ranking 2025, the college is ranked 25th in the Science category in India. In the NIRF Ranking 2025, it is placed 27th in the Overall category among colleges in India.

CUET UG 2026 exam will be held in May 2026, while the result is expected in July 2026. The registration process took place between January and February 2026, with a short re-opening window again in February 2026.
Ques. Do I need to take the CUET exam to get admission into Deen Dayal Upadhyaya College (DDUC)?

Ans. Yes, the CUET exam is compulsory for admission in Delhi University colleges like Deen Dayal Upadhyaya College. The student must appear in the CUET UG exam and get a score. After result, students need to register on the DU CSAS portal and fill college choices. Admission seat give on the basis of CUET score and subject combination only.
Ques. I finish CUET exam. What next step I should follow for the DDUC admission process now?

Ans. After the CUET results come, students need to go DU CSAS admission portal and register. Then fill course and college preference like DDUC. University make merit list based on the CUET score. If the score is good, the seat allotment will show in the portal. Then the student accept seat and pay admission fee to confirm the college. This process happens in a few counselling rounds.

The B.Sc (Hons.) at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya College is a 3-year undergraduate course. It is offered in specialisations such as Computer Science, Electronics, Chemistry, Zoology, Physics, Mathematics, and Botany. The annual fee is INR 47,555, and the total course fee is INR 1,42,665.

Ques. I want the cheapest course in DDUC. Which course have lowest yearly fees for students?

Ans. In DDUC, many UG course have almost similar fees. Courses like B.Sc, B.Com Hons and BA have around INR 31,555 yearly fees. BMS and some B.Sc Hons course cost little more. Most Delhi University colleges keep fees low because they are government colleges. The total 3-year fee is mostly between about INR 94,000 and INR 1.42 lakh.
Ques. I study science in class 12. Can I apply BMS course in DDUC also?

Ans. Yes student from the science stream can also apply to BMS in DDUC. Stream is not a strict problem. But students must appear CUET exam with the required subjects like Mathematics and General Test. Admission happens through CUET score and DU counselling. BMS course duration is 3 years, and the yearly fee is around INR 35,000 approx.

Deen Dayal Upadhyaya College (DDUC) is affiliated with the University of Delhi. The college offers many UG courses for students. The college offers B.Sc (Hons) as its popular courses. DDUC Admission in these courses is mainly based on the CUET exam, and after that, students have to go through the DU CSAS counselling process.
DU CSAS Application Fee
Step 1: Appear for the CUET Exam
First student need to appear in CUET UG exam with the required subjects. Without giving CUET exam student can not take admission.
Step 2: Register on DU CSAS Portal
After CUET result come, candidates have to register themself on DU CSAS portal for starting the admission process further.
Step 3: Fill College Preference
Students have to select their prefered courses and colleges in the portal. They can also choose DDUC in the list if they want admission there.
Step 4: Seat Allotment
Seats are given on the basis of CUET score, category and also depend on seat availability in the college.
Step 5: Document Verification
Students need to upload all required documents for verification. If the documents not correct, then admission may get problem.
Step 6: Pay Admission Fee
Candidates must pay the admission fee online to confirm the seat otherwise the seat can be cancelled by the college.
Step 7: Admission Confirmation
After document verification and fee payment is done, admission is confirmed and students can start attending their classes in the college.
Ques. I forget upload the document in DU CSAS portal. Will I still get admission in DDUC?

Ans. If the document is not upload correct in the CSAS portal, admission can face a problem. University checks documents like class 10 and 12 marksheet, CUET scorecard, photo and category certificate. If something is missing, the college may reject or ask for correction. So students should upload a clear scanned copy and check carefully before final submission in the portal.
Ques. I get low CUET score. Can I still get a seat in DDUC or DU colleges?

Ans. Low CUET score still has a chance, but depend on course demand and seat availability. In DU counselling, many rounds happen, and cut off change every round. Some courses with less competition may give a seat with a lower score, also. Students should fill out many college preferences in the CSAS portal to increase their admission chances.

For B.Sc (Hons.) Computer Science, the CUET closing marks in 2025 admission was around 676 in the first round. In the last round of seat allotment, the closing marks went down to around 606. This shows that the DDUC cutoff can change in different rounds depending on seat availability and number of students applying.
Ques. I scored around 600 marks in the CUET exam. Can I still get a course in the DDUC college?

Ans. Yes, admission is still possible in some courses. In Delhi University cutoff depends on the course demand and category also. Popular courses like B.Com Hons need very high marks, sometimes 700+ or more. But some science courses have lower cutoffs also. If the score is around 600, the student may still get a seat in later rounds.
Ques. I see a cutoff change every round. Why DDUC cutoff become lower in the last rounds?

Ans. Cutoff change because many student upgrade their college or leave seat after the first round. When a seat becomes empty, the next round cutoff become little lower. This happens in DU CSAS counselling every year. So students with slightly lower marks sometimes get admission in later rounds when seats are still available.

As per the latest DDUC placement record released by the institute, the highest package was around INR 8.12 LPA. According to the NIRF 2025 data, the median salary package for UG 3-year course was around INR 4.75 LPA.

Some of the top recruiters of DDUC include Accenture, RSA, WTW, DE Shaw, EY, PWC, Wipro, Maruti Suzuki, CodeYoung and many others. These companies come from different sectors like Finance, Consulting, IT, Manufacturing and FMCG.

Ques. I want a good placement from DDUC. Which course usually gives better job opportunities here?

Ans. In DDUC, some courses have better placement chance like BMS and B.Com Hons. These course related to business and finance, so many companies come for hiring. Companies like EY, PwC, Accenture and Wipro visit the campus. The average salary is normally around 4–6 LPA, but it also depends on skill and internship.
Ques. I did not get a campus placement in DDUC. What other career option students choose after graduation?

Ans. Many student not depend only on campus placement. Some go for higher studies like MBA, MSc or professional courses. Many students also prepare for government exams like UPSC, SSC or banking. Some students do internships and an off-campus job search also. In the NIRF data, many students also choose higher studies after graduation

Ques. Is attendance very strict in Deen Dayal Upadhyaya College for regular classes?

Ans. Yes attendance rule is there in college. In Delhi University colleges, students normally need around 67% attendance in each subject. If attendance is very low, then the student may not be allowed to sit in exam, or internal marks can be reduced. So, better attend classes regularly, even if the timetable is sometimes a little hectic.
Ques. Can students do an internship while studying in DDUC during their graduation years?

Ans. Yes, many students do internships while studying in college. Companies and startups offer part-time or short internships for DU students. Many internships also happen online. Doing an internship help student learn skills and also helps in placement later. Some companies, like consulting and finance firms, also give internship opportunities to DU students.
Ques. How many students actually get placement every year in the DDUC college campus drive?

Ans. Placement numbers change every year. According to NIRF placement data, around 97 students from the UG 3-year course got placed in 2025 from the eligible batch. Many other students choose higher studies like MBA or MSc instead of placement. So the placement number looks smaller, but many students continue studying after graduation.
Ques. Are hostel rooms available easily for all students in Deen Dayal Upadhyaya College?

Ans. Hostel seats are limited in the college. Total capacity is around 180 students in boys' and girls' hostels together, so not everyone get hostel. Rooms are usually twin-sharing and have basic furniture like a bed, a study table and a locker. Because of the lack of seats, many students choose PG or a rented room near the Dwarka area.
Ques. Is Deen Dayal Upadhyaya College considered a good DU college for science courses?

Ans. Yes, many students consider DDUC a good college for science courses. The college offers many B.Sc Hons specialisation like Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics and Computer Science. It is also ranked around 27th among colleges in India in NIRF 2025, which show good academic reputation. Because of this, many CUET students choose it.

Deen Dayal Upadhyaya College (DDUC), Delhi University, will mostly use entrance-based admissions in 2025, adhering to standardized protocols established by the University of Delhi. The Common University Entrance Test (CUET-UG), which is administered by the National Testing Agency (NTA), is used to admit students to undergraduate (UG) programs like BA, BSc, BCom, and BMS. To apply for admission using your CUET scorecard, follow these steps: download and print your CUET-UG scorecard from the NTA portal; then register on the admission/counselling portal of each participating university; pay the registration fee; submit and lock your preferences; attend counselling; upload documents; accept your seat and pay admission fees.

Ajay Kumar Garg Engineering College popularly known as AKGEC, was established in 1998 in Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh. The institute is affiliated to Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University, Lucknow, and is approved by the All India Council for Technical Education. AKGEC is the only Engineering college to be awarded A++ by NAAC. AKGEC has been ranked 77 out of 246 colleges in engineering by India Today and 131 out of 762 colleges by Collegedunia in 2025.

AKGEC offers B.Tech, M.Tech, and MCA courses. AKGEC offers B.Tech as its flagship course in 12 specializations, and M.Tech is offered in 4 specializations. The admission to B.Tech is based on JEE-Main score, followed by UPTAC Counselling or Direct Admission followed by AKGEC Entrance Test & Interview. The overall cutoff rank for General Category Students and AI Quota for JEE-Main ranges between 87578 - 567879. AKGEC B.Tech first-year fee is INR 1.24 Lakhs - 1.42 Lakhs. Out of 1,166 eligible students, 1,086 secured placements, while 9 students opted for higher studies. Some of the top recruiters included Amazon, Google, Infosys, Wipro, and Tech Mahindra.

Each hostel at AKGEC has a separate mess with a well-equipped kitchen and dining area providing hygienic, nutritious, and wholesome meals. Hostels have a gymnasium as well as indoor and outdoor sports facilities. Each hostel also has a TV room and a library with magazines and fiction/general reading books. Hostels are equipped with eco-friendly solar water heating systems. Hostels also have canteens and provision stores for minor items of daily requirements.

There are 2 hostels for boys named “Junior Boys Hostel Complex” and “Senior Boys Hostel Complex.” The Junior Boys Hostel can accommodate 300 students with double occupancy rooms. The Senior Boys Hostel can accommodate 600 students with single & triple occupancy rooms.
There are 3 hostels for girls at AKGEC. These hostels have double and triple seater rooms and accommodate about 600 students.
Ques. How do I get admission to AKGEC Ghaziabad after Class 12 without a high JEE Main rank?

Ans. AKGEC offers management quota seats. These seats don’t strictly follow the JEE Main cutoff, but you still need at least 65% in Class 12 with PCM. You’ll need to contact the admission cell directly (usually in July) and might have to attend a short interview or fill out an internal form. Many students use this route if they didn’t score well in JEE Main but still want a reputed private college with good placements.
Ques. Is the placement really good at AKGEC Ghaziabad or just average?

Ans. Placements at AKGEC are above average, especially if you’re in CSE, IT, or ECE. In 2024, more than 1,000 students were placed, and some even got offers from Amazon, TCS, and Deloitte. The average package was INR 5.5 LPA, and a few top students grabbed INR 20–30 LPA jobs (mainly off-campus or coding-based roles). The college also gives pre-placement training, hackathons, and internship support, which actually helps. If you’re willing to work on your coding and communication skills, you’ll have solid chances of getting placed.
Ques. What is the actual student life like at AKGEC Ghaziabad?

Ans. Student life at AKGEC is a mix of serious academics and active club culture. Classes and labs are regular, but there’s also enough time for events. You can join clubs like Technocratz (coding), Robonica (robotics), Kalakriti (arts), or Dramatics, and participate in the annual fest “Verve.” The campus is clean and disciplined, and the hostels are decent with proper mess food. Since it’s close to Noida, you also get access to tech workshops and industrial visits. Overall, it's a balanced and growth-oriented environment.

I'm not the biggest fan of my college, but let me give you a rundown of what’s good and not-so-great about it. If you’re considering a non-circuit branch like CSE or IT, any AKTU-affiliated college is pretty similar. Opportunities and salary packages for these branches are almost the same everywhere. Now, about my college:

I joined AKGEC back in 2015, and that's when I first met Prof. S. L. Kapoor. At the time, I didn't know he'd become our PROCTOR, and he's still in that role today. He's kind of like Professor Severus Snape from the Harry Potter series, if you're familiar with it. The reason I mention him is that, like Snape, he's really strict and disciplined, but also super kind and a great mentor. I could go on and on about him.

The main point is that if the MCA department is under his leadership, you have nothing to worry about. If you're studying MCA with someone like Prof. S. L. Kapoor guiding you, you can be confident about your choice. Hope this helps you out!

AKG Engineering College in Ghaziabad is quite well-known, especially in the AKTU network, as one of the top engineering colleges. Generally, the college manages to maintain decent placement records each year. Most students who get placed are usually from the CS or IT branches, and they can expect salary packages ranging from 3 to 8 lakh.

However, the college tends to focus heavily on academics and doesn't really host events or support students preparing for competitive exams. The college's reputation has grown because of some students who achieve high rankings in university and competitive exams like GATE and CAT. Their success comes from their own hard work and dedication, not necessarily from the college's efforts.

If you're at AKG or any college under AKTU, it's a good idea to start preparing from your first semester. Don't wait until your third or fourth year. Make sure to develop your technical skills as much as possible. The college has great infrastructure and offers technical and cultural societies, like Software Incubator, CSI, Big Data, and Cloud Cell, which are excellent for skill development. If you're studying CS or IT, your chances of getting placed through the college are better.

I'm in my final year at Ajay Kumar Garg Engineering College, so I've seen quite a bit. Up until my sixth semester, I thought differently about the place. Seniors told me that Infosys was the major recruiter and if you missed that, your chances of getting a job were slim. But that turned out to be untrue because there were plenty of job opportunities for everyone, at least in the CS/IT fields. For other branches like Mechanical Engineering, ECE, or EI, it's tougher, though ECE does see some placements. This year's placements have been better than before. If you're in CS/IT, there's about a 95% chance you'll land a job.

Beyond placements, though, the college doesn't have much else to offer. If I could go back, I wouldn't choose this college again. The faculty isn't great, and by the time you hit your third or fourth semester, you might lose interest in studying. There's a lot of favoritism toward top students. No fun events or fests happen here. While the hostels are decent, they're pricey. The location isn't great either. The college is strict about attendance and even sends letters home if you're below 75%. They won't ease up, even in your final year, and might bar you from placements without reason.

The focus here is mostly on rote learning, not so much on technical skills. A few students in my class are technically brilliant, but that's not due to the college. There are many societies like TAAL for dance, Euphony for music, and GOONJ for drama. These groups have some talented people. For the CS/IT students, technical groups like Software Incubator and OSSRD are worthwhile; others are not very useful.

I'm in the CSE branch, so my insights are mostly about that. I don't know much about the other branches. In the end, you can do well anywhere if you're determined and willing to work hard. Make the most of your time, create lasting memories, and you'll make great friends here. But you might end up wishing you'd picked a different college, and that's a common feeling.

Ajay Kumar Garg Engineering College, or AKGEC, is linked with AKTU, formerly known as UPTU. While it's considered a top institution, many students aren't too thrilled about it. The term "finest" seems to be a bit of a joke here since almost everything you do results in a fine. Seriously, they seem more interested in taking your money. Return a library book late, even if exams are happening, and you'll face a penalty. Arrive late to class? They're ready with a laptop and scanner to fine you for that too.

The college administration isn't exactly known for being supportive of students. If you have any issues, it's apparently your fault. The mindset is that you shouldn't have problems, and if you do, tough luck, it's not their concern. Sadly, about 2-3 students have taken their own lives over the past couple of years. Professor Colonel S.L. Kapoor is often mentioned as a significant source of stress, and I'm only mentioning this anonymously because of the potential backlash during my remaining time at college.

Even with valid medical reasons, the administration insists on attendance, threatening serious consequences if you miss classes. This could mean public shaming or scolding when you're actually in need of support, and of course, there's likely a fine involved.

The college feels more like a strict boarding school. They're overly focused on academic results and the Chancellor's Medal, but when it comes to placements, they don't seem to care much. Quality education is lacking, so students often study independently to achieve good scores.

Involvement in NGOs or humanitarian work is discouraged by S.L. Kapoor, who dismisses them as scams. However, they still expect you to have a certificate for such activities and criticize you if you don't.

While AKGEC claims to support nearby villages, they don't appear to follow through with any real help, which is disappointing. Despite having some good aspects, the negative ones seem to outweigh them significantly.

My first day at AKGEC was quite the experience. It started off as a regular day until the Discipline Committee, or DCs as we call them, came to our first-year-only hostel to take us to class. We all lined up, with fresh faces among us, while seniors stood by counting us. We had to learn some rules, like saying Jai Hind to everyone we met, because they might be seniors or faculty. You'll spot your batchmates because they'll be the ones in fully tucked-in, long-sleeved shirts until the Freshers' Party.

We were led to our classes, grouped with others from our branch, all unfamiliar faces. Seniors came in and had us do silly things like introducing ourselves to each of them and asking their names. I still don't get the point of that—it's not like we needed to know every senior's name.

What do you mean by guaranteed? Are you thinking that studying is optional? Or do you believe in building up your skills both practically and theoretically in your field? Keep in mind that if you work on developing yourself with valuable skills and knowledge, you'll eventually find the right job, either through campus placements or outside opportunities. If not, there are always BPO jobs available, which colleges may use to claim 100% placement. Regarding the college, I assume you've already checked its reputation. Thanks for asking!

CU, like other private colleges in the Punjab area, has its challenges. On the other hand, AKG stands out because it's located in the NCR, an area full of industries. It also has NAAC and NBA certifications, takes part in many national and international contests, and offers good placement opportunities. Good luck!

Choosing between VIT and Ajay Kumar Garg Engineering College (AKGEC) really comes down to what you want from your college experience. I'm graduating from AKGEC this year, and honestly, when I think about it, it didn't quite feel like a typical college experience. The campus looks great, almost like a picnic spot, and the teachers have good qualifications, but their teaching methods aren't the best. Since it's a UPTU college, there's not much room for creativity; classes can get pretty dull, and you'll spend a lot of time writing instead of really understanding concepts. It often feels like you're just memorizing stuff to do well on exams.

Another thing to note is that the faculty and management seem to care a lot about your grades. If you approach them with an issue, the first thing they'll ask is your percentage, and they form their opinion of you based on that. Even if you're a great person, having lower grades might affect how they see you. The college is quite strict and disciplined because it's run by retired army and navy personnel, and grading can be tough. It's not a laid-back environment.

If you're planning to study for competitive exams, AKGEC might not be the best fit since the college doesn't offer much support for that. When it comes to placements, students in CS and IT have the upper hand, but other colleges might offer better opportunities for students in different branches.

So, if you're someone who loves studying and doesn't mind a strict environment, AKGEC could be a good choice, especially if you're interested in CS or IT. But if you're looking for a fun college experience with parties and making lifelong friends, AKGEC might not be the place for you. In that case, VIT would likely be a better option.

I think it’s high time people stop comparing colleges and start working on themselves because the actual worth of a college is defined by your own willingness to make the best out of your situation. What actually matters is

So what I mean is don’t it all depends on how well you cope up and strive in any given college or situation. It depends more on you than the college you are associated with. In Fact, any other college will also offer you the same opportunities provided you are ready to make the best out of them.

Acharya Nagarjuna University Centre for Distance (ANUCDE) Education is a substituent college of Acharya Nagarjuna University. subject_lists.title: DG Ruparel College Campus and Facilities
subjects: Hostel: The college provides hostel facilities within the campus for boys that can accommodate 70 students. It provides necessary housekeeping services for cleaning, security, and a recreational room with a TV, newspaper, and indoor games for the students.

Counseling Center: The college has a career guidance & counseling center, namely “SUMAN,” which is available on Wednesday and Thursday from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m., totally free of cost. There, they guided students for career development, personality development, and personal problems.

Library: The college provides a well-resourced library with over 300 students (including staff) and has a different section for girls. The library contains a huge collection of general books, journals & magazines, CDs, rare books, e-books, and reference books, and it has 4 computers for OPAC.

Gymkhana: The college has a well-equipped gymkhana. It provides necessary space and equipment for various indoor and outdoor sports like cricket, swimming, lawn tennis, shooting, and badminton. It encourages students to participate in indoor and outdoor games and enhances their skills. The College Gymkhana provides facilities for most of the games, such as table tennis, kho-kho, kabaddi, volleyball, basketball, football, hockey, and softball, provided to their students.
Canteen: Located in the Gymkhana building with a proper seating arrangement, the college canteen provides a variety of freshly prepared food items to the students at an affordable price.

Ramnarain Ruia Autonomous College, located in Matunga, Mumbai, is a public college started in 1937 by the Shikshan Prasarak Mandali. It is affiliated with the University of Mumbai and became autonomous in 2017. The college offers undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral programs in arts, sciences, media, and vocational studies. It has NAAC A+ accreditation with a 3.70 CGPA and ranks in the 201-300 band by NIRF 2025 for colleges. It is approved by the UGC and recognized as a College of Excellence.

The college provides popular courses like BA in Psychology, History, and Media, B.Sc in Biotechnology, Computer Science, and Microbiology, B.Voc in Travel and Tourism, and M.Sc in Physics and Biochemistry. Admission for BA, B.Sc, and B.Voc uses class 12 marks, while M.Sc needs a college entrance test and bachelor’s marks.

Placement data from 2024 shows a median package of INR 3 LPA for undergraduates and ₹2.52 LPA for postgraduates. Top recruiters include Wipro, TCS, Infosys, Sun Pharma, and Veena World, with 12.5% of undergraduates and 42.66% of postgraduates placed.

Ramnarain Ruia Autonomous College in Mumbai offers B.Sc, BA, B.Voc, and M.Sc admissions for 2026. For B.Sc, students must pass Class 12 Science with 50% marks. Subjects like Physics, Chemistry, Biology, or Mathematics are needed for courses such as Biotechnology or Computer Science. Admission is merit-based on Class 12 marks, with no entrance exam.

For BA and B.Voc, students from any stream (Arts, Science, Commerce) with 50% in Class 12 can apply. Popular options include Psychology, History, Media and Communication, and Travel and Tourism Management. Admission depends only on school marks and merit lists.
For M.Sc, candidates need a bachelor’s degree with 50% marks in the relevant subject. Admission includes a college entrance test, with selection based on test scores and degree marks.
The application process starts online at muugadmission.samarth.edu.in or the college portal. Reserved seats are kept for SC (13%), ST (7%), and OBC (19%) as per University of Mumbai rules.

The Ramnarain Ruia Autonomous College campus is in Matunga, Mumbai, and has two connected buildings. It is easy to reach by train or bus. The campus has many facilities for students’ needs.

The Library has 150,000 books, including rare ones, and reading halls for study. There are modern labs for science courses like Biotechnology and Computer Science, including the Dr. P.S. Ramanathan Advanced Instrumentation Centre. A language lab and research centers help with studies. The campus has Wi-Fi, CCTV, and clean classrooms with good air.

For sports, the Sports Academy offers indoor and outdoor games, a gym, and coaching. A shuttle service helps students move around. The Hostel gives rooms for students from far places. The Canteen serves tasty, clean food. A medical room is there for health needs.

The college supports all students, with a special Cell for Visually Challenged Students offering Braille books and audio help. The Students Mutual Aid Fund helps with money problems since 1948. An Incubation Centre supports new business ideas. There is a big auditorium for events and a garden area for relaxing.
The Vidyarthi Pratinidhi Mandal organizes festivals like Utsav and Aarohan for fun and learning. The campus is safe and friendly, helping over 7,000 students with their studies and activities.
Ques. How are the hostel facilities at Ramnarain Ruia?

Ans. Ramnarain Ruia Autonomous College has hostel facilities for outstation students The hostel offers rooms with basic needs like beds, study tables, and storage. It has clean bathrooms and a mess for food. There is security with CCTV and staff. Boys and girls have separate areas. The hostel is on campus, making it easy to reach classes. It also has Wi-Fi and common rooms for relaxing. Students can apply during admission. The hostel supports a safe and simple stay for students studying at the college.
Ques. Does Ramnarain Ruia offer any scholarships or fee waivers to students?

Ans. Yes, Ramnarain Ruia Autonomous College offers scholarships and fee waivers. The Students Mutual Aid Fund, started in 1948, helps students with money problems. There are government scholarships for SC, ST, OBC, and other reserved groups. Merit-based scholarships are given for high marks in class 12 or college exams. Fee waivers are available for low-income students or special categories like differently-abled. Students apply through the college office with documents like mark sheets and income proof.
Ques. How is the transport connectivity for Ramnarain Ruia?

Ans. Ramnarain Ruia Autonomous College in Matunga, Mumbai, has good transport links. It is close to Matunga railway station on the Central Railway line, just a short walk away. Dadar and King’s Circle stations are also nearby. Local buses stop near the college, connecting to many parts of Mumbai. Auto-rickshaws and taxis are easy to find. The college offers a shuttle service for students on campus. This makes it simple for students to travel from different areas of the city to attend classes.
Ques. Is the library at Ramnarain Ruia useful for competitive exams?

Ans. The library at Ramnarain Ruia Autonomous College is helpful for competitive exams. It has 150,000 books, including study materials for exams like UPSC, MPSC, and bank tests. There are reference books, past question papers, and magazines. The library offers quiet reading halls and computers for research. It also has e-books and online resources. Students preparing for exams can use these to study. The staff helps find needed books. The library is open daily for students to use for exam preparation.
Ques. How is the student-faculty ratio at Ramnarain Ruia?

Ans. The student-faculty ratio at Ramnarain Ruia Autonomous College is about 35:1. The college has over 7,000 students and around 200 faculty members across arts, sciences, and vocational courses. This ratio means each teacher handles a moderate number of students, allowing for class teaching and some personal help. Faculty teach subjects like Biotechnology, Psychology, and Physics. The ratio supports lectures and practical labs but may limit one-on-one time.

Ques. How does Jai Hind College’s location in Mumbai actually benefit students?

Ans. Being located at Churchgate, Jai Hind provides access to everything, it's literally walking distance across the board for internships in media houses, finance firms, and NGOs. Even location-wise to cultural hubs like NCPA, Marine Drive, and art galleries nearby means exposure isn't limited to academia, the city becomes an extension of the classroom for us.
Ques. What makes the campus life at Jai Hind different from other Mumbai colleges?

Ans. There is a huge buzz at Jai Hind with events run by students, like Detour (BMM fest) and Entourage (BMS fest). We as students manage our own events on (marketing) sponsorships, PR and logistics etc. It literally feels like managing a startup. This is not something that every college allows you to experience at that scale.
Ques. Do students at Jai Hind feel the teaching style is more traditional or modern?

Ans. Most faculty are not stuffy or old-fashioned at JHC Mumbai. In programs like BMM and BMS, faculty focus on assignments that measure presentations, projects and case studies, rather than rote learning. Even in the more theory based subjects faculty relate back to real-life examples in Mumbai, which engage us more in both classes and learning.
Ques. How strong is the peer culture at Jai Hind competitive or collaborative?

Ans. At JHC it’s probably a mix, but in a good way. Since many of the students here are from various regions of India, you get a diverse motivated group as a peer group. While competition exists around placements and fests, on a day-to-day basis it feels more collaborative—people share notes, help each other with project work, and work together in clubs. That balance is a great benefit for all of us.

Jai Hind College is top-notch if you ask me. Most people in Mumbai would probably say the same thing. Good luck with your admission!

Joining Jai Hind College for my MBA has been such a rewarding experience. The curriculum is really relevant, focusing on practical knowledge that can be applied in real-life situations. The faculty is student-friendly and highly qualified, which makes learning enjoyable. Plus, the campus life is vibrant, with various events and activities happening all the time. The overall atmosphere encourages personal and academic growth, making it worth every bit of the effort.

I’m doing my Bachelor of Arts [BA] in Psychology at Jai Hind College, and I have to say, the faculty here is top-notch! They are very experienced and make the classes engaging. The course is well-structured, and while we don’t have many internship opportunities, the learning experience is solid. The campus is lively, and there are various clubs and activities to join, which keeps things interesting. The fees are quite manageable too, making it a great choice for students like me.
Jai Hind College in Mumbai offers several scholarships and financial aids for students. Here are some of them:

I think the beauty of the crowd in KC College mainly comes from the camaraderie and the involvement in various clubs and events like SCOPE and the sports day. In my B.Com program, we have a great mix of students who are all focused on their goals but still find time to socialize and participate in extracurricular activities. The friendly nature of both students and faculty creates a warm environment that feels like a community.

Jai Hind College admits 170 students into the psychology program in FYBA, but by the time TYBA rolls around, 132 of them have to leave because there aren't enough seats for psychology majors. This year, due to the pandemic, other colleges aren't taking outside students and are prioritizing their own, leaving us with the choice of either settling for part majors or abandoning our career plans. They also delayed giving us the results, so by the time we got them, the few colleges that were open to outsiders had already closed admissions.

When we ask them to add more seats, they tell us to reach out to Mumbai University, but the university tells us to tell the colleges to contact them. It's especially frustrating when we qualify for a full major with over 80% marks. The principal doesn't reply to our emails, and the teachers just keep saying we should settle for part majors. Meanwhile, colleges like Mithibai and KC are giving spots to all their internal students who scored 75% and above. It feels really unfair, especially during this pandemic when other institutions are going out of their way to support students, but our college just isn't willing to help. I wouldn't suggest Jai Hind to anyone!
I'm a BCom student at Jai Hind, and here's how my two years have been:
Festivals: All year round, you'll see stalls set up by companies sponsoring events. Our college is full of festivals, and it's fair to say we host the most grand-scale festivals.

Co-curriculars: If you join in, you'll probably spend more time on these activities than in class. I've been actively involved for two years, and in my final year, I'm focusing more on side reading to become more skilled than the average BCom student.

Extra-curriculars: There are loads of chances to take on projects with different associations in subjects like Accountancy, Economics, Political Science, English, Commerce, History, and more. Successful projects might even get you to represent the college at the University level.
Friendships: You'll always have friends around. You’ll find people you can connect with easily.
Canteen/Cafeteria: The food here is a favorite among students, except maybe for those into modeling or fitness. It's tasty and affordable.
Q. Is Jai Hind a mini world in itself? A. Absolutely!

Overall, Jai Hind College is a blast. Every college feels like its own little world. Students everywhere have stories like mine about their colleges. I've shared my experiences from Jai Hind. If you liked what you read, consider applying and joining us!
Hope you're doing well.

Don't stress about taking a gap year; it won't block your admission chances. The course you choose is what really matters. Some courses like BSc in Physics (Hons) and BA PS (Hons) might be tougher to get into, but I'm not entirely certain. It's a good idea to look at the previous year's cutoffs to get a better idea. Being a girl and in the SC category definitely works in your favor. In my opinion, there's more than a 90% chance you'll get into these colleges.

Yes, Jai Hind College is a good choice for BMS. The faculty here is quite friendly and supportive, which makes learning a lot easier. The curriculum is designed to be relevant to real-life situations, which I really appreciate. Plus, there are plenty of co-curricular activities that keep the campus life engaging.

The campus is spacious, and there are various events happening regularly that enhance the overall college experience. Overall, I feel like I'm getting a solid education here while also enjoying my time.

Delhi Metropolitan Education, established in 2012, is a premier private institute of Law and Management located in Sector 62, Noida. It heads a variety of schools and academic programs like DME Law School, DME Management School, and DME Media School. These schools offer BBA, BA(Journalism & Mass Communication), BA LLB(Hons.), BBA + LLB (Hons.), and LLM.

Admissions to the Delhi Metropolitan Education programs are conducted based on the scores of IPU CET/ CUET UG/ CLAT UG. 85% of the seats in counseling are reserved for Delhi Category students. Admission to the flagship BBA program is conducted based on the performance in the IPU CET exam conducted by GGSIP University. Seats are later allocated based on the counseling round results and the reservation quota. The average fee for the 1st-year BBA program is INR 1.15 Lakhs.

Ques. What scholarships are offered by Delhi Metropolitan Education?

Ans. Delhi Metropolitan Education offers merit scholarships to reward meritorious students with financial assistance. Scholarships are distributed based on their previous academic records or performance. Students acquiring ranks from 1 to 4000 in the IPU CET entrance examinations are offered a 20%-50% scholarship. CLAT ranks are also considered during scholarship.
Ques. Does Delhi Metropolitan Education offer hostel accommodation?

Ans. Delhi Metropolitan Education has collaborated with Delhi Technical Campus (Sister college of DME) to use their hostel facilities, which accommodate up to 700 students. Separate hostels for Male and female students with well-furnished rooms and attached toilets are offered. Single, Double, and triple sharing rooms are available. Mess facilities are available for the resident students. Transportation from the hostel is provided daily.
Ques. Is Delhi Metropolitan Education private or government?
Ans. Delhi Metropolitan Education is a private institute of Law and Management. Established in 2012, it is situated in Noida. Affiliated with GGSIP, it offers law, management, and arts courses.
Ques. What is the cost of Delhi Metropolitan Education?

Ans. Delhi Metropolitan Education offers 6 courses across BBA, BA LLB (Hons.), BBA + LLB (Hons.), and BA (Journalism & Mass Communication). The average fee of the flagship course of BBA is INR 1.15 Lakh.
Ques. Is Delhi Metropolitan Education a good college?

Ans. Delhi Metropolitan Education, affiliated with Guru Gobind Singh Indraprastha University, is a private management and law institute located in Noida. Admissions are accepted through the IPU CET exam or CUET, or CLAT UG exams. The infrastructural facilities and well-rounded curriculum are the pros of this institute. But the placement opportunities are not as enough as compared to other colleges.

Students can join clubs for dramatics, debating, NSS, NCC, and various literary, music, and dance societies. The college also encourages sports, providing training and facilities for indoor and outdoor games. These platforms help students explore talents, build leadership skills, and gain exposure beyond academics, making college life vibrant and engaging.
Ques. Does KC College support international exposure?

Ans. Yes, KC College provides students with opportunities for international exposure through collaborations, exchange programs, and academic tie-ups. The college hosts seminars, guest lectures, and workshops conducted by international experts, enhancing global learning perspectives. Students are encouraged to participate in global research projects, cultural exchanges, and international conferences. These initiatives broaden their horizons, develop cross-cultural understanding, and make them globally competitive. By integrating international opportunities into its academic structure, KC College prepares students for careers that demand global competence.
Ques. Does KC College use digital learning resources?

Ans. Yes, KC College integrates digital resources into its teaching and learning process. The college has smart classrooms, digital libraries, and e-learning portals that provide access to e-books, journals, and databases. During online or hybrid learning, students benefit from recorded lectures, video tutorials, and interactive platforms. ICT-enabled teaching methods make classes more engaging and research-friendly. The use of digital tools prepares students for the modern workplace, ensuring they are comfortable with technology-driven education and global learning standards.

KC College is well-known in Mumbai. It's important to remember that a BA in Film, Television, and New Media Production is not the same as a BMM course. They cover different topics and areas of study. Make sure to look into both programs thoroughly before deciding which one to pursue.

Honestly, I think KC College is better for a BMM. They have a solid placement cell, and companies like Deloitte and KPMG come to hire students. The faculty is also very supportive, especially for those pursuing other courses like CA alongside. The annual fest, Kiran, is a great way to experience college life, and the library is well-stocked. Overall, my experience has been good, and I feel like I'll have better opportunities after graduation.

Congrats on scoring 88.60%. While it's a great score, you might find it tough to get into KC College for BMM right away. The first few cut-off lists are usually quite high, often between 92% and 94%, especially if you're in the general category without any special quotas. If you do have a quota, getting in should be much easier.

With your score, you'll face stiff competition, so it's wise to apply to other colleges as well, just in case. Over time, cut-offs tend to rise, but sometimes students switch colleges later on, which might open up a spot for you. Best of luck, and hope this helps!

I think KC College is good for BAF. The Bachelor of Commerce [B.Com] (Accounting and Finance) course is quite convenient as it allows you to manage studies alongside professional courses like CA. The faculty is qualified, and I found the exams to be manageable. However, I do feel the fee structure is a bit high compared to the amenities provided, and there weren't any campus placements offered for our batch. Overall, if you’re looking for a flexible course, KC might be a good option.

Hey there, I'm currently in my third year of BMS, and I have to say, Lala College stands out as a top choice compared to others. The faculty is great, the facilities are nice, and the student community is lively. Of course, preferences can vary from person to person. Lala College is pretty laid-back when it comes to attendance requirements. They mention a 75% rule, but it's mostly just on paper. The professors are supportive and don't bother students unnecessarily, unlike what I've heard about Jai Hind.

I think the beauty of the crowd in KC College mainly comes from the camaraderie and the involvement in various clubs and events like SCOPE and the sports day. In my B.Com program, we have a great mix of students who are all focused on their goals but still find time to socialize and participate in extracurricular activities. The friendly nature of both students and faculty creates a warm environment that feels like a community.

Definitely Mithibai! I went to junior college there before switching to NMIMS for my degree, and I really regret that choice. Sticking with a regular B Com at Mithibai would've been way less stressful for me. Mithibai is top-tier in Mumbai, and getting in is a real blessing. I wish I hadn't made the switch.

My time at Mithibai was amazing, probably the best years I’ve had. Even with large class sizes (over 120 students), the teachers make sure to address each student's questions. They don’t just talk the talk; their faculty is truly exceptional. Each subject has its own dedicated teacher who knows their stuff inside out. They don’t hop from subject to subject. Teachers go the extra mile during board exams by offering personal attention to students who seek it. You won’t find such committed teachers easily elsewhere.

The students here are from respectable backgrounds and have strong values. You might hear rumors about Mithibai students hanging out and doing things like smoking or drugs. I was told the same before joining after my SSC. But during my two years there, I realized those students outside are actually from NMIMS. So don’t buy into the gossip that ‘Mithibai students aren’t good’. Compared to other colleges, Mithibai has the most decent crowd.

Attendance is 75% mandatory, which isn't too demanding. You’re already paying the fees, so might as well enjoy the AC while you're at it. You can track your attendance with an app and plan your leaves accordingly. The Aditi canteen on the ground floor is fantastic with a variety of dishes. Some folks even choose Mithibai just for the canteen, which is a silly reason, but it happens.

You'll meet great friends here who will stick with you for life. No backstabbers around. Overall, Mithibai gets everything right: faculty, facilities, community, and more. If you’re gearing up for your 10th-grade board exams, check the cutoffs online for open category and maybe the Gujarati quota if you’re lucky to be Gujarati, and aim for those scores.

KC College in Thane is quite good, especially for the Bachelor of Commerce [B.Com] (Accounting and Finance) course. I found the curriculum convenient and manageable alongside my CA preparations. The faculty is qualified and supportive, and the exams are not too tough to pass. However, I did feel that the fee structure isn't justified considering the amenities promised. Overall, it has been a decent experience for me.

If you're looking for a top arts college in Chennai, especially for subjects like painting or sculpture, you might want to check out the Government College of Arts & Crafts. It's located on Poonamallee High Road, close to Egmore, right across from the Police Commissioner's office. This college has been around for a long time and offers a variety of fine arts programs. You can find more details on their website.

If you're interested in music and dance, Kalakshetra in Besant Nagar is another well-known place that offers courses in dance, music, and visual arts. Their website has all the information you need to know.

KC College Mumbai has been a good experience for me while pursuing my Bachelor of Commerce in Accounting and Finance. The curriculum is quite flexible, which is perfect for me since I’m also preparing for CA. The faculty is qualified, and while there are around 120 students in a class, I feel the teachers do their best to cater to everyone.

However, I wish the fee structure was more justified because sometimes the promised amenities like the sports room and AC aren't up to the mark. Plus, there aren’t any campus placements for my course, which is a bit disappointing. Overall, it’s manageable but has its drawbacks.

Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College, also known as ARSD Delhi, is a public college established in 1959. It is affiliated with Delhi University. The college is recognised by the UGC, and it is accredited by the NAAC with an ‘A++’ grade. It has been ranked 7th under the Overall Category in NIRF 2025.

Some of the other top courses include the B.Sc (Hons.), B.Sc, BA (Hons.), B.Com (Hons.), B.Com, BA, MA and M.Com. Admission to these courses is strictly based on the Entrance Exam, such as CUET UG and CUET PG
ARSD Delhi offers UG and PG admissions on the basis of CUET. The tables below show important dates regarding admissions at ARSD Delhi .
ARSD Delhi offers admission to major courses, including B.Sc, BA and B.Com.
Here are the course details, first-year fees, and the Total fees for all the major ARSD Delhi courses and fees.
Source: arsdcollege.ac.in
ARSD Delhi Courses and Fees FAQs
Ques. Should I choose ARSD Delhi over other DU colleges if I want low fees, decent faculty and balanced college life with academics and activities?

Ans. ARSD Delhi is a good option for students who want low fees with proper DU exposure. Faculty are mostly supportive, and classes happen regularly most time. College life is not a very extreme side, but societies, sports and many events keep happening. It is good for students who want to study along with campus activities without too much academic pressure.
Ques. Can I manage part-time work or internships while studying at ARSD Delhi, because I am worried about schedule, attendance and academic pressure?

Ans. Many students manage an internship during the semester in ARSD Delhi. The class schedule is mostly structured, but not a very hectic type. Attendance rules are there, but it is manageable if students plan properly. College environment supports skill building and internship culture, especially for commerce and arts students, but time management is very important, otherwise, classes can be missed.

ARSD Delhi's most popular courses include B.Sc. ARSD Delhi Admissions are done based on the CUET UG Entrance Exam, along with CSAS Counselling. The eligibility criteria are that students must have passed 10+2 in the Science stream.
Admission Process Steps
ARSD Delhi Admission FAQs
Ques. If I take a gap year after Class 12, can I still apply to ARSD Delhi admission in 2026, and will I face any issues during the counselling process?

Ans. Gap year students are allowed in ARSD Delhi admission if the CUET score is valid and the eligibility criteria is fullfilled. DU does not reject students just because of a gap year. During CSAS counselling document are checked properly, but the gap year affidavit is mostly accepted. Many students with a gap year also get a seat if the cutoff is clear and preference filling is done correctly.
Ques. If I get a lower preference college first, can I upgrade to ARSD Delhi later because I want better courses and college through CSAS rounds?

Ans. Upgradation option is available in DU CSAS counselling rounds. If a higher preference like ARSD Delhi is filled above and the cutoff is matched in the next round, then the seat can be upgraded. Old seats get cancelled automatically. Students need to be very careful while filling preference list. Cutoff changes every round, so patience and the correct order of choice matter a lot.
Admissions to BA, B.Com B.Sc, and MA courses through CUET are based on the ARSD Delhi cutoff each year.

ARSD Delhi cutoff data shows that commerce and arts courses have more demand, with B.Com (Hons.) and BA Political Science having the highest cutoff, while science and applied science courses have lower and more flexible cutoffs in different rounds.
The cutoff trend shows a gradual decrease across rounds, with MA English and MA Political Science having higher cutoffs, while M.Com recorded the lowest cutoff by the last round.
ARSD Delhi Cutoff FAQs
Ques. If I score slightly below last year's ARSD Delhi cutoff, do I still have a chance in later CSAS rounds or special rounds for science courses?

Ans. Yes chance in later rounds because the cutoff changes every round. Science and applied science courses usually drop more compared to commerce courses. Many seats remain vacant in later rounds,s so the cutoff becomes more flexible. Special rounds also help students who have borderline scores. Preference filling should be done correctly, and waiting till the last rounds is very important.
Ques. If I belong to the reserved category, how much cutoff relaxation can I expect for ARSD Delhi, and does it really help in top courses like B.Com or MA?

Ans. Reserved category students get cutoff relaxation as per the DU rule. This relaxation helps many students to get ARSD Delhi seats even in high demand course. Still, competition remains strong in B.Com and MA courses. The category cutoff also change round wise. A proper document and category certificate is compulsory, otherwise benefit is not given in counselling.

Some of the top recruiters during. ARSD Delhi placements included KPMG, Deloitte, EY, BDO Rise, and Coding Ninjas, among many others.
ARSD Delhi Placement FAQs
Ques. If I am not from a commerce background, will I still get placement help at ARSD Delhi, or do I need to depend fully on off-campus options?

Ans. Placement support in ARSD Delhi is available for all streams, not only for commerce students. Arts and science students also geta chance to sit in a placement drive, but the job role option may differ. Many students use the placement cell mainly for exposure, and later apply off-campus also. Skill building, internship and extra courses play a big role in the final placement result.
Ques. If I want a higher package from ARSD Delhi, what extra things should I focus on during college years apart from academics only?

Ans. Higher packages mostly depend on skill more than college name. Students who do an internship, certification, case competition and society work get a better chance. Placement cell invite company, but selection is student-based only. Communication skills, Excel, coding or analytics help a lot. Consistent effort from the first year improves placement outcomes.

ARSD Delhi consistently ranks among India’s top colleges, excelling in Commerce, Arts, and Science, as reflected in evaluations by reputed agencies like NIRF, INDIA TODAY and Collegedunia. The details for the ARSD Delhi Rankings are mentioned in the table below:
ARSD Delhi Ranking FAQs
Ques. If I see ARSD Delhi ranking improving every year, should I trust the ranking more or focus on course and department quality before choosing a college?

Ans. Ranking give overall idea, but it should not be the only factor. ARSD Delhi ranking is good because of academics, placement and faculty combined. But students should also check the specific department strength. Some courses perform better than others. Seniors' feedback, syllabus and opportunities matter more than just the number in the ranking list.
Ques. If I choose ARSD Delhi mainly because of NIRF ranking, will it really help me in future jobs or higher studies admission?

Ans. NIRF ranking helps in creating a good impression, but it does not guarantee a job or admission. ARSD Delhi name adds value on a resume, but student performance matters more. Companies and universities see skills, marks and experience. Ranking helps in shortlisting sometimes, but the final selection depends on the student's effort and profile.
