ARSD Delhi College Campus & Facilities FAQs
Ques. If I am staying far from campus, will daily travel to ARSD Delhi affect my classes, society work and overall college experience badly, or is it manageable?

Ans. Daily travel is common for many ARSD Delhi students because hostel seats are limited. Most students manage classes and society work by planning a timetable properly. Metro and bus connectivity is good, so travel becomes easier. Sometimes travel is tiring, but college life, events and friends make it manageable for most students.
Ques. If I am more interested in societies and extracurricular activities, will ARSD Delhi give me enough exposure, or should I look for other DU colleges?

Ans. ARSD Delhi has many active societies and clubs which organise events regularly. Students get chances to participate in cultural, academic and sports activities. Exposure depends on how active the student is. College supports society, but student effort matters more. With regular participation, ARSD Delhi give decent exposure and experience.

Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma (ARSD Delhi ) College is known for its strong academic reputation in Arts, Commerce and Science streams, along with consistent NIRF ranking and a balanced campus environment in Delhi University. Lady Shri Ram College is considered one of the best colleges for Arts, Psychology and Commerce, having a very good campus culture and a strong name as a top women’s college. Shri Ram College of Commerce (SRCC) is mostly known as India’s No.1 commerce college, famous for very high cutoffs and excellent placement records.
Here is a comparison between ARSD Delhi College, LSR Delhi, and SRCC on key parameters relevant for students.

ARSD Delhi College stand out as a strong Delhi University option for students who want good quality education at low fees with a balance of academics and campus life. With the CUET-based admission and CSAS counselling process, the admission system is quite clear and fair. ARSD Delhi offer many UG and PG courses with a decent NIRF ranking every year. Cutoff is high for commerce and arts, but science courses are easier to get into. Overall, ARSD Delhi is good for study, skill building, activities and future career growth.
Ques. Does ARSD Delhi allow students to change course or stream internally after the first year if interest change or their performance improves later?

Ans. ARSD Delhi normally do not allow easy internal course change after admission. DU rules for migration or course change are very strict. Some rare cases depend on vacancy and university permission. Students should choose courses carefully during CSAS preference filling. Depending only on later change is risky and mostly not possible in a practical situation.
Ques. Is attendance very strict at ARSD Delhi, and can low attendance create problems during the exam or internal assessment marking?

Ans. Attendance rules exist in ARSD Delhi, like other DU colleges. Some departments are strict while others are a little more flexible. Low attendance can create issues during internal marks or exam form filling. Students usually manage by attending regular classes and informing the teacher in genuine cases. Completely ignoring attendance can cause unnecessary academic problems.
Ques. Are research projects, field work or practical exposure given importance at ARSD Delhi or is the study mostly classroom-based only?

Ans. ARSD Delhi focus on classroom teaching, but project work and practical exposure also exist. Science students do lab work regularly, arts students get assignments and field work sometimes. Many teachers encourage seminar and research-based learning. Exposure depends a lot on the department and the teacher's interest, not the same for every course.
Ques. Do ARSD Delhi students get opportunities for exchange programs, workshops or DU-level academic events outside the regular syllabus?

Ans. ARSD Delhi students get chances to attend DU seminars, workshops and academic fest. The college also host conference and guest lectures sometimes. Exchange programs are limited, but workshop exposure is decent. Students who actively follow notice and teacher guidance get more opportunities. A passive student may miss such chances easily without active involvement.
Ques. Is ARSD Delhi considered good for students preparing for competitive exams like UPSC, NET or MBA along with graduation studies?

Ans. ARSD Delhi is suitable for students preparing for competitive exams because the schedule is not extremely hectic. Many student preparefor UPSC, NET or CAT along with classes. The library environment and peer support help a lot. However, self-discipline is very important. College supports indirectly, but the main preparation depends fully on the student's effort.

JB Institute of Technology (JBIT), Dehradun, established in 2009, has been approved by AICTE, PCI, and UBTER, and is affiliated with Uttarakhand Technical University. JBIT Dehradun’s B.Tech program is ranked 196th by The Week. Outlook ranked the college 103rd, and TOI ranked JBIT Dehradun 147th in 2025. It is accredited with an NAAC 'A' Grade.
Programs: JBIT offers UG, PG, and Diploma courses. The most popular programs are B.Tech, followed by BPharm.

Placement: According to research and student reviews, JBIT Dehradun has an 80–90% placement rate. The institute has top offers of INR 30 LPA, while the average package offered was INR 4.4 LPA. Top recruiters include companies like Tata Consultancy Services, IBM, and Tech Mahindra
JBIT admits students to the B.Tech program through JEE Main scores, while M.Tech admissions are offered based on GATE. The important entrance exam dates are listed below:
Admission to JBIT’s B.Tech program is conducted through JEE Main, followed by counselling. The tentative JEE Main 2026 schedule is as follows:
GATE exams are going to be held from February 7th, 2026, it will continue till February 15, 2026. The candidates can check the full schedule from the table below:

JB Institute of Technology (JBIT), Dehradun, offers a variety of programs at the UG, PG, and Diploma levels. The total academic fees for the B.Tech program at JBIT is INR 3.72 Lakhs, which includes tuition and other academic charges. The hostel fees are around INR 2.8 Lakhs. The total expenditure comes to about INR 6.52 Lakhs for the full program.
Given below are the JBIT courses & fees for the coming academic year:
Ques. Is the total cost of studying B.Tech at JBIT worth it compared to other private colleges?

Ans. Yes. JBIT’s total B. Tech expenditure is around INR 6.52 Lakhs, excluding hostel, which is relatively moderate compared to many private engineering colleges in Dehradun that charge between INR 7–12 Lakhs. ROI is better at JBIT Dehradun.
Ques. Does JBIT offer affordable options for students who don’t want to pursue engineering?

Ans. JBIT provides several non-engineering programs such as BCA, BBA, B.Sc (IT), B.Sc Agriculture, and Polytechnic, with 1st-year fees starting as low as INR 46,300. These programs have total fees between INR 1.39 Lakhs–2.57 Lakhs, making them budget-friendly choices for students.
JBIT Dehradun admissions are entrance-based and follow an online/offline process depending on the course.
The process generally includes:
Given below are the JBIT admission details:
Ques. How difficult is it to get a B.Tech seat at JBIT Dehradun, and does JEE Main rank matter a lot?

Ans. Admission to B.Tech at JBIT is moderately competitive. JEE Main scores are accepted, and many students also enter through Uttarakhand counselling (UKTU/AI Counselling) or institutional merit lists. A very high JEE rank is not mandatory.
Ques. Is direct admission possible at JBIT Dehradun for courses like BCA, BBA, and B.Sc (IT)?

Ans. Yes. JBIT offers direct admission for several non-technical programs like BCA, BBA, B.Sc (IT), and B.Sc Agriculture. No entrance exam is required for these courses unless the institute conducts a short screening or personal interview.
Ques. Does JBIT reserve a certain number of seats for Home candidates?

Ans. Admissions through UKTU/AI counselling often include reservation benefits for home-state-domiciled students, especially for B.Tech, Polytechnic, and other technical programs. These students may have slightly easier access to seats in state quota rounds.
JBIT rankings in 2025 improved slightly in TOI from 2024 (150 to 147 rank), and it remained stable in Outlook (103). The institute maintains a mid-tier national position.

JBIT Dehradun placement data, as per research and student reviews, indicates that the placement rate is 80–90%. The highest package offered is INR 30 LPA, while the average package ranged between INR 4.4 LPA and INR 8 LPA, depending on the program and specialization.
Top recruiters at JBIT Dehradun include TCS, Wipro, Infosys, Tech Mahindra, HCL, Cognizant, Amazon, L&T Infotech, Capgemini, BYJU’S, IBM, and Accenture, among others
The table below shows the number of scholarships that are available to students studying at JBIT Dehradun.

The comparison between JBIT Dehradun, DBS Global University, and DIT University shows that JBIT Dehradun offers the most affordable fee structure. In terms of placements, DIT University leads with the highest salary packages up to INR 58 LPA and an average of INR 7.5 LPA, followed by DBS Global with a highest package of INR 24 LPA and an average of INR 6.7 LPA. JBIT Dehradun offers a strong return on investment.
Ques. Which institute is better for high-placement potential between JBIT, DBS Global University and DIT University?

Ans. If placement package potential is the main factor, DIT University leads with the highest salary of INR 58 LPA and an average of INR 7.5 LPA, significantly higher than JBIT and DBS. JBIT offers decent placements with a highest of INR 30 LPA.
Ques. Between JBIT, DBS Global, and DIT University, which college is better for overall campus environment and academic diversity?

Ans. DBS Global University stands out with 121+ courses and strong corporate exposure. DIT University is better for tech-focused students who want rigorous academics and top-tier placements. JBIT offers a simpler, quieter campus environment with fewer courses, and the engineering & BPharm are at a very low cost.
JBIT Dehradun has a 25-acre campus in Dehradun, Uttarakhand.
JBIT Sports Facilities
JBIT Dehradun provides hostel accommodation for both boys and girls, with an annual fee ranging from INR 58,000 to INR 70,000, inclusive of food and laundry services.
Ques. Is JBIT Dehradun a value-for-money college compared to other private colleges in the region?

Ans. Many reviewers consider JBIT Dehradun a “value-for-money” institute. Given its low tuition and total fees compared to other private colleges, along with decent placement and internship opportunities, JBIT provides a good ROI for students.
Ques. How is campus life at JBIT Dehradun?

Ans. JBIT Dehradun campus life is vibrant, balancing academics and extracurricular activities. Students have access to indoor and outdoor sports facilities, a gymnasium, cultural events, workshops, and technical fests.
Ques. Is JBIT Dehradun affiliated and recognized?
Ans. JBIT Dehradun is a private institute approved by AICTE and affiliated with Uttarakhand Technical University (UKTU). You can check the details from the UGC website regarding the college's status.
Ques. How is the faculty and academic environment at JBIT Dehradun?

Ans. The faculty at JBIT Dehradun is qualified and supportive, guiding both theory and practical sessions. Classrooms and labs are well-equipped, especially for engineering and IT courses. If you are interested in research, you have to approach the professor with your proposal individually.

subject_lists.title: Rajdhani College Admission Process
subjects: Attempt CUET- Candidates need to attempt their respective CUET (Common University Entrance Test) for admissions into both UG and PG courses. For UG courses, candidates need 10+2 from a recognised board, and for PG courses, candidates need a Bachelor's degree from a recognised University.
DU CSAS Portal Registration- Once the Candidate qualifies the CUET exam, they have to register on the official DU CSAS Portal and choose the desired colleges with courses of their choice.
Check Cutoff- Once the forms are filled, candidates need to wait for the release Cutoff of their desired colleges.

Counselling Participation- Once the Cutoffs are released, the candidates need to participate in the Counselling session where seats are allotted to the candidates according to the CUET Score and preferences.

Payment of Fees- Once the Seat is allotted, the candidate needs to complete the Document Verification Process and finally pay the fees to block the seat in their desired College with their own choice of course.

Ques. What is NCC at Rajdhani College?

Ans. Rajdhani College has two well-established companies of more than 300 cadets, enrolled in the National Cadet Corps for both girls' and boys' wings. There are two companies viz, 7 Delhi Girls Battalion senior wing (7DGBN - SW) for girls cadets and 6 Delhi Battalion senior division (6DBN - SD) for boys cadets. CC is a three-year course at the graduate level, and successful completion of this course awards cadets with a certificate, which has specific incentives in different government job sectors. The National Cadet Corps organises training camps for students in rural and urban areas. As per policy, 50% of the enrolled strength is to take part in such Annual Camps. Loyola College Chennai is an autonomous institution founded in 1925. The institute has been awarded the status of “College of Excellence” by UGC and is accredited with an 'A++' grade by NAAC. It is affiliated with University of Madras. Loyola College Chennai is ranked 14th in the College category by NIRF 2025, and placed 5th in Commerce and 6th in Science by Collegedunia.

It offers popular B.Sc and M.Sc programs under a two-shift system. UG admissions are based on 10+2 marks, while PG admissions require a relevant bachelor’s degree followed by GD/PI. Loyola College fees are category-based: UG fees vary by board (HSC, CBSE/ISC, others), and PG fees differ for University of Madras graduates and students from other universities.
For Shift I, M.Sc (Madras University students) costs about INR 13,740-INR 15,150 for the 1st semester, while B.Sc (HSC board) costs INR 14,910-INR 21,040, depending on the specialisation.
Loyola College Chennai reported strong placement outcomes, with the highest package of INR 22.5 LPA and an average package of INR 6.34 LPA, according to the Placement Brochure 2024.

Loyola College admits undergraduates solely on a merit basis, while PG candidates must take an additional entrance exam consisting of GD and/or PI, administered by the university. The curriculum of the popular Data Science (M.Sc) program is well-rounded with intensive laboratory work, industry talks, and case studies. The other popular courses, such as BCA and BBA, have updated curriculum, aligned with the academics as well as industrial developments in the relevant fields.

The college also offers PhD in Economics, Commerce, History, English, Zoology, Physics and Chemistry. There are two active Diploma and PG Diploma programs as well, in the School of Film Studies and Management, respectively.

Loyola College Chennai conducts admissions for UG, PG, and doctoral programs through a fully online process, with the application portal typically opening after the release of Tamil Nadu 10+2 results for UG courses.

Admissions are primarily merit-based. UG candidates are shortlisted based on their Class 12 (10+2) marks, while PG admissions are based on graduation scores and may include entrance tests, group discussions and / or PI for select programs.

To apply, candidates must register on the official portal, choose their course, fill in personal and academic details, upload required documents, and pay the application fee. A unique application number is generated to track the admission status online.

Shortlisted candidates are offered provisional admission, which becomes final after document verification and payment of the admission fee. Applicants required to appear for entrance tests are notified separately after submitting their application.

Ques. Are mobile phones allowed inside Loyola College Chennai ?

Ans. No. Electronic gadgets such as mobile phone, ipad, ipod,smart watches are prohibited inside Loyola College campus. Students are also discouraged to travel around the camous in their personal vehicles. Any such vehicle, if used to commute by a student, is to be parked at the parking area inside the campus.
Ques. Is there any dress code / uniform at Loyola College Chennai ?

Ans. While Loyola College Chennai doesn’t require students to wear uniforms, they are needed to dress in a way that’s suitable to the academic environment of the college. Girls are required to wear decenly cut salwaar kameez while boys should sport formals. Neat and tidy appearance is also mandated by the college.
Ques. What are the attendance regulations at Loyola College Chennai?

Ans. Loyola College Chennai mandates an attendance of 75% in each subject in a semester to be eligible for the final examination. Barring special cases such as health issue related absence, absence of a differently abled student caused by any difficulty, no consideration is extented to any defaulter.
Ques. What are the shift timings at Loyola College?

Ans. Loyola College conducts classes in two shifts : Morning Shift (8:15 AM – 1:15 PM) for students working part time after college hours and Afternoon Shift (1:30 PM – 6:30 PM) for students capable of financing their education without any assistance from the college.
Ques. Is Loyola College co-ed?

Ans. Loyola College is a partially co - educational instituition. Some of its courses are co-ed, while others admit male candidates only. For instance, the UG courses at the department of Commerce admit only male students. However, the college has separate hostels for boys and girls to accomodate students belonging to both genders.
Ques. Does Loyola College provide scholarships to differently abled students?
Ans. Yes. Loyola College alumni base lends financial aid to differently abled students under the college’s Student Support Service program.

I'm currently a first-year B.A. (Economics) student at St Joseph’s University in Bangalore, previously known as St Joseph’s College. I've got some insights from my seniors who have graduated. In my opinion, Loyola College in Chennai is one of India's top Jesuit institutions. It's consistently ranked among the top 10 colleges in India by NIRF and offers a wide range of courses in Humanities, Science, and Management. It mainly caters to men, though some courses are open to women.

St Joseph’s University, also a Jesuit institution in Bangalore, has a strong reputation here. It's known for its rich legacy of over 120 years and a strong alumni network. As a co-ed college, it has a balanced mix of male and female students. The university is highly regarded for its Humanities, Science, and B.Voc programs, among other courses. While it may not be as famous outside Bangalore, it remains a prestigious institution in the city and across India.

When it comes to placements, both colleges provide good opportunities. Loyola College, Chennai tends to have a higher placement rate due to its nationwide recognition. St Joseph’s also offers solid placements, although slightly less compared to Loyola, but much depends on individual student performance.

To sum up, both institutions are well-respected Jesuit colleges in India with excellent faculty. Whether you choose Loyola or St Joseph’s, you'll receive not only academic excellence but also holistic development and character building. Both colleges have strong placement records and send their students to top companies.

Loyola College is quite well-known outside Tamil Nadu, especially in major cities like Mumbai and Delhi. Many people regard it as one of the top colleges in India. As a student of the Bachelor of Commerce (B.Com), I've experienced a lot of pride in my college's reputation.

The placement opportunities here are impressive, with companies like Deloitte and TCS recruiting students, which adds to its recognition beyond Tamil Nadu. The college has a strong alumni network that contributes positively to its reputation in other states.

It really comes down to your perspective. Loyola College offers a fair amount of freedom, but they do have a bit of an annoying rule against using camera phones. If you're aiming for courses like chartered accountancy, you might want to consider somewhere else, like Vivekananda, which offers better support for that field. The student community is great, and the faculty is pretty decent too. There are tons of opportunities for club activities and other Co curriculars if that's what you're into. The attendance policy is more relaxed compared to other colleges. Plus, having Loyola on your resume is a nice perk. Hope this helps!

Loyola College is known for its strict environment, particularly concerning academics. In my Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) course, we have a rigorous exam structure where attendance is closely monitored. You need to maintain a certain percentage to sit for exams, and they are pretty serious about ensuring students follow these rules.
It can be challenging, especially if you're juggling extracurriculars and studies, but it helps instill a sense of discipline.

I got 87% in the Tamil Nadu State Board exams and was really eager to study mathematics at Loyola College, even though my math score wasn't the best. I decided to apply for physics, mathematics, and chemistry, hoping to get into at least one of them. To my surprise, I got shortlisted for both physics and mathematics. I was over the moon and joined Loyola in 2016, and I stayed happy throughout my time there. Loyola isn't just a college; it's so much more.

I chose Loyola College for my Bachelor of Commerce (B.Com) degree mainly because of its reputation. Regular exams and internal assessments keep us engaged and motivated.

The campus life is vibrant, with plenty of clubs and activities, and the annual fest is a highlight of the year. I've also noticed good placement opportunities, which is a big plus for me as I prepare for my career ahead.

Some negative aspects of Loyola College Chennai, particularly in the Bachelor of Commerce [B.Com] program, include the outdated curriculum. The syllabus often lacks relevance to modern business practices, especially in areas like digital marketing and advanced accounting software. This can hinder students' preparedness for the job market, making it difficult for them to compete with peers from other institutions. Additionally, while the faculty is generally well-qualified, some professors may not effectively engage students, leading to a less interactive learning environment.

Another concern is the high fee structure for the Bachelor of Commerce [B.Com] program. While the college has a reputation for excellence, the financial burden can be significant for many students. Despite the availability of scholarships, the criteria can be stringent, and not all students benefit from them. This can create a financial strain, especially for those from lower-income families.

Lastly, campus life has its downsides too. While events like "Ovations" are engaging, some students feel that there could be more inclusivity in extracurricular activities. The pressure to participate in various clubs and events can sometimes feel overwhelming, detracting from the overall college experience. The infrastructure, although extensive, may not always meet students' expectations in terms of maintenance and facilities, which can affect their daily life on campus.

Ques. How is life at Women's Christian College (WCC)?

Ans. Women’s Christian College (WCC) in Chennai provides a vibrant academic environment, offering diverse undergraduate and postgraduate programs in arts, sciences, and commerce. The college is supported by a dedicated faculty that ensures quality education and mentorship. Campus life is enriched with active participation in cultural events, festivals, and various clubs and societies catering to academic, artistic, and social interests.
Ques. Is there a hostel facility at WCC?

Ans. Yes, WCC provides hostel facilities for students. The hostel fee is additional, and candidates need to pay INR 150 as hostel charges along with the application fee. Detailed information regarding the hostel accommodation, including facilities and rules, can be found on the official website.
Ques. How are students selected for admission at WCC?

Ans. Admission at WCC is based on a merit list that is prepared from Class 12 or equivalent marks (for undergraduate programs) and Bachelor’s degree marks (for postgraduate programs). The selection is done according to the category (e.g., Open, SC/ST, BC, MBC, etc.), and a counseling session is organized for document verification before confirming the admission.
Ques. What are the reservation policies at WCC?

Ans. WCC follows the Tamil Nadu Government’s reservation norms for admissions. There are reserved seats for categories like SC, ST, OBC, and MBC. Candidates belonging to these categories are given a 5% relaxation in the aggregate marks required for admission.
Ques. How does WCC support placement opportunities for students?

Ans. WCC has a dedicated placement cell that facilitates campus recruitment for students. Top recruiters include companies like Cognizant, Infosys, Zoho, Amazon, and Kotak Mahindra Bank. The placement process includes pre-placement training, internships, and career counseling to help students secure employment in their desired fields.

Ques. What facilities are present on the QMC campus?

Ans. Queen Mary's College offers students a variety of academic and support facilities. The college boasts fully equipped science labs, computer labs, and a central library containing thousands of books, journals, and research materials. Hostel blocks in the campus provide secure accommodation for students from remote locations. The college also sustains sports facilities, seminar and cultural event auditoriums, and canteens offering economic meals. Its seaside location provides not only natural scenery but also an open, refreshing atmosphere of learning that is not easily found in urban schools.
Ques. Does Queen Mary's College offer hostel accommodation?

Ans. Yes, hostel accommodation is available on campus, tailored specifically for women students. The hostels are situated within the college campus, with a secure and friendly living atmosphere. Rooms are equipped with minimal facilities, and dining halls serve wholesome meals. Recreational rooms and reading rooms within the hostels facilitate balancing study and leisure by students. Admission to the hostel is on merit, with preference for students from outside Chennai or far-off districts of Tamil Nadu.
Ques. What is the atmosphere at Queen Mary's College?

Ans. The atmosphere at QMC is a mix of academic achievement, cultural diversity, and historical heritage. As one of the earliest women's colleges in India, it continues to empower women by providing them with education and opportunities for leadership. The campus is serene and inspiring with the lush greenery, heritage buildings, and Marina Beach view. Besides academics, the college actively supports participation in cultural fests, NSS, NCC, and other student clubs to provide a holistic environment for development. The unique combination of tradition and modernity makes QMC a truly distinctive learning space.

Ques. How is campus life at SJCC?

Ans. The SJCC campus, although small and centrally placed on Brigade Road, is filled with student activity. It boasts of smart classrooms, seminar halls, finance labs, sports courts, an amphitheater, and a chapel. The college is famous for having energetic fests, student clubs, outreach activities, and entrepreneurship activities. Both in academics and co-curriculars, SJCC provides a complete development atmosphere to every student.
Ques. What is the process of internal assessments at SJCC?

Ans. Internal assessments at SJCC are ongoing and comprehensive. Every subject has two internal tests, assignments or projects, and class participation as part of it. Internals have a weightage of 30–40% depending upon the course structure, while the remaining marks are tested in end-semester exams. Test timetables are normally publicized prior to the test, and absence from a test necessitates a legitimate reason accompanied by permission from the HoD for retakes. Work is either individual or group work and is commonly in the form of presentations, case studies, or written reports. Internal marks are uploaded on the student portal, and continuous monitoring of performances gives assurance that students know their position in the semester.
Ques. What clubs and associations are there at SJCC?

Ans. SJCC has a rich mix of student clubs and associations that form the core of campus life. Ranging from academic clubs such as the Commerce Association, Entrepreneurs' Cell (E-Cell), and Finance Club to cultural squads like the Dramatics Club, Western and Indian Music Teams, and Fashion Team. There are interest-based clubs as well, such as the Literary Club, Quiz Club, Debating Society, and Photography Club. These are joined during the annual club orientation and are urged to actively participate throughout the year. Leadership positions in these clubs are much sought after, and students participate in inter-college events and national-level events under their name. Active participation in clubs also leads to internal evaluation and is awarded during convocation.

Ques. Is Mount Carmel College fully co-ed now?

St. Joseph’s University Bangalore's admission process is completely online and is conducted in three admission cycles starting from February till the end of June. Students who are interested in taking admission to the institution must apply on the official website of the university.

St. Joseph’s University Bangalore's Admission 2024 is ongoing under admission cycle 1 conducted from February to April. The deadline to apply for most undergraduate degree courses is in February and the applications for postgraduate courses are open till April.
The admission cycle 2 of St. Joseph’s University Bangalore is from April to May wherein the last date to apply for UG courses is April 10, 2024 and the deadline for PG courses is May 09, 2024.
This is the final phase of admission held from May to June. The deadline to apply for UG courses under this phase is May 09, 2024 and the applicants of PG courses can apply till June 08, 2024.

Note: The university conducts Ph.D. admission process in December for January intake consisting of an entrance test and an interview round. The final merit list will be available on the official website.
Some of the UG courses offered by St. Joseph’s University are B.Com, BBA, BA, B.Sc, BCA, B.Voc, and BSW. The PG courses available in the institute include M.Com, M.Sc, MA, MSW and MCA.

The application fee for St. Joseph’s University UG courses is INR 800. The registration fee for PG, PG Diploma and Ph.D. programmes at St. Joseph University is INR 1000. The university conducts an entrance called St. Joseph’s University Entrance Test (SJUET) for admission in different programmes. Students applying through an entrance test have to pay INR 200 extra in addition to the application fee prescribed. If a candidate wants to edit the application form, a fine of INR 50 will be charged.

The date and time of the entrance test will be published on the admit card and the entrance tests are scheduled three days after the last date to apply. For example, the last date to apply for MA English is April 10, 2024 then the entrance test will be held on April 13, 2024.
To apply for admission to undergraduate courses, the candidate must have cleared the Class XII examination and should have updated the scores obtained in the St. Joseph’s University application form.

SJUET will be conducted on campus for Indian applicants. The foreign candidates will be screened by associated schools or departments. However, the School of Communication and Media Studies will conduct an online entrance test for international students. Candidates can also apply for more than one programme. The university will make arrangements so that the student can attempt both entrance tests on the same day with a half-hour break.

My cousin completed his B.Tech from Nirma Institute of Technology who stayed in the community hostel named Saurashtra Kadva Patel Samaj situated in Gandhinagar. However, he had friends from various hostels, and here is his insight about the hostels.

Hiramani: This is the most liberal hostel for students in terms of rules and timings. You can return late at night and can indulge in typical hostelling activities like playing LAN games, watching movies on the laptop, etc, as long as you aren’t disturbing others. However, many students complain about the bad quality of mess food.

SGVP: It is a gurukul of Swaminarayan, thus making it quite religious and strict in terms of rules and decorum. Honestly, if you belong to a religion other than Hinduism then you might feel uncomfortable at times. However, the food quality is one of the best as they provide really healthy and tasty breakfast, lunch and dinner. The biggest drawback of this hostel is that there are no doors in the room hence no privacy at all.
Also, check out the following restrictions you have to face if you live in SGVP.

Saurashtra Kadva Patel Samaj: Here, my cousin chose to live for 2 years out of his B.Tech journey. The hostel was neat and clean and fees were just 20000 for a year, however, the food was just satisfactory.

Overall, it is highly recommended for freshers to join SGVP because of cleanliness, great food, and discipline. But, if you have budget constraints, the fees might seem high. Nevertheless, it is worth the fees.

Kristu Jayanti University has 11 hostels for girls and 7 for boys. The accommodations have been reviewed by students as peaceful and academically aligned. However, in terms of placement, the packages offered to its students are in the lower range compared to the industry standard. Despite having a dedicated placement cell and placement support programs in place, the university fails to attract the top placement offers.
Ques. How is student life at Kristu Jayanti University?

Ans. Since turning autonomous, Kristu Jayanti University has built a strict environment on campus that students compare with a prison. Students are required to maintain a certain percentage of attendance and abide by strict guidelines that have proven to be hectic. The campus, being of a moderate size, fails to provide the sense of vastness and freedom one expects from college life. In a nutshell, the university is best suited for candidates used to a restricted environment.

Vignan's Institute of Information Technology (VIIT) is a private institute established in 2002. The institute is affiliated with Jawaharlal Nehru Technological University, Kakinada, and has received approvals from AICTE, UGC, and NBA. VIIT Vishakhapatnam is ranked 201-300 in B.Tech by NIRF in 2024 out of 300 colleges in India.

VIIT offers a range of programs, including a B.Tech and M.Tech degree with eleven and eight specializations. Apart from that, the college also offers an MBA and an MCA degree course. A Thriving Campus Life: MIT is not just about academics; it's a vibrant hub of opportunities. You must join student clubs, including technical ones, to explore your passions beyond the classroom.
Sports Galore: If you're a sports enthusiast, you're in for a treat! MIT boasts semi-professional cricket and football teams, guaranteeing an adrenaline-packed experience and fierce competition.

Culinary Delights: When it comes to food, Manipal has you covered. With two fantastic Mexican restaurants and a variety of options, you'll rarely be disappointed by the gastronomic adventures you can embark on. Plus, the college mess is a cut above the rest, making sure you're well-fed and satisfied.

Balancing Recreation: It's true that Manipal is known for its lively social scene. While temptations are around, remember that your choices are what matter most. Find the right balance between academics and recreation to enjoy a fulfilling college experience.

Supportive Faculty: The professors at MIT, especially in Mechanical and Civil engineering, are both knowledgeable and approachable. While the education system may focus on achieving high marks, you'll have experts to guide you along the way.

Placements and Beyond While placements have their challenges, MIT provides you with the tools to shine in higher studies. It's an excellent choice if you aspire to continue your education and build a strong foundation for future success.

At ISB&M Pune, entrance exam score accounts for only 25% of the final selection decision. Academic performance, GD/PI performance, and work experience together determine the remaining 75%, making profile strength as important as percentile. The eligibility criteria for ISB&M Pune Admissions 2026 are outlined in the table below.
The table below covers the eligibility conditions applicable to the 2026-28 PGDM admissions cycle at ISB&M Pune.
Note: ISB&M follows a no-reservation-in-intake policy as a private institute. However, a 5% relaxation in minimum academic percentage is extended to reserved category candidates.
Step 1: Register and appear for at least one accepted national entrance exam - CAT, XAT, GMAT, CMAT, MAT, or ATMA - and obtain a valid scorecard.

Step 2: Apply online at is.inbm.ac - paying the application fee of INR 500 - INR 1,800 depending on the application deadline window. Payment is accepted via debit/credit card and net banking. The application fee is non-refundable.
Step 3: Await shortlisting - Candidates are evaluated on a combination of entrance exam percentile, past academic performance, work experience, and overall profile.
Step 4: Attend the GD and PI rounds - The selection weightage is: Written Test/Entrance Score 25%, Academic Performance 25%, GD and PI 40%, and Work Experience 10%.
Step 5: Receive the offer letter - Confirm your seat by paying the initial deposit of INR 1.1 Lakhs within the stipulated acceptance window.

Step 6: Submit all original documents - Class 10 and 12 mark sheets, graduation degree or provisional certificate, all semester mark sheets, entrance exam scorecard, and valid photo ID - at the time of program commencement.

Direct admission is not available at ISB&M Pune. All candidates are admitted exclusively on the basis of national-level entrance exam scores followed by the GD and PI process. There is no management quota or walk-in admission route. Candidates without a valid entrance exam score are ineligible to apply.

Ques. Is a work experience mandatory to apply for PGDM at ISB&M Pune?

Ans. No, work experience is not a mandatory eligibility criterion. Final-year graduation students and fresh graduates can apply. However, work experience carries a 10% weight in the selection process, so candidates with relevant experience do receive a slight advantage during GD/PI evaluation. Freshers are not disadvantaged if their entrance scores and academics are strong.
Ques. Does ISB&M Pune accept ATMA scores, and is it weighted the same as CAT or XAT?

Ans. ISB&M Pune accepts ATMA alongside CAT, XAT, CMAT, GMAT, and MAT. All accepted exam scores are considered valid for shortlisting. The selection committee evaluates the overall profile - entrance score, academics, GD/PI - so the specific exam used does not determine admission outcome provided the percentile meets the minimum cutoff threshold.
Ques. What is the CAT cutoff at ISB&M Pune for PGDM admissions?

Ans. The overall CAT cutoff for PGDM programs at ISB&M Pune for General Category applicants is 60 percentile. For MAT, the minimum cutoff is 80 percentile for General Category applicants. These are minimum shortlisting thresholds; final selection depends on the holistic evaluation including GD and PI.
Ques. Does ISB&M Pune offer dual specialization in PGDM, and does it cost more?

Ans. Yes, ISB&M Pune offers PGDM with dual specialization options, allowing students to combine two disciplines - for instance, Marketing and Finance, or HR and Business Analytics. The PGDM program at ISB&M is offered in dual specializations across the available streams. The fee structure is the same regardless of whether a student opts for a single or dual specialization combination within the standard PGDM program.
Ques. Can students from outside Maharashtra apply, and is there a domicile requirement?

Ans. ISB&M Pune is a private institution approved by AICTE and affiliated to Savitribai Phule Pune University. Admissions are conducted nationally through entrance exam scores and GD/PI, with no domicile restriction. Students from any state in India can apply and are assessed on the same merit criteria. Maharashtra domicile candidates may be eligible for state government scholarships through schemes like MahaDbt, which are not available to out-of-state students.

Ques. Is Jaipuria Institute of Management, Noida, good for an MBA/PGDM?

Ans. According to Reddit discussions, students and aspirants consider Jaipuria Institute of Management Noida a decent Tier-2 management institute with good campus facilities and acceptable placement opportunities. However, opinions on ROI are mixed, especially when compared with top-tier MBA colleges.
Ques. What do students say about placements at Jaipuria Institute of Management Noida?

Ans. Many Reddit users mention that average placements are generally considered decent for a Tier-2 B-school, with common opportunities in marketing, sales, BFSI, and operations roles. Some users estimate average packages around INR 7-8 LPA, while others feel ROI depends heavily on individual skills and performance.
Ques. Is the ROI at Jaipuria Institute of Management Noida, worth it?
Ans. Based on student opinions, the college offers decent exposure and placements, while others believe the fee-to-salary ratio may not be ideal compared to top MBA institutes.
Ques. What kind of student crowd joins Jaipuria Noida?

Ans. According to discussions, the student crowd is diverse, with students coming from different academic backgrounds and states. Campus life is considered active due to clubs, events, competitions, and the hostel.
Ques. Does Jaipuria Noida have strict attendance rules?
Ans. Yes, as per some Reddit users, the college has asked about attendance requirements and class timings, indicating that attendance policies are taken seriously in regular PGDM academics.
Ques. Is the brand/reputation of Jaipuria Noida worth it according to people about Jaipuria Institute of Management Noida?

Ans. In peer groups (e.g., CAT/CAT-prep forums), students often compare JIM Noida with similar MBA/PGDM options and many tend to choose Jaipuria because of its NCR location & brand perception, especially over lesser-known institutes, noting that it’s seen “as strong as some mid-tier private B-schools” even though ROI concerns exist.
Ques. Is Jaipuria Institute of Management Noida really considered a tier-2 B-school by students, or is that exaggerated?

Ans. Many peers on Reddit describe Jaipuria Noida as more of a tier-2/3 choice than a top-tier B-school, especially when weighing ROI vs competition from more recognized institutes. Some students even debated whether repeating CAT to aim for a “better college” makes more sense than joining JIM because of brand impact and long-term career value
Ques. Do real students feel the placements lived up to what Jaipuria claims?

Ans. Experiences vary: some Redditors and review-site commenters say placements are decent with students getting offers at reputed companies (e.g., Deloitte), especially if individual academics and interview prep are strong. But others counter that packages and ROI aren’t always as great as promoted (average vs highest figures) and caution that outcomes depend heavily on individual effort and domain choice.

Jaipuria Institute of Management has a one-of-a-kind ‘Uncampus’ which combines all four campuses- Lucknow, Noida, Jaipur, and Indore. This ensures common admissions, centralized placements, intra-campus faculty exchange, a uniform curriculum, and a vast and diverse alumni network.
During the 2023 placements at Jaipuria Institute of Management, 1000 offers were made to a batch of 930 students. Over 300+ recruiters, including 110+ new recruiters, participated in the placements.
The average package for the top 10% of students stood at INR 12.34 LPA. The average package for the top 20% of students stood at INR 11.08 LPA.

You will get into Jaipuria Institute of Management Lucknow even without giving any exam. Tier 4,5 institutions aren’t a good choice for pursuing your management studies.

The top 25 business schools have the right to claim that they provide the necessary management education and experience. You must aim to pursue your management studies from the top 25 business schools. By top 25, I mean the best 30-35 institutions
that can be grouped into the top 25.

I did some research on what management institutions you should join to have a successful career. According to me, do not choose Jaipuria Institute of Management Lucknow as your priority. If you wish to get a good start, score well in the CAT examination, and get 90+ percentile. You can then secure a seat in one of the best management institutes that will groom your personality and provide you with the necessary skills.
Yes, the Jaipurua Institute of Management is certainly a great choice for pursuing a PGDM as it's among the top B Schools in India. It has 4 campuses located in Noida, Jaipur, Indore, and Lucknow.
Considering the above points it can safely be concluded that Jaipuria Institute of Management is a great choice for PGDM.

The return on investment of the ROI depends more on the candidate's performance than the institute itself. The primary step should be to focus on achieving a high CAT score around 95+ percentile and apply to the top B Schools. If you fail to do so then you can consider the aforementioned B Schools.

Assuming the average package to be around 8 LPA, out of the entire batch around 20 students will secure a package of more than 8 LPA, in some cases maybe 12 or 14 LPA. Now compare these packages with the fees of around 9 Lakhs and also take into consideration other expenses, your investment will be around 12 lakhs. This is great for someone who received a package of 14 LPA, but for those who received low packages, the ROI is very less.
So, it depends on how well your profile, grades, and performance in the interview are!
I will try to cover all the major parameters to give you a detailed review of the MBA from Jaipuria Institute of Management

Academic: Jaipuria Institute of Management, Noida PGDM course is highly regarded and is coveted among MBA aspirants. The course is relevant to the recent trends in the industry. The institute offers premium quality education and industrial exposure to its students.

Faculty: The great academic environment is attributed to the highly learned faculty. Frequent guest lectures help provide exposure to the industrial interface. The professors here are very cooperative and guide you throughout. Their continuous evaluation method is effective in disciplining the students.

Clubs: The prime location of the institute attracts the best crowd. Numerous clubs and committees actively help in the holistic development of the students and harnessing their talents to the fullest.

Fees: Jaipuria Institute's Management fees are lesser than other B Schools. The Noida branch fee is ? 6,75,000/Yr; the Lucknow branch fee is ? 5,75,000/Yr; the Ghaziabad branch fee is ? 4,00,000 (Total Fees) and the Jaipur branch fee is ? 5,70,000/Yr.
Scholarship: The institute also provides scholarships based on merit up to 1 lakh rupees.

Placements: Jaipuria Institute of Management is known for its excellent placement scenario. Prior to the placements, the students are trained to perform well in the interview. The average package is in the range of 7-12 LPA.
Overall, Jaipuria Institute of Management is a great choice for MBA.
Honestly speaking, it’s highly illogical to compare a premiere B School like Jaipuria Institute of Management with a technical institute like GL Bajaj Institute of Management and Technology.
GL Bajaj on the other hand functions under the umbrella of Dr. Abdul Kalam Technical University (AKTU). This is more of a technical institute than a B School.

So both these institutes cannot be compared. If you are planning to pursue an MBA, then Jaipuria is the right choice but if you are planning to pursue Engineering only then is GL Bajaj a decent option.

The most important aspect is the overall grooming of the students, and thankfully they pay a lot of attention to that.

The biggest advantage or upper hand that you’d get at Jaipuria as compared to many other colleges is the corporate readiness, more chiseled and groomed personality, and better placement opportunities.

For students in CSE or ECE, placement opportunities are abundant, with nearly everyone getting placed.
Salaries range from 6 to 14 lakhs, depending on skills.
However, for branches like Mechanical, Civil, or EEE, placements are fewer, with about 40% securing jobs.
Non-circuit branches have fewer placements compared to circuit ones.
JNTUH is one of the top colleges in Telangana, aside from BITS and IIT Hyderabad.
The curriculum is well-structured, with schedules and exams planned in advance.
Some professors are very skilled, while others are average.
First-year syllabuses are completed on time, and some teachers offer extra sessions.
Students are encouraged to learn independently through resources like NPTEL and YouTube.
The first-year hostel has strict anti-ragging rules.
There's also an international hostel for students from countries like Nepal and Africa, offering 2 BHK flats shared among 2-3 students for ?6000 monthly, excluding food.
The campus has two libraries, including a digital one with fast internet and access to paid journals.
A new sports complex offers facilities like a gym and courts for various sports, with cricket tournaments held between branches.
Financial help from TEQUIP is available for research and projects, and students can attend free courses at IIT for 1-2 weeks.
Fees are quite affordable at ?10,000 for BTech and ?35,000 for IDP, with scholarships for economically weaker and meritorious students.
There is no dress code, allowing students to wear casuals and enjoy a lot of freedom.
Internship opportunities are mostly for CSE and IT students.
The syllabus doesn't always match industry needs.
There's no strong alumni network, and convocation is only for department toppers.
Career guidance is lacking, and there's no bus service for day scholars.
A minimum of 75% attendance is required.
The college could benefit from more advanced labs, better playgrounds, and more field trips and industrial visits for practical learning.
Additional facilities like a swimming pool and gym inside the sports complex would be beneficial.
The entire campus is equipped with Wi-Fi, which is fantastic for e-learning. If you use it wisely, it can be really beneficial.
The university, e-library, and college libraries have an extensive selection of books and e-magazines. They also offer resources for competitive exams, which is quite helpful.
There's a centralized computer center that's open all day, every day, which I found incredibly useful.
The labs get the job done.

Most placements are in the software sector. If you're looking to work in fields like civil, mechanical, chemical, metallurgy, or electronics, you might struggle to find a job in your area through campus placements.
There's no proper communication system like student emails. We live in a tech-savvy world, but beyond Wi-Fi, there isn't much innovation here. It feels quite outdated.

The campus rules are quite strict. If you're anywhere near the girls' hostel, the security guards will yell at you as if you're breaking some major rule. It's surprising to see such strict regulations in a leading institute.
I couldn't find an NPTEL local chapter or any push for smart learning. The internet mainly gets used for social media instead of educational purposes.
There aren't any art clubs, dance groups, literary events, or NCC activities. Mostly, it's just small disputes between different departments.

If you're looking for a solid B.Tech option in Hyderabad with a rank below 5k, Anurag University for Computer Science and Engineering is a good pick. The curriculum is well-structured and includes practical labs that help in gaining real-world skills. The college has decent internship opportunities, and many students get placed in top companies like Amazon and TCS with good packages. The hostel facilities are also quite good, and the campus environment is friendly and supportive.

JNTU College of Engineering has a pretty poor reputation. During the pandemic, while some universities showed understanding and flexibility with fees and exams, JNTU-H didn't seem to care much. Other places allowed students to pay fees in installments and gave more time to study for exams. But JNTU-H, named after Nehru, didn't really make any efforts like that.

Even before the pandemic, they didn’t consider any religious festivals, and last semester, many students who usually scored well ended up with surprisingly low marks because the grading wasn't done properly. Since September, their online classes have been rushed, like trying to squeeze a full semester into a short time. And for labs, they expect students to complete lab records without actually attending practical sessions. There are just a lot of issues to point out with this university.

I’m currently pursuing my Bachelor of Technology in Cyber Security at JNTU Hyderabad, and I find the curriculum to be quite relevant to current industry needs. The exams are structured well, with two midterms and a semester exam, allowing us enough time to prepare. The faculty is friendly and mostly helpful, although the teaching methods could improve to be more interactive.

For placements, students become eligible from the 6th semester, and the highest package has been 52 lakhs, so there are good opportunities if you work hard. The campus life is vibrant, with various clubs and activities, which makes studying here enjoyable.

I spent two years glued to my phone, one year playing cricket, and just a few days hitting the books. My four years were all about having fun. Staying in the hostel was a blast with my friends. We went on bike rides and trips, creating lots of happy and a few sad memories.

Being surrounded by a lively group of friends made time fly by. Semesters seemed to start quickly, but slowed down when exams and practicals came around. Studying wasn't a big focus; we’d have all-nighters before exams, with someone breaking down the entire syllabus overnight.
Festivals brought even more excitement. Teasing juniors and giving them a hard time was amusing. Finishing my B.Tech was bittersweet because I had to leave all of that behind.

I really miss those moments: the playful banter from Kulai and Ram, Yerra Sai's laid-back attitude during cricket, Akhil's intensity, Aman's kind words, Vamsi's bowling skills, Tejasai's powerful hits, Nikhil's wild antics, Ravi's random thoughts, Som's innocence, Dharma's big appetite, and my favorite thing, wicket keeping.
Studying engineering at JNTUH in Hyderabad has its ups and downs. The college offers a range of courses like BTech, a 5-year Integrated Dual Degree program, and IIDP.
I'm an alum of JNTU College of Engineering Hyderabad, and here's my honest take on the place.
As of February 2018, here are some positives I noticed:
Now, for some of the downsides: I chose this college because it's one of the best in the state, but a few things let me down.

Studying Computer Science and Engineering at JNTU Hyderabad has been quite a mixed bag for me. The curriculum is relevant to current industry needs, but sometimes I feel it's not as hands-on as it could be. The exams are conducted every semester, and they are moderately difficult.

I've heard from seniors that the placements are good, with many companies coming to hire students. The average package is about 4-5 LPA, which is decent for a government college. However, some faculty members could improve their teaching methods, and the overall student-faculty interaction could be better.

I would say that my experience at Jawaharlal Nehru Technological University Hyderabad (JNTUH) has been quite positive overall, especially in the Bachelor of Technology (B.Tech) in Computer Science and Engineering course. The curriculum is well-structured and focuses on practical applications.

We have exams every six months, which includes two mid-term exams and one final exam. The faculty is generally helpful, and I appreciate their approach to teaching, although some could improve their interaction with students. The fee structure is manageable for most, and I've been fortunate to receive a government scholarship that covers a significant portion of my tuition.
Campus life is vibrant with various events and clubs, making it a great place to grow both academically and socially.

Based on my personal experience and opinion, here's a list of some of the top engineering colleges in Hyderabad under JNTU that have great faculty and infrastructure. Starting with JNTUH, then OUCE, followed by CBIT, Vasavi, VNR, MVSR, MGIT, Srinidhi, GNITS, CVR, Gokaraju, KMIT, BVRIT, CMRCET, VJIT, and MREC.
I think applying for the usual revaluation in JNTUH is useless because mostly the difference in marks is 0. However, the challenge evaluation is worth the try.

I know many friends whose marks increased drastically after applying for challenge evaluation despite being the same after the normal revaluation. Unfortunately, this is how the scenario is here and you have no choice but to apply for it.

However, this process is very costly, around 10000 out of which 9000 can be redeemed if there is an increase in marks. So it’s advisable to go for a challenge evaluation especially if it's a question of promotion or an active backlog right before your placements.

SSN School Of Management (SSN SoM), Chennai was founded by Mr. Shiv Nadar, founder and chairman of HCL Enterprise, an $8.1billion global organization. SSN is part of the Shiv Nadar Foundation which has substantial interests in the field of education. The institute is accredited by NAAC with an ‘A++’ grade. The institute is autonomous under Anna University, Chennai.

SSN SoM Chennai offers one of the best known MBA programs in South India and is a preferred institution by MBA aspirants. The institute has a consistent and quality placement record of 92%. Students were placed in a variety of roles in IT, Banks & Financial Services and FMCG companies. The average CTC offered was INR 6.36 LPA. SSN recognizes that placement is the most important culmination in the two-year journey of students. SSN School of Management adopts a pro-active strategy to identify opportunities for students in reputed companies. The preparation for this is an integral part of the program and includes special on general awareness of industry and environment and a variety of training on communications, soft skills, group discussion, aptitude and facing interviews. The alumni of SSN also contribute to this effort through counseling and mock activities. Some of the placement highlights of SOM Chennai are as follows:

Computer Lab: The department has adequate computer laboratory facilities with the latest in Hardware and Software. The institution scrupulously follows the AICTE norms regarding computer resources to be made available to students.

Library: The institution has a well-stocked library with a wide range of management books as well as journals, both national and international. The collection is constantly reviewed and updated with new titles and editions.

Online access: The institution has subscribed to online access of over 1000 business journals and magazines through EBSCO. Students also have access to Capitaline database and case studies through the European Case Clearing House.

SSN SOM Chennai has more than 22 well-qualified and experienced faculty members (including adjunct faculty). The institute has an esteemed group of professors, practice professors, and adjunct faculty. Most of the faculty members at the School of Management are Ph.D. holders and have rich experience in teaching/ research/ consulting. Teaching methods include case studies, field studies, seminars, simulations, career-centric projects, experiential learning assignments, and independent work. The Adjunct faculty from the industry handles one-third of the courses on a full-time basis reflecting a strong blend of the industry-academic interface. A unique culture of SSN is the easy accessibility of faculty members to facilitate a great learning experience for students.

Ques. Does the institute provide scholarships?

Ans. Yes, SSN School of Management is part of overall initiative of the scholarship program of SSN Institutions. Six scholarships are awarded every year. Following are the scholarships provided by SOM Chennai:

Scholarships are awarded only after joining the program and not at the time of the grant of admission. First-year scholarships are awarded based on past academic records, admission test scores and GD/PI performance. The second-year scholarships are awarded based on first-year performance in the MBA program.
Check: SSN SOM Chennai Scholarship
Ques. How are admissions done under Management and Government Quota?
Ans. Government Quota

Admissions to the Government Quota are handled by the Directorate of Technical Education, Government of Tamil Nadu. Candidates seeking admission under the Government Quota must have written the TANCET exam (Tamil Nadu Common Entrance Test) conducted by the Anna University. The single-window counseling normally takes place in the months of July/ August every year at the Government College of Technology, Coimbatore. Seats for the MBA program at SSN normally get filled up on the first day of counseling much ahead of its peer institutions.

Admissions under the Management Quota to SSN School of Management are made purely on merit. Candidates seeking MBA admissions under the Management Quota must have written one of the entrance tests - CAT, XAT, CMAT, ATMA, MAT or TANCET. The selection process is based on the scores in the entrance test as well as past academic record and performance at the Group Discussion and Personal Interview organized by the institution.

CMR Engineering College is one of the top 10 Engineering colleges of Hyderabad and an UGC Autonomous institution which was established in 2010. It is approved by AICTE, affiliated to JNTU, Hyderabad, and has been accredited by NIRF and NBA. CMREC is ranked with an ‘A’ grade by NAAC and is also rated 5-star under Institution Innovation Council, Ministry of Education, Govt of India & Achieved ARIIA Ranking. The college has also received 80+ awards including “Best Education and Development Award” by Central Institute of Tool Design, “Best Students Chapter Award” by ISTE and “Best Student Forum Award” by Institute of Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering. CMR Engineering College is also ranked at the 22nd position under “Top Emerging Private Engineering Colleges” Category in India and 20th among the “Top Private Engineering Colleges” category in Telangana by The Week.

CMR College of Engineering offers 7 Undergraduate courses, 2 Postgraduate courses, and 2 PhD courses in the discipline of Engineering with a total intake capacity of 1224 students for B.Tech and M.Tech combined. Admission to UG courses is granted based on score obtained by aspirants in last year’s qualifying exam and TS EAMCET while a valid score in TS PGECET is required for admission in PG courses.

The college has a strong base of 6000+ Alumni Network, 300+ companies for placement, 6500+ students have been placed till date, 7000+ have received internships, and the highest package reported is INR 44 LPA. During 2024 placements, the highest and median packages stood at INR 15 LPA and INR 5.5 LPA respectively.

CMREC has also signed MOUs with major leading enterprises like Cambridge for Business English Certification, DELLEMC for Big Data, Ui Path for RPA, Oracle for AI & Machine Learning in Java, epam for Pre-education program, CISCO for Networking and CS, AWS educate for Cloud Development, CYIENT for Software Development, ZenSar for employability and skill development of students while DIGITAL CONNECT is its Digital Marketing Partner, Internshala is Internship Partner, paloalto is Cyber Security Partner.

CMR Engineering College also has professional memeberships with The Institution of Engineers, Institutions of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, Indian Society for Technical Education, Institution of Electronics and Telecommunication, Computer Society of India, and the Society of Automotive Engineers India.

The CMR Engineering College is situated in a vast area of 10 acres of land and is surrounded by lush greenery. Also the college has established modern infrastructure including artistically designed buildings, Wi-Fi enabled campus, aeriform classrooms and labs to strengthen technological skills of students and libraries to assist students and faculties academically. Apart from this, campus is vibrant enough to help students prosper personally and professionally as several co-curricular events and activities, social, cultural and recreational learning windows along with sports events are held on a regular basis in collaboration with various Associations, Clubs, Societies, Professional Bodies and Students Chapter to ensure all around development of students, inculcate creative skills in them and keep them physically and mentally fit. Also the things which makes CMREC unique and different from others are its dynamic community of supportive peers, caring and mentoring professors, and friendly staff.

Auditorium: The CMR Engineering College has an amazingly developed Auditorium with a seating capacity of 500 people to organize national level symposiums, college functions and other gala and cultural fests and dynamic sound system is installed here.

Sports & Games: The CMR Engineering College has spacious and well equipped grounds to conduct various Indoor like Table Tennis, Chess and Caroms and Outdoor sports and games like Football, Cricket, Hockey, Basketball, Volleyball, Cycling and Running during and after college hours. In addition to this, college has a Sports Council to organize annual sport meets, events, sports competitions and Inter-collegiate tournaments.

Gymnasium: The CMREC has a well-resourced Gym having machines like treadmill, stretching machines, suspension trainer, stationary bike, abdominal bench, cross trainer and various weight training equipment to keep students physically fit.

Canteen: An aesthetically developed canteen is also there in college to serve a wide variety of lunch, break-fast eateries and snacks. Along with this, North and South Indian and Chinese foods along with veg and non-veg foods are served by canteen staff with utmost hygiene.

Labs and ICT Facilities: CMR Engineering College uses a diverse set of ICT tools to communicate, creates, disseminate, store and manage information. And each lab is well-equipped with LCD Projector, Computers, Wi-Fi Facility, Audio and Camera facilities.

Seminar Halls: College has a well –resources and air-conditioned Seminar hall with a seating capacity of 240 students in every department to help crucial workshops and seminars using Multimedia projectors and Audio Video amenities.
Transport Facility: The College has 46 buses to pick and drop students and staff members from Hyderabad and Secunderabad region.

Library: CMR Engineering College has also established a voluminous and expensive multistoried Central Library with a seating capacity of 200 people to fulfill the academic requirements of students, faculties and also to nurture an uninterrupted learning ambiance for everyone. This athenaeum is a home of 13050 Volumes, 1966 Titles, 1256 CDs, 923 Journals, various Text Books, Reference Books, 100 e-Books, Magazines, e-Journals, Subject PPT’s, Subject Animations, 500 Project Reports, Tutorials, 100 Subjects NPTEL Text, 300 Subjects MIT Open-Courseware, 1500 Software Video-Tutorials, 471 Course Materials, 3055 Question Papers, 104 STEP Material, 2500 companies’ information and 68 staff published Articles followed by 11000 NPTEL Video Lessons.

First Floor of Library: Reference Section, Periodicals Section, Digital Library, Discussion Room

Facilities for Divyangjan: CMREC provides physical facilities like wheelchairs, Stretchers and hand sticks along with a lift facility to especially abled persons. And Braille Software is also there to assist visually challenged students, rest rooms and scribes to help Divyang students during exams and guest lectures to keep them motivated.

Students Activity Clubs: The CMR college has various AICTE Sponsored clubs including AI Club, Cultural Club to organize events like Traditional day, Fresher’s day, Annual day, Alumni meet, Teachers Day, Women’s Day celebration and Farwell Day, Event Management Club, Robotics Club, Social Media Club, Ideation Club, Sports and Fitness Club, Photography Club, Younify Rdaio Club, Smart Vision Club, Aakriti Club to organize Massive Bucket Immersion, Recycling and Eco-Film Festival like events, Coding Club, NDLI Club, HEV-Club, Vaidyukta Club, Embetronics Club, NGCN Club, Block Chain Club, Champ Maths Club, Aakriti-Nature Club and CREST English Club to improve reading, writing and thinking competencies of students.

The college also provides new-age courses like Data Science and AI & ML. These programs are designed to provide both academic and practical knowledge.

Ques. Does RBVRR Women’s College require an entrance exam?

Ans. Most UG courses do not require any entrance exam and are offered based on merit. However, MBA admission requires TS ICET, and some M.Sc programs may consider OUCET. The process is straightforward and transparent. Selection lists are published online.
Ques. What is the placement package at RBVRR Women’s College?

Ans. The highest package offered is around INR 8.2 LPA, while the average package is approximately INR 1.4 LPA. Students are placed in companies like Accenture, Wipro, and Cognizant. The college provides training and placement support. Opportunities are mainly in the IT and service sectors.
Ques. Does RBVRR Women’s College provide scholarships?

Ans. Yes, RBVRR offers multiple scholarships for deserving students. These include government scholarships for SC/ST, OBC, and minority students. Institutional support, like the Poor Aid Fund and the Needy Student Grant, is also available. The aim is to make education accessible for all.

Ques: Is CMAT compulsory for MBA at JIMS Rohini?

Ans: No, CMAT is not compulsory for admission to the MBA programme at JIMS Rohini. You can also apply with a valid score from CAT, XAT, MAT, or GMAT. Along with any one of these entrance exams, you must meet the basic eligibility rules like having a graduation degree with at least 50%.
Ques. My extra-curricular achievements are not outstanding. Do I get a chance?

Ans. Extra-curricular and personal achievements are not considered during initial shortlisting for PI. But these will be considered by the overall merit preparation and it carries 5% weightage in final merit preparation.
Ques. Will my request for rescheduling of the PI slot be entertained?

Ans. NO, Requests for rescheduling of PI will not be entertained in any case. Based on the scores of the qualifying exam, candidates will be called for Group Discussion & Personal Interview which will be conducted offline in the JIMS Campus, 3, Institutional Area, Sector-5, Rohini, Delhi-110085 (Near Rithala Metro Station), on April 15, 2026.
Ques: What is the eligibility criteria for admission to BCA at JIMS Rohini?

Ans: For admission to the BCA course at JIMS Rohini, candidates must meet the basic eligibility criteria set by the institute. Students can apply if Students have passed Class 12 with at least 50% aggregate marks along with English and Mathematics (or Computer Science/Informatics Practice) as compulsory subjects. Alternatively, candidates who have completed a three-year Diploma in any branch of Engineering from a recognized Polytechnic with minimum 50% aggregate marks are also eligible to apply. Admissions to the BCA program are done through the IPU admission process. The vacant seats after exhausting the merit list of CET will be filled through the merit list of CUET.
Ques: How to get admission to BBA course offered at JIMS Rohini?

Ans: To get admission in the three-year BBA course at JIMS Rohini, candidates need to follow a simple three-step process. First, you must have passed Class 12 with at least 50% aggregate marks and English as one of the main subjects. Second, you need to appear for and qualify the IPU CET entrance exam conducted by GGSIPU. Finally, based on your IPU CET score, you have to participate in the GGSIPU counselling process for seat allotment. Only candidates who complete all three steps successfully get admission. The vacant seats after exhausting the merit list of CET will be filled through the merit list of CUET.

So, candidates preparing for the next academic session must aim to secure more than 75 percentile to secure a seat at JIMS Rohini.

Ques. What is the admission process for JIMS Rohini?

Ans. Admission Procedure for JIMS Rohini varies from course to course. Ans. JIMS Rohini PGDM IB is a 2-year full-time PGDM program in International Business. The program is a window to global career-building opportunities mainly in the field of Export-Import, Foreign trade, Logistics management, Foreign Exchange Departments of banks, and many more.

Ans: JIMS Rohini offers PGDM (General) course, which is equivalent to MBA across five specialisations. Apart from this, candidates can also apply for admission to PGDM (International Business) and PGDM (Retail Management) courses. These courses are also offered across further specialisations.

Ans: CAT qualified students get a scholarship of INR 50,000 only if they meet the criteria. Students must secure 80 percentile in CAT and a minimum of 70% aggregate in Class 10, Class 12 and graduation. A partial fee waiver is applicable on second, third and fourth installments.

Budhha Institute of Technology, popularly known as BIT Gorakhpur, established in 2009, is a private AKTU-affiliated engineering and management institute. With AICTE approval, this college has been ranked 627th among other engineering colleges in India by Collegedunia in 2025.

BIT Gorakhpur offers UG and PG programs like B.Tech, M.Tech, B.Tech (Lateral), and Diploma. B.Tech, being the flagship course, is available in the following disciplines: CSE, AI & Machine Learning, Data Science, IT, Computer Science, ECE, Civil Engineering, and Mechanical Engineering. Both direct and entrance-based admissions are conducted. Admission to B.Tech programs is based on performance in the JEE Main. Seats are allocated based on UPTAC counselling rounds. The average fee for B.Tech 1st year is INR 61,200.

BIT Gorakhpur placement records for 2025 are yet to be released. But according to the latest students’ reviews, the highest package secured varies from INR 11.5 LPA to INR 11.23 LPA by B.Tech departments. A total of 70% of students have been placed across all the UG & PG departments. It includes some of the top companies like TCS, Wipro, HCL, and Cognizant.

BIT Gorakhpur offers 22 UG and PG courses in Engineering. Popular specializations of B.Tech are CSE, ECE, Civil Engineering, IT, and Mechanical Engineering. M.Tech, and diploma programs are also available for students. The average fee for the 1st year B.Tech program is INR 61,200, whereas the cost for the 1st year M.Tech Program is INR 64,000. Refer to the following table for BIT Gorakhpur Courses & Fees.

BIT Gorakhpur admissions for UG and PG programs are based on the performance in the entrance exams. B.Tech and M.Tech admissions are conducted based on the JEE Main/GATE Score. Further, through UPTAC counseling, seat allocations are done. Admissions are conducted in both online and offline modes. Students can refer to the table below for the admission procedure.

IIEBM Pune campus is built with the corporate world in mind.

Its classrooms are well equipped with white boards and comfortable seating arrangements. They are well illuminated through large glass windows. Each classroom has a notice board for important announcements.

The library displays a rich collection of books, e-books, journals, e-journals, magazines and databases. Its online portal is always accessible from students' systems from anywhere. The library database is completely digitized with multi-user integrated library management.

IIEBM auditorium is a prized possession of the institute. It is equipped with a futuristic projection system, accompanied by Dolby Atmos Audio Technology. The plush hall is capable of seating 500 people at a time. Corporate events, cultural programs, workshops are held in this auditorium.
Take a tour inside IIEBM Pune
Its cafeteria has a capacity of 400. It’s a multi cuisine establishment maintained hygienically. A FSSAI approved catering company is employed as the food provider of the cafeteria.

The campus comprises two boys' and three girls' Wi-fi enabled hostels, both under 24/7 CCTV surveillance. Resident wardens as well as security guards are employed to ensure safety of students inside the hostels as well as the campus. Each hostel has its own common room with TV and other recreational facilities.
The hostel rooms are quite spacious and equipped with separate study tables, cabinets, and lights for each student.
The corridors outside the hostel rooms are long and clean. The hostels have fire exits installed.
The campus has a luxurious lounge for students and staff to catch their breaks in between classes.
Apart from these, IIEBM Pune campus has a wellness centre for students and staff, providing them the scope to unwind with various indoor sports. It also has a meditation centre.

Ans. Yes. IIEBM Pune offers international placement opportunities. Students with very strong academic records are considered for such positions. These opportunities may vary from one academic year to another, depending upon availability.

Ans. Yes. IIEBM Pune runs a Career Development Program. It consists of alumni and corporate mentoring, club participation and hands-on projects to expose students to the practical approach of management as well as financial studies.
Ques. Does IIEBM Pune support entrepreneurship?
Ans. IIEBM Pune arranges for students to take part in consulting projects. They are assigned live clients and mentioned regarding building and running start-ups.
Ques. Does IIEBM Pune follow a strict regime of teaching?

Ans. The rules and regulations at IIEBM Pune are quite strict. Maintaining a 90% attendance percentage is mandatory. The areas the institute focuses on are punctuality, grooming and code of conduct, the very aspects a corporate professional is judged by.
