I would say that my experience at Jawaharlal Nehru Technological University Hyderabad (JNTUH) has been quite positive overall, especially in the Bachelor of Technology (B.Tech) in Computer Science and Engineering course. The curriculum is well-structured and focuses on practical applications.

We have exams every six months, which includes two mid-term exams and one final exam. The faculty is generally helpful, and I appreciate their approach to teaching, although some could improve their interaction with students. The fee structure is manageable for most, and I've been fortunate to receive a government scholarship that covers a significant portion of my tuition.
Campus life is vibrant with various events and clubs, making it a great place to grow both academically and socially.

Vignan's Institute of Information Technology (VIIT) is a private institute established in 2002. VIIT offers undergraduate, postgraduate, and diploma courses in Engineering and Technology across various specializations. The institute is affiliated with Jawaharlal Nehru Technological University, Kakinada, and has received approvals from AICTE, UGC, and NBA. VIIT Vishakhapatnam is ranked 201-300 in B.Tech by NIRF in 2024 out of 300 colleges in India.

VIIT offers a range of programs, including a B.Tech and M.Tech degree with eleven and eight specializations. Apart from that, the college also offers an MBA and an MCA degree course. Candidates can seek admission to B.Tech and M.Tech after appearing in the EAMCET and PGECET entrance exams, respectively. For MBA and MCA, admissions will be conducted through the Integrated Common Entrance Test (ICET). VIIT's flagship course is B.Tech, with a first-year fee of INR 68,700. The overall BTech cutoff rank for general category students in AP-EAPCET ranges from 12768 to 90808.

Vignan's Institute of Information Technology has not yet released its placement report for 2025. Additionally, 109 students have been selected for higher studies at the postgraduate level. The college campus is well equipped with well-maintained facilities.

Sushant School of Art and Architecture was established in 1989 and is considered one of the best Architecture Colleges all over India. It is ranked 11th for Architecture by India Today 2020. SSAA has been ranked as Number 1 Private Architecture School by The Outlook in 2017, it has also been awarded as the Best University of Architecture Studies by Assocham National Education Excellence Award 2017.

The most popular program offered at Sushant School of Art and Architecture is Bachelor of Architecture (B.Arch). The duration of this course is 5 years. The selection is given on the basis of either the 12th Boards score + NATA scores (50:50 Ratio) or the 12th Boards score + JEE Paper 2 (60:40). The other courses offered at the college are M.Arch, BFA, and Ph.D. Admission to these courses is done through document verification, entrance examination, and personal interaction.

Panipat Institute of Engineering and Technology (PIET) is a private institute established in 2006. The institute is affiliated with Kurukshetra University. Approved by the AICTE and UGC. PIET is also accredited by NAAC with an ‘A+’ grade and holds NBA accreditation.

According to the PIET Panipat 2025 placement report, it has achieved a placement rate of around 75%. The highest package offered was INR 38 LPA, while the average package is INR 5 LPA. Top recruiters included Google, Amazon, Infosys, Wipro, HCL, IBM, TCS, Capgemini, and Deloitte.
More info on the placement can be found here.

PIET Panipat accepts JEE Mains scores for admission to the B.Tech program. The exam dates for JEE Main have been released. Candidates can check the tentative schedule of both the exams tabulated below:

PIET Haryana offers UG, PG, and Diploma programs. The total fees for the B.Tech program are approximately INR 10.2 Lakhs. The table below provides details of PIET Haryana courses & fees, for the academic year 2025–26:
PIET Panipat Admission 2026 is currently open. Admission to the MBA program is based on CMAT/ MAT test scores and PIET personal interview.

The second popular course is B.Tech Information Technology (IT), with a closing rank of 847809 in Round 1.
Given below are the details of the PIET Panipat JEE Main 2025 cutoff:

PIET Haryana has demonstrated strong placement performance with a placement rate of around 75%. The highest package offered was INR 38 LPA (by Google), while the average package is around INR 5 LPA. The highest International package secured by student is INR 1.4 Cr. PIET Panipat placement report says 240+ reputed recruiters participated in the 2025 placement drive, including Google, Amazon, Infosys, Wipro, HCL, IBM, TCS, Capgemini, and Deloitte.
The table below shows the number of scholarships that are available to students studying at PIET Panipat

Comparing the three colleges, SAITM, PIET Panipat, and Geeta Engineering College Panipat, the total fee structure for a 4-year duration is INR 4.2 lakh for SAITM, INR 7.2 lakh for PIET Panipat, and INR 3.33 lakh for Geeta Engineering College. Although PIET has the highest fees of INR 7.2 lakh, it has better placement and industry exposure. The highest package at PIET is INR 30 LPA. Despite having the highest fee, only a few packages of SAITM were INR 40 LPA for students. Geeta Engineering College does not offer as many placement options for students, with a maximum of an INR 12 LPA package. Therefore, even though PIET Panipat is more expensive than the others, it is an all-around better option.

PIET Panipat has a modern and thoughtfully laid out campus to support academics and extracurricular activities. There are air-conditioned classrooms, modern computer labs, research labs, and a library with adequate resources. There are separate hostels for boys and girls with furnished rooms and dining facilities. The campus has medical facilities; transportation services are available for those students commuting from the city. There are also banks, ATMs, and other necessary services within the reach of the campus in Panipat.
PIET Academic Building
PIET Sports Facilities

According to Harish Kumar's review on Collegedunia, PIET Panipat provides a great ambiance on the campus, including a huge, adequately equipped infrastructure, and several recent features. The college focuses on AI, analytics, robotics, and other learning developments. The course curriculum covers many relevant areas, and the projects and internships begin from the later semesters. The placement cell is also proactive, and pre-placement training and internship support are given; the average package is INR 4–5 LPA. The hostels are secure and friendly. The campus life is well-equipped, energetic, featuring sports facilities, parks, and technology equipment incorporated into the classrooms, vending machines, and bookstores. Harish points out the scholarship opportunities for the merit and reserved-category students. The faculty assists and supports students.

This video shows the PIET Panipat Campus Tour, showcasing the institute’s modern infrastructure, spacious classrooms, and well-equipped laboratories. It highlights the hostel facilities, cafeteria, and sports complex, giving viewers a glimpse of student life on campus. The video also covers the library, innovation and startup corners, and the vibrant cultural and technical activities that make PIET a lively and engaging place to study.
Ques. What are the fees for the hostel at PIET Panipat?

Ans. PIET has secured separate, fully furnished boys' and girls' hostels with round-the-clock security and Wi-Fi facilities. The hostel offers comfortable accommodations, a hygienic dining facility, recreational amenities, and communal areas. The dormitories are clean, conducive to studying, and friendly to student life, with regular cleaning and supervision from the wardens.
Ques. Are there any sports and fitness facilities provided at PIET Panipat?

Ans. PIET has a variety of sports and fitness facilities, including cricket, football, volleyball, basketball, and badminton courts, as well as a center for fitness workouts in a gymnasium with modern equipment, and has open large spaces for outdoor sports. Our philosophy is about lifelong physical fitness, sportsmanship, and teamwork. Students are also provided with opportunities to compete in intercollegiate tournaments and in the annual sports meet organized by the college.
Ques. Does PIET Panipat have any support for students for research and innovation, and or any entrepreneurial activity?

Ans. Yes, the college supports research, innovation, and entrepreneurship for students at PIET by providing labs and research Cells, and support for incubation of start-ups. The Innovation and Start-up Corner provides support for the project, patent application, and training to work collaboratively with product development industry experts in research and innovation.
Ques. How are the students and the student culture at PIET Panipat?

Ans. The student culture at PIET is inclusive, vibrant, and career-oriented. Students actively engage in the many technical, cultural, and social activities, which help to develop leadership & teamwork skills among the students. To ensure a good work-life balance, the Institute frequently hosts festivals, seminars, industrial visits, and similar events.

MDI Gurgaon campus is spread across 35 acres of land. The classrooms of MDI Gurgaon are well-equipped with all the modern facilities. The campus at MDI Gurgaon comprises hostels, IT infrastructure, a library, and other facilities. MDI Gurgaon campus is situated near the Indira Gandhi International Airport. The airport is just 12 km away from the campus.

Hostels - MDI Gurgaon provides accommodation to its students on a twin-sharing basis in Chaitanya, Change Masters, and Takshashila hostels. It also has a hostel named Kshitij, where rooms are available on a twin-sharing / four-sharing basis. There are separate hostel blocks for the girl students known as Oddessy (Twin-sharing) and Kaveri (twin / triple-sharing). Hostel rooms are provided with a bed, a study table, a chair, a cupboard, and the usual fixtures. The rooms of these hostels are air-conditioned and fully furnished.

Library - MDI Gurgaon Library holds a rich collection of printed and electronic resources such as Books, Journals, Databases, Audio-Visual Materials, CDs/DVDs, E-Journals, Reports, Case Studies, Training Manuals, etc. The Library has a collection of over 55,000 books and around 2.3 lakh E-Books. It also provides access to 17,000 International Journals.

Clubs & Committees: MDI Gurgaon has various student-run clubs and committees. Academic clubs like Marquity, Monetrix, Strategist, and Opsession focus on marketing, finance, consulting, and operations, respectively.

Activity clubs such as Sanskriti, MART, Samaritans, and Mile organize cultural and social initiatives. Major campus events are conducted by event clubs like Illumina, Imperium, Delphique, and TEDxMDIGurgaon.

Committees like the International Relations Committee, Alumni Relations Committee, and Corporate Communications handle global collaborations, alumni engagement, media, and admissions. Other committees manage hostel and mess services, campus technology, and sports facilities.

A typical Day at MDI Gurgaon - A typical day at MDI Gurgaon starts with lectures, which usually start around 8 a.m. and go till 2-5 p.m. with a break in between. Events, assignments, case studies, presentations, and attending clubs & committee meetings are a part of daily life at MDI Gurgaon.
Ques. What programs are offered at MDI Gurgaon?

Ans. MDI Gurgaon offers a wide range of management programs at the postgraduate, doctoral, and executive levels. At the MBA/PGDM level, it offers PGDM (Post Graduate Diploma in Management), PGDM-HRM (Human Resource Management), and PGDM-IB (International Business), which are its flagship full-time programs. In addition, the institute offers FPM (Fellow Programme in Management) and EFPM (Executive Fellow Programme in Management) for doctoral-level research in management. MDI Gurgaon is also well known for its executive MBA programs, including Executive PGDM, as well as a variety of Management Development Programs (MDPs) that cater to working professionals and corporate executives.
Ques. Does MDI Gurgaon offer scholarships?

Ans. Yes, MDI Gurgaon offers merit-cum-means scholarships to 10 deserving students in the PGDM, PGDM-HRM, and PGDM-IB programs, which include a 50% waiver on tuition fees. The scholarship amount ranges from INR 8 Lakhs to INR 11 Lakhs. To be eligible for this scholarship, students must have a minimum of 6.0 CGPA, and their parents' income should not be more than INR 8 Lakhs. In case of a tie between students, MDI takes the scores in Term I and Term II into consideration.
Ques. What is the CAT Cutoff percentile for MDI Gurgaon?

Ans. The overall CAT cutoff for admission to MDI Gurgaon MBA/PGDM for candidates belonging to the General category is 95 percentile. This means that applicants are expected to secure a minimum of 95 percentile in the CAT exam to be shortlisted for the selection process. However, meeting the cutoff alone does not guarantee admission, as MDI also considers sectional cutoffs, academic performance, work experience, and performance in the Written Ability Test (WAT), Group Discussion (GD), and Personal Interview (PI). Generally, candidates with a percentile above 95 have a higher chance of receiving a call from MDI Gurgaon for its flagship PGDM programs.
Ques. Is there a gender diversity component in the selection criteria for MDI Gurgaon?

Ans. Yes, MDI Gurgaon gives importance to gender diversity in its admission process. Female candidates get an extra 2.5% weightage during the final selection. Apart from this, the institute also gives value to academic diversity (students from different study backgrounds), regional diversity (candidates from different parts of the country), and sports or extracurricular achievements. These factors, along with CAT/GMAT scores, past academics, work experience, and performance in WAT-GD-PI, are considered while making the final selection.
Ques. What is the application fee for MDI Gurgaon?

Ans. The application fee for MDI Gurgaon is INR 3,000, including GST, for most PGDM programs. There is a single, unified application form for all the PGDM programs offered at both MDI Gurgaon and MDI Murshidabad.
Ques. Is MDI Gurgaon better than IIFT Delhi?
Ans. Both MDI Gurgaon and IIFT Delhi are top B-schools, but their strengths differ.

MDI Gurgaon: Known for its flagship MBA/PGDM program, it has strong placements in consulting, marketing, HR, and general management. In 2025, the average package was INR 25.6 LPA, with the highest at INR 54 LPA. The CAT cutoff is around 95 percentile, and the campus is 35 acres.

IIFT Delhi: Specializes in International Business and Finance, with recruiters focused on trade, analytics, and global roles. In 2025, the average package was INR 27.3 LPA, with the highest at INR 85.4 LPA. The CAT cutoff is higher, around 98 percentile, and the campus size is 6.5 acres.
For finance, trade, or international business, IIFT Delhi is a better choice. For consulting, marketing, HR, and diverse general management roles, MDI Gurgaon has an edge.
Ques. Can I get direct admission to MDI Gurgaon without a CAT score?

Ans. No, direct admission is not possible at MDI Gurgaon. Admission is strictly based on a merit-based process that includes a valid entrance exam score (CAT or others, depending on the program), followed by WAT, GD, and PI rounds. The institute does not have a management or NRI quota for direct admission.

Students can find typical Personal Interview (PI) experiences for SJMSOM MBA admission. These are neutral descriptions of the process, based on common patterns. The personal interview (PI) at SJMSOM, IIT Bombay for the MBA program is usually short (10–20 minutes) and friendly, but it can get detailed on your profile. Most interviews have 2–3 panelists (professors, alumni, or faculty).They almost always start with:"Tell me about yourself" — Keep it short: education, work experience (if any), hobbies, and why MBA.Common questions asked at SJMSOM include: About your work experience: What do you do? Biggest challenge or achievement? Technical details from your job (e.g., testing types, programming, ETL tools, database joins if you're from IT/engineering). Why MBA? Why SJMSOM/IIT Bombay? (Be ready to explain how it fits your goals and what you won't learn just by continuing your job.) Academics: Questions from your undergrad subjects, final-year project, or basic concepts (e.g., derivatives, regression if engineering background). Current affairs/economy: Budget highlights, GDP of India/China, fiscal deficit, exchange rates, privatization, elections, state-specific info (e.g., Maharashtra regions, governor), economic policies like BS6 norms or scrapping policy. HR/personal: Hobbies, family (e.g., siblings, parents' profession), name origin (if unique), ethical dilemmas (e.g., choosing between companies selling tobacco vs. sugary drinks), women entrepreneurs you admire, or fun ones like "Do you bully your brother?" or "Probability of not getting selected?" Other calls: Which other B-schools you have calls from and your preference order. Sometimes a small puzzle or math question. The panel is polite and interactive. Be honest, confident, and prepared on your resume, current news, and why you want SJMSOM (highlight its IIT tag, placements, operations/consulting focus). Quick Takeaway from the Candidate:“I think I missed the technical part and my answers weren’t sharp enough on ‘Why MBA’. The panel was polite but they really test if you’re serious about switching to management.”

Akash Kumar, MBA (General) of 2024, says, “I was fortunate to receive acceptance letters from SJMSOM and K J Somaiya Institute of Management. ultimately, I choose SJMSOM because of its strong alumni network in consulting…” Keep reading.

Ques. How tough is the SJMSOM interview for engineers with work experience?

Ans. SJMSOM interviews can be very tough and feel like a tech or MTech test rather than MBA. Many candidates with 1-3 years work experience in IT or consulting get heavy grilling on undergrad topics like DSA, DBMS, circuits, distributions, or graphs. Panels may say you are behind if basics are forgotten. But if you revise college subjects well, it helps a lot.
Ques. What is the panel and duration like in SJMSOM interviews?

Ans. SJMSOM panels usually have 2 or 3 professors (mix of male and female, sometimes with industry experts). Interviews last 10-20 minutes. Panelists are friendly in some cases and help if you get stuck, but in others, they grill hard and may not listen fully to answers.
Ques. Any tips for preparing for the SJMSOM MBA interview?

Ans. For SJMSOM, revise undergrad technical subjects thoroughly (math, stats, engineering basics, DSA for CS). Know your work experience stories well. Read basic current affairs and economy news. Be honest if you don't know something, panels sometimes explain. Stay calm during grilling, as good CAT score and work ex also matter for final selection.

SJMSOM is nestled within the 545-acre IIT Bombay campus, surrounded by lakes and greenery, offering a peaceful yet vibrant environment. The institute features modern U-shaped air-conditioned classrooms, seminar halls, and access to large auditoriums for events and lectures. It houses two computer labs equipped with 139 PCs and software like SAS, SPSS, and Minitab, all connected via high-speed LAN and campus-wide Wi‑Fi. Students benefit from both the SJMSOM library and IIT Bombay’s Central Library, with access to thousands of books and top academic databases like Elsevier, EBSCO, and ProQuest, supporting a rich academic and research-focused environment.

The campus offers excellent residential and recreational facilities, including separate hostels for boys and girls with mess services, common rooms, and 24×7 security. At SJMSOM Hostel, students enjoy sports amenities such as swimming pools, courts for various games, and a fully equipped gym. The surrounding campus includes banks, medical services, and open green spaces. Cultural and academic festivals like Mood Indigo, Techfest, and Avenues keep the community vibrant. With scenic spots like Sameer Hill and lakefront trails.
Ques: What is the eligibility criteria for SJMSOM for MBA?

Ans: Aspirants with a four-year Bachelor’s degree or a Master’s degree in any discipline with 60% aggregate (55% aggregate for SC/ST) can apply. Further, CA, ICWA, CFA, CS, or FRM with a first-class bachelor’s degree in any discipline with 60% aggregate (55% aggregate for SC/ST) can also apply. SJMSOM IIT Bombay also accepts applications from candidates appearing for the final degree examination. However, in such a case, the final admission is subject to the fulfilment of the eligibility conditions at the time of admission.
Ques: What is the seat intake for MBA at SJMSOM?
Ans: SJMSOM offers 152 seats to MBA students. The total seat is divided among the general and reserved category. Check below the category-wise MBA intake:
Ques. What are the courses offered at SJMSOM?

Ans. SJMSOM offers a full-time MBA (Master of Business Administration) program, which is its flagship course. It also provides a Doctoral program (Ph.D.) in Management and an Executive MBA (EMBA) in collaboration with Washington University in St. Louis, USA.

It also offers Inter-Disciplinary Dual Degree Programs (IDDDP), like B.Tech + MBA and BS + MBA, designed for IITB students. These programs allow students to earn two degrees in an integrated manner. The MBA program includes core courses, electives, internships, and projects. The Ph.D. program is research-focused and suited for those aiming for academic or consulting careers.

The Executive MBA is targeted at professionals with work experience and offers global exposure. Each course has its own eligibility criteria and admission process. All programs are designed to build both conceptual understanding and practical skills in management.
Ques: Does SJMSOM accept admission in MBA through any other exam besides CAT?

Ans: SJMSOM only accepts CAT scores for admission to its flagship MBA programme. Aspiring candidates must apply for the CAT exam and should aim to score well in it. Candidates based on their CAT scores will be selected for the Personal Interview (PI) round.

I have friends in all the 3 institutes so I happen to be the right person to answer your question

A friend in NIT Trichy told me that the lectures are boring and the professors are incapable of delivering the concepts in a skillful manner. Most of them are hardly interested in teaching and offer no individual assistance. Only a few exceptional professors help you here.
Meanwhile, my friends at BITS Pilani and IIT Bombay were all praised for their respective institutes.
So yes there is a huge difference in the quality of education and opportunities offered by the aforementioned institutes. However, in the long run, it’s your skills and talents that matter.

Choosing a B-school can be a tricky decision especially when it comes to ROI. I understand that ROI is one of the most important factors when it comes to MBA courses since funding your education with loans come with its own set of challenges. But the institutes that you have mentioned above certainly surpass the challenges since they belong to the tier 1 category.

You might come across articles and blogs stating that FMS or JBIMS do not provide a typical MBA environment but for me, that discussion does not even make sense. What is an MBA environment after all? You spent 2 years of your life at the campus and wish to land a good job. FMS, JBIMS, and IIT Bombay all three have good market reputations, they home the best candidates and charge minimal fees. So, if ROI is even a little bit of a concern for you, go for these colleges without any second thought or regret.
IIT Bombay boasts a long list of notable alumni in various industries. Some of the most eminent figures have been listed below
These famous alumni from IIT Bombay have made the institution's name and are highly considered idols by many IITians.

When considering which business school to attend, it can be helpful to think about the impact that the institute will have on your resume. On the one hand, SJMSOM is an older institute that is well-known for its engineering program at IIT. While it may have a strong reputation in certain fields, it may not be as well-known for its MBA program. On the other hand, the newer IIMs, including IIM Ranchi, have not yet fully established their reputations in the business world. While they may have the prestige of being part of the IIM network, they may not yet have the same level of recognition as older institutes.

Ultimately, the value of an MBA degree will depend on what you make of it and the effort you put into your studies and career development. It is important to carefully consider both the reputation and the resources of the business school you choose in order to make the most of your MBA experience.

IIT B is particularly known for its specialization in Operations. Although it has a decent specialization in other domains like Marketing and IT as well, it is for Operations that people usually choose it. Some consider IIM Shillong or Trichy a better option for Finance. But I personally think that SJMSom IIT B is overall a better choice.

I cannot choose one between IIM Trichy and Shillong as both are at an equal level at this point. Despite being new, Trichy has managed to be in the league of Shillong. It has been growing at a fast pace and may even surpass IIM Shillong in the near future.
So if I am to rank the above options it has to be
SJMSom>IIM Shillong=IIM Trichy

SJMSOM at IIT B was founded in 1995, making it a relatively newer institution. But for a couple of years now, it has been making headlines because of some really outstanding profiles that were provided. Its core competencies are operations and supply chain management. There is no doubt that IIT B is the best choice if you want to work as a product manager. IIT B also has a beautiful campus with excellent facilities.

Additionally, it would give you the opportunity to take part in MOOD-I, the most significant cultural festival in all of Asia, which is held at IIT Bombay. With the well-known tech fests, there is another opportunity for you to participate. Furthermore, there are benefits to living in Mumbai. For guest lectures, the majority of the industry experts live nearby and are easily reachable.

IIM Lucknow was founded in 1984, so it has 11 batches more alumni than IIT B, resulting in approximately 3300 more alumni (considering 300 students per batch on average). It is also the fourth oldest IIM, following A, B, and C. You will gain a lot more industry experience, which will assist you in deciding what you truly want to do. In addition, IIM L offers better opportunities in Sales & Marketing, Consultancy, and BFSI than SJMSOM. Furthermore, you will be networking with a large number of students from all over the country and forming lifelong friendships. Furthermore, the IIM tag for a managerial position has an advantage over the IIT tag, which is still developing.

It would be fine if you went to IIM L, SJMSOM, or any other B school a few years later. When you switch from the first company you get after your placements, the new recruiters will be more interested in your work than in the college you attended. And the impact of your college's name gradually fades. What remains are the lessons you've learned and the memories you've made over the last two years.

Personally, I will recommend you join IIM Lucknow . The reason being your outstanding profile. With such an amazing profile you have multiple chances of getting selected in the top firms in Consulting and Investment Banking areas. Many of these reputed companies do not visit the campus if SJMSOM at all. So you will be losing a lifetime of opportunities.

Also, at the end of the day, IIM Lucknow is a top 4 IIM and its brand name will influence you throughout your life. The fees are not a problem as the majority of the students take educational loans offered at low-interest rates. You can pay it back within 5-7 years with the high paying job you land post-MBA.

IIM Shillong is the better college among these. The institute puts emphasis on hands-on learning. You will learn how to handle real-time issues. The coursework and teaching go well beyond classroom learning. IIM Shillong has made great strides in recent years in terms of facilities and infrastructure. It has an impressive placement record. IIM Shillong placements in 2022 witnessed the highest CTC of INR 55.22 LPA. This year the major recruiters were Deloitte, DE Shaw, TATA Steel, etc.

MDI will be a better option for all specializations, except Operations. If you are interested in Operations, IIT Bombay is much better. MDI Gurgaon placements are excellent. Big names such as Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, and BCG have visited the campus placements. The 2022 placement drive had an average CTC of INR 26.65 LPA.
MDI offers the best placement in the finance domain after IIM A, B, C, FMS, and XLRI. JP, HSBC, Nomura, Stanchart, etc. are some of the major recruiters from the finance sector.
MDI placement records for Marketing are good as well. HUL, Coke, Pepsi, and P&G are some significant recruiters from the marketing sector.

Among these colleges, IIFT Kolkata or MDI will be better for Finance. According to MDI Gurgaon placements 2022 record, BFSI, and E-Commerce sectors had placement rates of 22% and 13%. During 2021 placement drive, 55 students from MDI were placed in the Finance sector. The highest CTC offered in this sector was INR 21-23 LPA.
You can also consider IIFT Kolkata. It offers similar opportunities as IIFT Delhi, in the Finance sector. During IIFT Kolkata Summer placements 2021, the top recruiting sector was BFSI.

KLE Dr. M.S. Sheshgiri College of Engineering and Technology, also known as KLEMSSCET, Belgaum, established in 1979, is a private engineering institution under KLE Society. It is affiliated with KLE Technological University, and is AICTE approved. It is also ISO certified and NBA accredited for all BE programs. KLEMSSCET B.Tech was ranked 111 in India in 2024 by The Week, while its B.Tech was ranked 76 by Outlook out of 150 colleges in India in 2019.

KLEMSSCET provides UG programs such as BE, BCA and PG programs such as M.Tech, MBA and MCA in various specializations. Its flagship course is BE in Computer Science and Engineering. The fees for the whole duration of the course stand at INR 9.72 Lakhs (General Quota). Admission to BE is entrance-based, requiring a valid score in KCET or COMEDK UGET, with a minimum of 50% in 10+2 (PCM).

KLEMSSCET placement report 2025 is not available as the season is ongoing. However, according to the KLEMSSCET’s 2023 placement report, 652 offers were made by more than 75 companies. More than 80% placement rate has been recorded by the college in case of CSE and ECE, with a highest package of INR 34 LPA and an average package of INR 8.05 LPA. Serum Connect, Federal Bank, Electrobit, Continental, TCS Ninja, DXC Technologies and Mercedes Benz top the list of recruiters.
The key highlights of KLE Dr. M.S. Sheshgiri College of Engineering and Technology are provided below:

KLEMSSCET offers 22 courses across the UG and PG levels. Below are the details for key programs:

Admission to KLEMSSCET is entrance-based for admission following KLE Technological University guidelines. For admission to BE, a candidate must have a valid score in KCET or COMEDK or JEE Main, and the candidates must possess 50% in 10+2 with Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics. For M.Tech, admission is taken through GATE or PGCET Karnataka scores; for MBA and MCA, PGCET, CAT, MAT, or GMAT scores are considered. Admission to Ph.D. is made based on the University Level Research Aptitude Test (ULRAT) of VTU.

KLEMSSCET accepts KCET, COMEDK UGET and Karnataka PGCET scores for admissions. The 2025 cutoffs are not yet released, but below are the 2024 and 2023 cutoffs (closing ranks) for the general category (All India quota) exams:

Keeping the 2024 report as an indicator, the college had an 80% placement rate in CSE and ECE and a total of 652 offers were given by more than 70 companies. The highest package was an INR 34 LPA, while the average was an INR 8.05 LPA. Major recruiters included: TCS, Wipro, Accenture, Cognizant, Federal Bank, Electrobit, Continental, TCS Ninja, and Scientific Games. The placement cell trains the students in aptitude, reasoning, and resume building, and offers a huge auditorium for pre-placement talks and interview setups for video conferencing.
KLEMSSCET offers scholarships based on merit and need, including:

The 17-acre Belgaum campus of KLEMSSCET provides a dynamic ambience with modern facilities. These include smart classrooms, Digital Library, well-equipped laboratories, viz., CSE lab and Biomedical Lab. Residential facilities give accommodation to 500 boys and 500 girls with Wi-Fi, gym facility, and medical treatment supported by Vaidyashree insurance at KLE’s Dr. Prabhakar Kore Hospital. Students are allowed to participate in 10 student clubs, one annual tech fest VAIVIDHYAM, and sports tournaments. Other facilities include 6 buses, cafeteria, ATM, and 24-hour security.

Ques. How does student life on KLEMSSCET campus generally go?

Ans. Student life at KLEMSSCET is equally disciplined and vibrant. Freshers may find those initial rules of attendance, dress code, and behavior quite useful, and majority adjust to them. The campus encourages co-curricular activities and has clubs for robotics, cultural activities, NSS, coding, and so on. Events such as KLE Fest, technical symposiums, hackathons, and sports meet keep the life away from academics. Students like the peaceful atmosphere offered by Belgaum's Udyambag area.
Ques. What engineering courses are available at the UG and PG levels at KLEMSSCET?

Ans. At the UG level, the college offers a wide variety of engineering courses under the BE program, including Computer Science and Engineering (CSE), Electronics and Communication Engineering (ECE), Mechanical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Electrical and Electronics Engineering (EEE), Chemical Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, and Artificial Intelligence and Data Science (recent addition). On the PG level, it offers M.Tech. specializations (with courses like Machine Design, Power Systems, VLSI, and so on), MBA (dual specialization), and MCA. The research laboratories and departments also allow for Ph.D. study within VTU.
Ques. How are grievances and student concerns handled at KLEMSSCET?

Ans. KLEMSSCET college has an Internal Complaint Committee (ICC) for gender-related issues, a student grievance redressal cell for academic and administrative matters, and an anti-ragging committee to maintain discipline and safety. Students can raise grievances by voting for their department heads and faculty mentors to either the principal or to a formal disciplinary committee where mostly the matters are resolved at the department level. The views are represented by electing class representatives or student council members, helping to ensure that these voices are heard at the authority level.

subject_lists.title: SPJIMR Campus Life & Facilities
subjects: Campus: It is spread across 45 Acres in Mumbai. The campus has a library, hostels, multiple cafeterias, a jogging trail, etc.
Library: It is stocked with 29,000+ books, 30,000+ e-books, and 8,000+ digital resources. The institute has collaborations with external libraries (e.g., British Council, American Resource Centre).

Hostel: The institute has separate hostels for boys & girls. The rooms are allocated on a double or triple sharing basis. They are air-conditioned and offer a common room with all the amenities as well.
Mess: Dining options include a central mess, two bistros, an executive dining area, and a night canteen, serving vegetarian meals.

Sports: The institute has a recreation centre with indoor games, open-sky sports (like pickleball), a gym, and yoga classes. Outdoor sports courts are available for cricket, basketball, football, and volleyball.

A Typical Day at SPJIMR: It starts with early morning lectures that can extend until 7-8 pm, but usually gets over by 5-6 PM. Post-lecture evenings are dedicated to assignments, presentations, pre-reads, etc, for the next day's lectures.

paragraphs: Senior Content Writer | Updated on - Apr 8, 2026
18 Mar, 2026 SPJIMR PGDM Admission 2026-28 has closed. The interviews concluded on Feb 17, and the program will start in June 2026.

S. P. Jain Institute of Management and Research (SPJIMR), established in 1981, is a private management institute located in Mumbai. The institute holds the Triple Crown accreditation from AACSB, AMBA, and EQUIS​.
PGDM (MBA) and PGPM are the most popular full-time programs. The institute also offers multiple executive programs in part-time mode.
Direct Link: SPJIMR PGPDM Admission 2026
PGPGM registrations at SP Jain has started for Phase 2. SPJIMR PGPGM admission dates 2026 are as follows:
PGPM registrations open 3 times a year on a rolling basis. The tentative admission schedule for all three phases is given below:

SP Jain offers PG courses are residential programs in full-time mode. Executive courses are available in part-time mode. In addition, the institute provides various entrepreneurship courses and an online PGDM program. Here are the highlights of SPJIMR Courses & Fees:
Admission to SPJIMR (SP Jain) is granted based on scores obtained in entrance exams, along with profile evaluation and/or interview. The accepted exams vary by program:

Candidates with a Bachelor’s Degree are eligible to apply. In addition, a few courses require a mandatory work experience in a full-time setup. The final selection will be based on a valid entrance exam score, academic profile, work experience, and personal interview rounds (depending on the program).

Candidates have to apply online on the official website @spjimr.org. Shortlisted candidates will be called for group discussions or a personal interview. Finally, applicants need to submit their entrance scores. The application fee is INR 2,000.

The majority of the seats at SPJIMR Mumbai are offered through CAT scores. The round 1 SPJIMR CAT Cutoff for the general category stood at 85th percentile (2024 and 2023 both). It was the same for admission to these postgraduate programs for candidates belonging to the EWS, OBC, SC, and ST categories.

“SPJIMR doesn’t publish official CAT cutoffs, but competitive applicants often aim for high percentiles (~98+) — though strong profiles get consideration too.” — Reddit user summarizing admission competitiveness

SPJIMR Mumbai has concluded the placement drive for the batch of 2024-26 with a 100% placement rate. 46% students were offered PPOs. Consulting was the top-performing domain with 40% of the total job offers.
Some of the top recruiters included Kearney, TAS, BCG, Aditya Birla Group, Accenture Strategy, Goldman Sachs, HUL, Nestle, HSBC, Morgan Stanley, and Colgate-Palmolive.
The major highlights of SPJIMR PGDM placements are provided in the table below:

The institute has transitioned from autumn placements to summer placements for its PGDM programs. The PGDM cohort of 2025-27 was the second batch to participate in the summer placement cycle of the institute.

The batch received 425 internship offers. Consulting sector made the highest number of offers, ie, 32% of the total internships. The top recruiters at SPJIMR Summer Internship included Alvarez & Marsal, Airtel, Dabur, Diageo, HCCB, Mastercard, Perfetti Van Melle, Phillip Capital, and Visa
Given below are the highlights of PGDM summer internship:

The total fees for MBA at SPJIMR Mumbai increased by 17.78% (approx.) for 2026 as compared to 2025 (INR 22.5 Lakhs). However, the ROI decreased from 142.22% to 127.36% based on the average package secured by the institute.
“Placements at SPJIMR feel less chaotic than some IIMs because the process is structured and quick.” — Quora comparison discussion
SP Jain provides scholarships to PGDM students in need based on their academic performance, extra-curricular activities, and conduct.
Further, the institute also offers financial assistance to students of GMP and FPM programs. The details for SPJIMR Scholarships are mentioned below:
Students of PGDM courses receive a merit cum means based financial assistance for both years. They are reimbursed for the entire tuition fee.
Apart from financial assistance, the institute also offers the Mirae Asset Foundation (MAF) Scholarship for PGDM and a merit-based scholarship for PGDM (BM).

Under the MAF Scholarship scheme, students with a family income of less than INR 8 lakhs are granted scholarships for two years of the PGDM program. Every year, two participants from the first and second years are awarded scholarships worth INR 5 lakhs each.

Furthermore, the merit-based scholarship will be available to second-year students of the PGDM (BM) program only, depending on their academic performance in the first year. Based on the evaluations, applicants are provided with partial or full financial assistance.
SP Jain (SPJIMR) is known for its PGDM program in India as well as globally. It has been consistently ranked in the top 10 B-Schools of India. Details about SPJIMR Ranking are provided below:
SPJIMR is located in the financial capital of India, Mumbai. It is known for its culture and diversity, Abhyudaya program, global exposure, and great RoI.

“Campus life at SPJIMR isn’t just academics and placements. We had trips, sports, late nights in group work, and unexpected memories that weren’t in any brochure.” — A first-year PGDM student sharing a slice of everyday experiences beyond studies on Reddit
“Life at SPJIMR feels like that classic B-school experience — clubs, competitions, cultural events, and endless group projects with people from diverse backgrounds.” — Anonymous Student
Ques. Is it possible to apply for SPJIMR without appearing for CAT?
Ans. CAT is the most common exam for Indian applicants applying to SPJIMR. However, candidates with a valid GMAT score can also apply to the PGDM and PGPM programs.
The vast majority of seats are filled by CAT-qualified candidates, with only about 4–6 seats usually going to GMAT-qualified applicants.
Ques. How many seats are there in the MBA program of SPJIMR?

Ans. SPJIMR offers a total of 396 seats to its PGDM (MBA) program. Out of which, 120 seats are for PGDM General and 120 seats for PGDM (BM). The remaining 36 seats are for OCI/PIO/foreign applicants (PGDM General).
Ques. Can I change my PGDM specialisation after I join the program at SPJIMR?
Ans. In the first year of SPJIMR, students will study all the functional areas of management, providing a holistic perspective of general management.

The 2nd year will deal with specialisation courses, and the students will be given an option to change their specialisation at the end of the first year. This will be based on the candidate’s performance, merit, and faculty panel decision.
Ques. What is the PGPM program at SPJIMR?

Ans. The PGPM program at SPJIMR is a residential program for experienced professionals. It is offered for 18 months, where the first 2 months are online, 12 months at the campus, and the remaining 4 months for projects and international immersion.
This course is for candidates with at least three years of work experience and strong domain expertise. The course will help participants move to more expansive roles in general management.

It prepares participants to lead larger teams and handle greater responsibilities in business, enabling them to evolve into well-rounded managers with broader knowledge, enhanced skills, and the mindset required for senior roles.
Ques. What advantages do partner schools provide to GMP students of SPJIMR?
Ans. The GMP program at SPJIMR is offered in collaboration with top-ranked B-schools worldwide. These schools provide students with multiple advantages, and a few of them are listed below:
Ques. What benefits does SPJIMR provide to FPM scholars?

Ans. SPJIMR offers a fully funded full-time residential FPM program. The students have to pay only the application fee and a refundable deposit of INR 10k. They are provided with a stipend of INR 40k per month during the program.

The institute takes only 5 candidates per year, and they can apply for a maximum of 2 areas of specialisation. However, they can change their specialisation before finalising seminar courses, provided they have valid reasons.
Ques. How can students get involved in campus life at SPJIMR?

Ultimately, the best college depends on your preferences and future prospects.

All the aforementioned colleges are among the best B Schools in India so the choice between them depends on your preference and future prospects. You need to determine what exactly you want from the program and where your career currently is.
In general, ISB is for people who have better industry experience, good leadership skills and decent academics. The other B Schools focus more on excellent academics throughout your career.
The ranking of these institutes in my opinion is ISB, IIM-A, B, C>IIM-L, FMS, XLRI,>SPJIMR

The above preference order is based on a number of factors like career progression, college market value perception, quality of faculty, quality of students, academic learning, quality of recruiters and infrastructure.

Both IIM Kozhikode and SPJIMR offer an excellent curriculum in MBA that is taught by the best and most learned faculty. One of my cousins chose IIMK over SPJIMR because she was inclined toward Finance specifically. Additionally, the IIM tag helped her avail better opportunities.

SPJIMR on the other hand has a few drawbacks that make you want to reconsider joining it. Firstly, it has a triple occupancy room system which may not be fit for everyone. Secondly, its culture is a bit restrictive focusing only on mental development.

Overall, If you are a CA or a CFA graduate with Financial Corp experience, you will be exposed to similar cultures and opportunities on both campuses. But if you are an engineer, you will get better opportunities at IIM Kozhikode.
Ultimately, the final decision is yours to make!

Institute of Engineering and Management (IEM Kolkata) was established in 1989 and is a private engineering and management institute affiliated with MAKAUT. The first campus was in Salt Lake, Sector V. The institute is approved by AICTE and accredited by NBA and NAAC with ‘A’ grade. In 2025, IEM was ranked 221st (B.Tech) and 173rd (Computer Applications) by CollegeDunia, and placed in the 151–200 band (B.Tech) by NIRF.
Note: From 2026, the institute will not consider WBJEE for admission to its B.Tech. programs.

Placement: IEM Kolkata has not published the placement details of 2025, but from students' reviews and research, the highest salary offered was INR 32 LPA for B.Tech. students. IEM NIRF Report 2026 states that the median package is around INR 6 LPA for B.Tech and INR 3.36 LPA for M.Tech, while the MBA median package is about INR 17 LPA.
Students can find the IEM Kolkata NIRF Report 2026 here.

Some of the top recruiters at the Institute of Engineering and Management Kolkata include Amazon, Tata Consultancy Services, Capgemini, Wipro, Cognizant, Infosys, Accenture, Deloitte, PwC, Ernst & Young, IBM, HCL Technologies, Tech Mahindra, Larsen & Toubro, and ITC Limited.

IEM Kolkata has many useful facilities for students. There are separate hostels and common rooms for boys and girls. The campus has a medical unit for free health check-ups and vaccinations, and every student gets a Mediclaim policy worth INR 50,000. It also provides bus services.

Each department has its own lab. There are special labs like AI+ML Lab, AR-VR Lab, and Data Science Lab. The digital library is open all day, all year, with thousands of books, journals, and access to websites like IEEE and J-GATE. The campus has free Wi-Fi and an AC Canteen. It also has sports rooms and areas for games like cricket, football, table tennis, and chess.
IEM Sports Facilities

According to Subhrodip Pal’s review on CollegeDunia, Institute of Engineering and Management Kolkata offers decent infrastructure, disciplined campus life, and good academic facilities, though the campus environment is quite strict and academically demanding.

The student mentions that the total B.Tech course fees are around INR 8,50,000 with scholarships like SVMCM available. The campus hosts events such as INNO FUSION, hackathons, and student clubs, but sports facilities and open spaces are limited due to the relatively small campus size. Classrooms follow a traditional setup with projectors and mic facilities, and the library provides adequate academic resources.

IEM Kolkata provides separate hostel facilities for boys and girls, located close to the main academic campus. The hostels offer a range of options; Non-AC and AC rooms, typically with double or triple occupancy. Annual fees for Non-AC rooms are approximately INR 1 lakh to INR 1.05 lakhs, while for AC rooms is approximately INR 1.66 lakhs, depending on amenities. The hostels are furnished with basic bedding, Wi-Fi connectivity, and access to a mess that serves three meals daily. Safety features include 24/7 security, CCTV surveillance, and resident wardens to ensure student welfare.

IEM Kolkata is a top private institute known for its strong academics, consistent placements, and great ROI. It offers a median package of INR 6 LPA for B.Tech and an impressive INR 16.4 LPA for MBA, with top recruiters like Amazon, TCS, Capgemini, Infosys, and Wipro. With fees around INR 8 lakhs to INR 8.65 lakhs and scholarships up to 100%, IEM Kolkata provides a competitive ROI for meritorious students. If you’re unable to secure admission into top-tier national institutes like IITs, NITs, or top private universities such as VIT or SRM, IEM Kolkata is a strong alternative.
Ques. Is IEM Kolkata good for B.Tech CSE?

Ans. Yes, IEM Kolkata is a good choice for B.Tech in Computer Science and Engineering (CSE). With total fees of about INR 8.65 lakhs and various merit-based scholarships (up to 100%), the ROI is strong. The median package for B.Tech stands at around INR 6 LPA, with top recruiters such as Amazon, TCS, Infosys, Capgemini, Cognizant, and Wipro hiring regularly from the campus.
Ques. Is it worth studying for an MBA from IEM Kolkata?

Ans. Yes, pursuing an MBA from IEM Kolkata is a good choice for students who are looking for a good, placement focused B-school without paying high fees. The institute has a strong record of placements and ROI, with a median package of INR 16.4 LPA and a ROI of 50% in 2024 and top recruiters including Amazon, TCS, EY, Capgemini, Axis Bank, and more.
Ques. Can a student get admission to IEM Kolkata through WBJEE?

Ans. No, students cannot get admission to IEM Kolkata through WBJEE anymore. The institute has discontinued admissions via WBJEE from the current academic year. Earlier, IEM Kolkata accepted candidates based on WBJEE and JEE Main scores, but now all B.Tech admissions are conducted solely through IEMJEE, the institute’s own entrance examination and counselling process.
Ques. Can I apply to IEM Kolkata through IEMJEE or IEMCET, and who is eligible for these exams?

Ans. Yes. For admission to B.Tech or B. Tech (Lateral Entry) at the Institute of Engineering and Management, students can appear for the IEMJEE. If you are applying for other programs like BBA, BCA, BHM, BBA LLB, MCA, or M.Tech, you need to take the IEMCET conducted by the institute. Both exams are used by IEM to shortlist candidates for counselling and admission.
Ques. Is the IEMJEE as tough as the JEE Main?

Ans. IEMJEE is not as tough as JEE Main. While both exams share a similar syllabus based on the Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics topics from Classes 11 and 12, the difficulty level and competition are quite different. Given below is a comparison between IEMJEE and JEE Main:

Yes, you can get admission to IEM (Institute of Engineering and Management) without appearing for IEMJEE, depending on the course and category. IEM offers direct admission or merit-based admission through national/state-level entrance exams like JEE Main, WBJEE, or sometimes based on 12th-grade marks. MCA at IEM Kolkata is a 2-year, full-time, degree program offered On Campus.

First, ensure you meet eligibility: 10+2 with Physics, Chemistry and Maths from a recognised board. Then, apply online for the institute’s entrance exam, IEMJEE, through the official website. After appearing and qualifying in IEMJEE, participate in the counselling for seat allocation based on entrance score and preferences. Finally, complete document verification and fee payment as notified by the institute to confirm your admission.

IEM Kolkata reserves around 25% of B.Tech seats for Management Quota, allowing admission based on Class 12 PCM marks without requiring JEE Main, WBJEE, or IEMJEE scores. Candidates must meet the eligibility criteria and pay higher fees for direct admission under this quota

Admission to the Institute of Engineering and Management, Kolkata, is entrance-based. For B.Tech, candidates must qualify WBJEE or IEMJEE and meet 12th PCM criteria. Apply online, attend counselling, verify documents, and pay fees to confirm admission. Final admission is granted after completing all formalities and document submission.

IEM Kolkata BBA is offered as 3 Years Full Time program, with total intake of 120 seats. The minimum eligibility criteria for BBA is 10+2 with 50%. The total fees for IEM Kolkata BBA is INR 3.35 Lakhs for the complete course duration. IEM Kolkata Hostel Fee is INR 1.05 Lakhs.

IEM Kolkata B.Tech Computer Science and Engineering is offered as 4 Years Full Time program. The minimum eligibility criteria for B.Tech is 10+2 with 60%+WBJEE. The total fees for IEM Kolkata B.Tech Computer Science and Engineering is INR 8.67 Lakhs for the complete course duration

Candidates have to register at wbjeeb.nic.in/wbjee for BTech admissions. For MBA admissions, candidates can apply through the official website: cetmat.formflix.com/jemat.

Disbursement: The bank will transfer the loan money to the institute to pay your fees and costs as soon as XLRI verifies your registration.

RNS Institute of Technology in Bangalore could be a good choice if you value solid infrastructure and strong academics. The school is known for its supportive faculty and good placement results, particularly in tech-related fields. Located in Bangalore, it has a lively campus life and active student community.

The courses offered are accredited, and the institute has some level of autonomy which allows for flexible academic options. If you're keen on engineering and looking for good placements and infrastructure in Bangalore, RNSIT is definitely worth thinking about.
If you're part of the CS or IT departments, things are pretty chill. The staff is supportive, and attendance isn't strictly enforced. These are probably the top departments based on what I know.

On the other hand, if you're in EEE or ISE, you might just be counting down the days until graduation. It can get tough, especially if you end up with backlogs, which is possible if you're not good at sweet-talking or are too straightforward.
Departments like ECE and Mechanical are somewhere in between. I used to feel a bit jealous of my friends in CSE and IT. I graduated from EEE in 2015.

Another downside of studying at RNSIT is the limited extracurricular activities and events. While there are a few major fests like Pantheon and Parichay, the frequency and quality of these events often leave much to be desired. Many students feel that there should be more opportunities for cultural engagement and technical events to enhance our college experience.
The campus life can feel a bit dull at times due to the lack of vibrant activities and events throughout the year.
The most annoying thing? Honestly, there are a lot of things that bug me about the college, but I'll share them all here.
First off, there's no sports complex. Seriously, most colleges have one, and some even have two or three! We've just got this tiny sports room that's almost always locked.
Then, there's no amphitheater, and we don't even have an auditorium.
The budget for our fests is pretty low. With better funding, they could be way more organized. It's something every student deserves.

As for clubs, we barely have 3 to 5, and only about 1 or 2 are active for a couple of months each year. It would be nice to have more interesting clubs. Club interviews and projects would make college life much more fun and memorable.

They keep taking away phones, but why not have mobile lockers in every classroom? I mean, I'm not saying I'd use them since my phone is my only entertainment during some classes, but for those who would use them, why not have lockers?
Teachers could also go beyond just the 5 or 6 units in the VTU syllabus and teach some extra valuable stuff. Not all students would appreciate it, but those who are interested would benefit.
Lastly, they should stop opening schools, preschools, and PU colleges on the campus. It just ruins the vibe.
So, those are my gripes. I hope someone is paying attention.

I feel RNSIT is a good college for pursuing a Bachelor of Engineering in Cyber Security. The curriculum is relevant and prepares us for real-world applications. The faculty are supportive and approachable, which makes learning easier. The placement opportunities are decent, with many companies visiting, and the highest package was around 56 LPA. However, the campus life could use more events and activities to engage students. Overall, I think it's a good option for those looking to enter the cyber security field.

RNS Institute of Technology in Bangalore is generally considered a bit below average among Indian colleges. Some of my friends who went there, even those with really good grades, ended up with job offers around 3.5 to 4 lakhs per year. This is mainly because there aren't many companies visiting the campus for recruitment. Companies like Bosch, Aricent, TCS, Infosys, Accenture, and Thoughtworks do hire for the CSE department. If you're looking for better opportunities, you might want to check out autonomous colleges in Bangalore.

My time at RNSIT for the Bachelor of Engineering (Cyber Security) course has been quite mixed. While I appreciate the curriculum's relevance to current trends, the internal exam frequency feels overwhelming. We have three internals each month, which can be quite hectic.

Placement opportunities seem promising, with many companies like Infosys and Adobe visiting for recruitment. However, the highest package is around 55 lakh, but I think the average is lower. Overall, the college environment is supportive, but I feel there could be more focus on practical learning.

Placements at RNSIT Bangalore are generally quite good. If you have over 70%, you're likely to secure a job with at least one company, though it might not be in your core field. Even students with 65% have plenty of opportunities, as many large companies look for candidates with that percentage. Some companies even consider candidates with 60%. So, having more than 65% gives you a great chance of landing a job.

Typically, about 500-600 students out of 800 get placed each year. Only a few companies offering core jobs and high salaries visit, around 3-4. About 20 companies come to the campus, and another 20 invite students to pool campuses. The average salary package is around 3.5 lakh.
LNMIIT beats RV when it comes to meeting important criteria.
My sister chose RNSIT for her B.Tech degree. According to her, there are several factors one needs to consider while choosing one’s college.

One of them is the distance of the college from one’s home (or place of stay). Choosing a college near one’s place of stay buys a lot of time which one can then use to pursue one’s studies/interests. Moreover, one feels much more relaxed because the travel time is reduced to such a great extent.
Barring Civil and Mechanical, all the other departments witness good placements at RNSIT. The faculties of RNSIT are supportive as well.
Thus, you can consider choosing RNSIT over MVJCE Bangalore, given that the option suits your personal preferences.

Anyone with a bachelor's degree (or equivalent) who belongs to a family business and plans to take it forward can apply. Admission depends on your score in the Business Admission Test (BAT), a personal interview, and your past academic record.

XLRI and ISB place less stringent emphasis on school-level marks, focusing more on holistic candidate evaluation in comparison to the IIM’s.

ISB Hyderabad is certainly a better choice than IIM Ahmedabad for a 1 year MBA executive. It has better faculty, an international student profile, an amazing campus, and more than 800 students in a single batch. The admission process is also simpler than IIM Ahmedabad. ISB Hyderabad has a much more diverse crowd than IIM Ahmedabad which usually comprises CS-related people.
PGP-X at IIMA is its flagship program whereas the one-year program in ISB is their main program so it carries more value and more focus is given to that program.

IIM Ahmedabad too has its own perks one of them being its rich legacy of 50+ years and an excellent alumni enterprise spread across the globe. Also, since the batch is smaller the competition is less so the placement opportunities are more. Recruiters coming to hire PGP students also roll out lateral offers for PGP-X students.
Ultimately, choose the one that aligns with your personal preferences and future goals.

There is no right answer to this question as the value of an MBA program can vary depending on individual circumstances and goals. It’s a personal decision and its credibility depends on many factors like -Why MBA, why ISB, and why now?

I have many friends at ISB Hyderabad pursuing an MBA and most of them claim that the efforts they invested while preparing for admissions were worth it. They got placed with decent packages and met many like-minded and smart people. They learned many life lessons in the 1 year. They had the opportunity to interact with more than 50 CEOs of top firms. Most of them claimed that their affiliation with ISB Hyderabad has uplifted their value in the industry as well as the society.
The general opinion of most of them was that the MBA from ISB Hyderabad was worth the time and money invested.

All the aforementioned colleges are among the best B Schools in India so the choice between them depends on your preference and future prospects. You need to determine what exactly you want from the program and where your career currently is.
In general, ISB is for people who have better industry experience, good leadership skills and decent academics. The other B Schools focus more on excellent academics throughout your career.
The ranking of these institutes in my opinion is ISB, IIM-A, B, C>IIM-L, FMS, XLRI,>SPJIMR

The above preference order is based on a number of factors like career progression, college market value perception, quality of faculty, quality of students, academic learning, quality of recruiters and infrastructure.

The institute boasts a central library with over 10,000 books, 165+ research publications, and offers a wide range of courses with 45+ programs to choose from, including 30 government-allotted seats.

Students from any part of the city can travel easily, if not comfortably. The authorities are constantly trying to upgrade the connectivity through shuttle or private arrangements by the student community at the university.

Health Centre: The recent management added an advanced health care centre in the university for the students. The health care centre keeps close contact with the administrators of the universities about existing health services and informs them about the planning and allocation of the resources. The authorities have plans to develop the university health centre to improve overall safety since the Pandemic.

Library: A modern Central Library with a rich collection of more than 61000 books. Learning resources, journals (national & international level) in all the disciplines taught are spread over an area of more than 16,758 square feet. It has an air-conditioned reading hall, a separate hall for the periodical section and an electronic resource centre. The library has a dedicated Internet facility where students are encouraged to make use of e-journals (IEEE, ASME, and DELNET, etc), e-theses, and NPTEL video lectures and web-based NPTEL lecture contents.

Azad Institute of Engineering and Technology provides hostel facilities for the students. The Institute has fully furnished separate hostels for boys and girls. Azad Technical Campus has a two separate Boys Hostels “Azad Boys Hostel” for II, III, and IVth year boys and “New Azad Boys Hostel” for Ist year boys as well as there are two separate Girls Hostel “Abdul Kalam Girls Hostel “ for II, III, and IVth year girls and “New Abdul Kalam Girls Hostel” for Ist year girls both are fully equipped with modern facilities which can accommodate 600 students in Boys Hostel and 500 students in girls Hostel. Ques. Does Azad Institute of Engineering and Technology have clubs?

Ans. Yes, Azad Institute of Engineering and Technology have clubs, and they are the Faculty Club, technical and innovation clubs, the Horse Riding Club, and cultural and fest clubs. Additionally, Azad Institute of Engineering and Technology also has an FM Radio which is used to make important announcements and play some lively music during breaks.
Ques. Is staying in the Azad Institute of Engineering and Technology hostel compulsory?
Ans. No, staying in the hostel is not compulsory. Students can choose whether to live in the hostel or arrange for their accommodation outside the campus.
Ques. Is it possible to apply offline for admission to Azad Institute of Engineering and Technology?

Ans. Yes. Indeed. Azad Institute of Engineering and Technology accepts offline applications in addition to online ones. Interested applicants can go to the college's on-campus admissions office, fill out the required form, turn in the necessary paperwork, pay the application fee, and finish the admissions process offline.

A typical day at FMS Delhi starts with case discussions in class, where participation really matters. Between lectures, you’ll find students either in the library, preparing for upcoming evaluations, or rushing to society meetings. Evenings are usually spent working with peers: either on assignments, internship prep, or planning events.

Rohit Jawa's path to CEO of HUL exemplifies the transformative power of FMS Delhi. The college's rigorous academics equipped him with the business foundation needed for the FMCG industry, while its focus on well-rounded development shaped his leadership and communication skills. Rohit joined HUL straight out of FMS as a management trainee, and his 35-year climb through the ranks to CEO is evidence of the program's ability to prepare students for exceptional careers.

In terms of Faculty, FMS's MBA program is beyond par as compared to other B Schools as most faculties have years of experience and are the leading academicians in the country in their area of expertise. Examples are Prof. Kavita Singh for OB, Prof. Venkat Raman for HR etc. FMS Delhi follows a semester system so it makes it difficult for students to go on international exchange programs.

Candidates are shortlisted based on a weighted score. This score is calculated by combining the percentiles from all three sections of the CAT exam (VARC, DILR, and QA) with differential weightage (40% 30% 30% respectively). Additionally, your marks from Class X and XII are considered (10% weightage each), with a bonus for scoring above 75% (10 points) or between 60-74% (5 points).

There's also an encouraging diversity factor: women candidates receive an additional 5 points for shortlisting purposes only. If you make the cut-off for this shortlist, you'll be invited for a Personal Interview (PI) where your performance will be evaluated alongside your weighted CAT score, academic marks, and a discussion on your Statement of Purpose (SOP). The weightage for final selection breaks down as follows: 50% for the weighted CAT score, 10% each for Class X and XII marks, 10% for the SOP discussion, 5% for Extempore and 15% for your performance in the PI.

FMS Delhi used to be renowned as a marketing campus with its legacy of making top-rank marketers such as the current CEOs of HUL, Loreal, and Tata Play. However, today, the campus hosts all the industries such as consulting, finance etc., in its placement process with consulting extending the most number of offers. Companies include the likes of Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanely, HUL, Nestle, McKinsey and Co., Bain, BCG etc.

Life at FMS Delhi is not chilled out as it is one of the Top B-Schools in the country. FMS Delhi is a red building with some Classrooms and Academic Blocks while the IIMs have huge campuses. IIMs have hostel facilities for the Students while FMS Delhi students live in PG and Flats.

It depends on what Chill life means to you. Comparing life at FMS with IIMs in terms of "chilled out" can vary from individual to individual. Some students may thrive in high-pressure environments, while others may prefer a more relaxed atmosphere. Both FMS Delhi and Top IIMs offer excellent Education experiences.

FMS Delhi is one of the Top B-Schools in India, often compared with IIM A, B & C. FMS Delhi has the best RoI, low fees of INR 2 Lakhs, and a batch size of 251 + Supernumerary Seats (for batch 2024-26).

FMS Delhi MBA Admission is based on various criteria such as CAT Scores, Academic Scores, Statement of Purpose, Extempore and Personal Interview. Getting admission to FMS Delhi is not an easy task; it is highly competitive as it's one of the top management institutes in India. Here are some tips on how to prepare for admission:

Prepare for CAT: Admission to FMS Delhi is based on CAT Scores, so you should start preparing for the CAT a year or more before the exam, which gives you enough time to cover the syllabus and practice thoroughly.

Prepare for Extempore and Personal Interview: Apart from CAT scores, FMS Delhi takes Extempore and Personal Interview into consideration. You should prepare for Extempore and PI topics and work on your Communication Skills and Confidence.
Stay Updated: Keep yourself updated with what's happening in the world, like in business, economy, and politics. As it is important for Extempore and PI rounds.
Getting into FMS Delhi requires dedication, great marks, hard work, and good communication skills.
ISB caters to working professionals with more than 2 years of experience. If you do not belong to this category, this institution is not for you.
Now coming to the other options,

The HR program of XLRI is very old and renowned. Because of it, XLRI receives a slightly higher number of recruiters. This boosts its average package. Its limited batch size also benefits its placements. IIMK, FMS and XLRI receive more or less the same companies. But IIMK and XLRI attract MBB (McKinsey, Bain, BCG) for their front end roles, which IIMI and FMS do not.
Considering all these factors, XLRI is the best choice, mainly because of its small batch size. It is followed by IIMK and FMS, and IIM Indore comes last.

As per the official website, the online registration for MBA admissions at FMS Delhi takes place from the second week of September to the second week of December. The announcement of candidates shortlisted for GD+PI is held in the first week of January. The GD and PI rounds take place around March second week, and the course finally commences in the first week of July.
These timelines can vary, but this is the usual pattern for the MBA selection cycle at FMS Delhi.

For MBA admission, FMS bases shortlisting almost on CAT score (with section-wise weightage: VARC 40 %, DILR 30 %, QA 30 %). An extra 5 marks is added for female candidates during shortlisting. Final selection uses a composite score: 50% from CAT, 10% each from Class 10 and 12 marks, 10% from Statement of Purpose, 5% from Extempore, 15% from Personal Interview. Women get +5 bonus marks at the interview stage. For General-category applicants, CAT percentile cut-offs have been very high, 98-99+ percentile to get an interview

QIS College of Engineering and Technology (QISCET) is a private college in Ongole, Prakasam District, Andhra Pradesh, established in 1998 by Sri Nidamanuri Educational Society. The campus offers undergraduate and postgraduate programs in engineering, management, and computer applications. It is affiliated with Jawaharlal Nehru Technological University, Kakinada (JNTUK) and approved by AICTE, NBA, and UGC, with NAAC ‘A+’ accreditation and ISO 9001:2015 certification. The college provides courses like B.Tech, M.Tech, MBA, MCA, and BBA. It is ranked 201-300 in India among B.Tech colleges as per NIRF 2025 rankings.

QISCET is best known for B.Tech courses in 14 specializations, including Computer Science Engineering, Electronics and Communication Engineering, Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Civil Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, and Data Science. The first-year fee for B.Tech is INR 87,600.. Admission to B.Tech requires 10+2 with physics, chemistry, and mathematics, and a valid AP EAMCET score, followed by APSCHE counseling. Previous 2024 cutoff ranks for B.Tech were around 40,000 for Open Category and 70,000 for Backward Classes.
The latest placement data from 2024 shows a total of 824 offers made with the highest package being INR 10 LPA.. Top recruiters include TCS, Infosys, Wipro, Amazon, and Cognizant.

QIS College Of Engineering And Technology (QISCET) offers B.Tech, MBA, MCA, and M.Tech admissions for 2025. For B.Tech, students need 10+2 and must take AP EAMCET. The cutoff is about 40,000 for OC and 70,000 for BC, with 1980 seats available.

For MBA and MCA, students take AP ICET, while M.Tech needs GATE or AP PGECET. There are 90 MBA, 180 MCA, and 18 M.Tech seats. After clearing exams and counseling by APSCHE, students submit documents and pay fees. SC/ST students may get fee cuts. QISCET checks all papers before final admission.

The QISCET placement data in the 2024-2025 academic year shows that 28 companies hired students, making a total of 824 offers. The highest salary offered was INR 10 LPA by DAZN, while most companies offered between 3 to 5 LPA. The company that hired the most students was Tech Mahindra, with 125 offers, followed by Surya Tech Solutions with 97 offers and BYD Auto with 65 offers.

The ECE branch had the highest number of placements with 250 students placed, followed by EEE with 125 students and CSE with 157 students. Other branches like MCA and MBA saw fewer placements, with only 27 and 3 students placed.

This data shows that most students were placed in core engineering branches. Many well-known companies like Infosys, Cognizant, and Deloitte also recruited students. Overall, the placements covered a wide range of courses and companies.

The campus of QIS College of Engineering and Technology (QISCET) is located in Vengamukkapalem, Ongole, Prakasam District, Andhra Pradesh. It covers 13 acres and provides a clean, modern space for students. The college is affiliated with Jawaharlal Nehru Technological University, Kakinada (JNTUK) and approved by AICTE, with NAAC ‘A+’ accreditation and ISO 9001:2015 certification.

QISCET has large classrooms with smart boards and projectors for teaching. The library offers many books, journals, and digital resources, supporting student studies. Computer labs have high-speed internet and Wi-Fi across the campus for research and learning. The college provides hostels for boys and girls with clean rooms, water purifiers, and security. A medical center is available for health needs, and a cafeteria serves meals and snacks.

The campus includes sports facilities like a gym, playgrounds for cricket, volleyball, and basketball, and indoor games. A convenience store and bank/ATM are on-site for daily needs. Transport services with buses connect the campus to nearby areas like Ongole Railway Station (6 km) and APSRTC Bus Stop (5.9 km).

An auditorium with audio-visual tools hosts events and seminars. Laboratories for engineering branches are well-equipped for practical learning. The Training and Placement Cell helps students with career skills and job placements. For more details, visit the QISCET website.

A recent review on Collegedunia posted in 2025 shared “nightlife near the campus is peaceful and safe. students often relax at nearly tea stalls, cafes, or on hostel common areas”. Read the full review
Ques. How is the transport connectivity for QISCET?

Ans. The transport connectivity for QISCET is good. The college is in Vengamukkapalem, Ongole, Andhra Pradesh, near Ongole Railway Station (6 km) and APSRTC Bus Stop (5.9 km). Vijayawada Airport is 170 km away. QISCET provides bus services for students from nearby areas, ensuring safe and timely travel. The campus is easily reached by road, and local transport like autos and taxis is available. Students can also use public buses or trains to travel to Ongole.
Ques. How are the hostel facilities at QISCET?

Ans. QISCET offers hostels for boys and girls on campus. The rooms are clean, spacious, and have basic amenities like beds, fans, and water purifiers. Hostels provide hot water and 24/7 security with cameras. There is a mess serving meals, and the environment is safe. SC/ST students may get free hostel facilities. The hostels have Wi-Fi and study areas. Common rooms have TVs and indoor games. For specific details like fees or rules, students can visit the QISCET website or contact the hostel office directly.
Ques. How does the Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning course at QISCET compare to that in other colleges?

Ans. The B.Tech in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning at QISCET is a four-year program with 60 seats. It covers topics like data science, algorithms, and programming. The fee is around INR 90,000 per year. Other colleges like ABR College and Prakasam Engineering College also offer AI and ML with similar curriculums, but QISCET has NAAC ‘A+’ accreditation, which is higher than Prakasam’s ‘B++’. ABR College charges lower fees (INR 35,000/year) but has fewer seats (60). QISCET’s placement for AI includes companies like TCS and Infosys.
