University College of Engineering (UCE), Osmania University, Hyderabad, is a government engineering college in Telangana. It was established in 1929 and is part of Osmania University, a public university in India. The college is approved by AICTE, and several of its courses are NBA-accredited. It has been awarded an NAAC A+ Grade. UCEOU is also recognized by UGC and is considered one of the top engineering colleges in the state. In 2024, it was ranked in 101-150 Band by NIRF for 159 by Collegedunia in 2025 for B.Tech.

The flagship program offered at UCEOU is the B.E. program in specializations like Computer Science (CSE), Electronics and Communication (ECE), Electrical (EEE), Civil, Mechanical, and Biomedical Engineering. It also offers M.Tech, MCA, and Ph.D. programs. The total fee for B.E. is INR 59,770 - INR 1.3 Lakhs for the first year, while M.Tech fees range between INR 59,770 - INR 69,770 for the first year, depending on whether they are full-time or part-time. Admission to the B.E. course is done through the TS EAMCET exam, and for M.Tech, students are selected through GATE or TS PGECET.

UCEOU has a dedicated placement cell that assists students in securing placements at top companies. In 2025, recruiters from companies such as Amazon, Oracle, Infosys, Juspay, and D.E. Shaw hired students from the campus. The highest package offered was INR 45 LPA, while the average package was INR 10 LPA. The overall placement rate at UCEOU is around 80%.

University College of Engineering (UCE), Osmania University, Hyderabad, has a long history of producing talented and successful graduates. Over the years, many of its alumni have gone on to become leaders in engineering, technology, research, government, and business. These former students have made a strong impact in India and around the world, making the college proud of its rich legacy.
Ques. Is UCEOU Hyderabad a college run by the government?

Ans. Yes. Founded in 1929, UCEOU is Telangana's oldest engineering college and a public government institution. It is run by Osmania University, an NAAC A+ accredited institution with UGC recognition. The college offers engineering and technology undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral programs and has AICTE approval. It is regarded as one of South India's most prominent government engineering schools.
Ques. How knowledgeable and experienced is UCEOU's faculty?

Ans. The faculty at UCEOU is very qualified; many of them have Ph.D.s, have published research papers, and have taught for many years. The faculty frequently participates in industry consulting and government-funded projects. With an emphasis on real-world application, project work, and ongoing evaluations, instruction is student-centered. A number of faculty members also serve as mentors for GATE and Ph.D. candidates.
Ques. Does UCEOU have a dress code or uniform policy?

Ans. At UCEOU, there is no rigid dress code. Respectful and well-groomed attire is encouraged for students. It may be necessary to wear lab coats or formal clothing for specific labs, practicals, or presentations. The college upholds a relaxed yet orderly culture that values each student's uniqueness while promoting professionalism.
Ques. Can students from other countries or NRIs apply to UCEOU?

Ans. Yes, Osmania University's Foreign Relations Office accepts applications from both foreign and non-resident students. Academic transcripts, evidence of English proficiency, and comparable test results must be submitted. After being accepted, they get help with student support, housing, and visas. In the past, the university has accepted students from Southeast Asia, the Middle East, and Africa.

Ques. Is it mandatory to stay in a hostel to pursue courses at GIM Goa?

Ans. Yes, GIM offers both PGDM courses on a full-time and residential basis. Students are required to stay in the hostel. Students get a discount on registration if they register for a hostel as early as possible.
Ques. Are there any reservations for Goan candidates at GIM Goa?

Ans. . GIM doesn't have any reservations for Goan candidates. But for final selections, group discussion, and personal interview, the qualifying cut-off score will be increased by 15 points for the Goan candidates.
Ques. Who can opt for a PGDM part-time course at GIM Goa?
Ans. Those applicants who are working executives with a certain level of work experience can opt for a PGDM part-time course. This course’s classes are held at weekends only.
Ques. What is an Achiever’s Round at GIM Goa?

Ans. Achiever's round at GIM Goa is a profile-based short-listing of candidates based on their self-reported achievements in various fields such as academics, sports, co-curricular, professional experience, etc.
Ques. Is it mandatory to appear for the GIM Goa Entrance Exam for admission into PGDM?
Ans. The GAAT (GIM Analytics Aptitude Test) is mandatory only for those who are interested in taking admission to PGDM BDA and IDA. The other PGDM candidates do not need to appear for GAAT.
Ques. Do I need prior work experience for admission into GIM Goa?

Ans. No, it is not mandatory to have work experience for admission into any of the PGDM programs at GIM Goa. Though the work experience does act as a benefit and has a weightage of around 10% in the final selection.
Ques. Where are interviews conducted from GIM Goa?

Ans. For Achiever’s and Elite round candidates, the Interview centres are located in cities including Bangalore, Goa, Kolkata, Mumbai, and New Delhi. For regular-round candidates, the interview/ selection process will take place online.
Ques. How can I get a scholarship in GIM Goa?

Ans. GIM Goa offers scholarships for all the PGDM program students based on the Academic Competence and Excellence Scholarship Scheme. Each of the scholarships amounts to INR 5 lakhs. These scholarships are only for the students who have secured admission through the Achiever’s round.

IIM Udaipur and GIM Goa offer unique experiences, but they cater to different student preferences. IIM Udaipur boasts a rigorous curriculum similar to top IIMs, with a strong emphasis on research and a vibrant campus life featuring numerous clubs and events. However, placement stats can be a bit underwhelming for a newer IIM. GIM Goa, while not explicitly detailed here, has a reputation for a strong focus on practical learning and industry exposure, making it appealing for those interested in a more hands-on approach. Personally, I would pick IIM Udaipur for its academic rigor and active campus culture, but if you're someone who values practical experience and a laid-back environment, GIM Goa could be the better choice for you.

Yes, pursuing a PGDM from GIM Goa is definitely worth it! They offer a variety of specializations, excellent internship opportunities with reputed companies, and strong placement support. Here are the specializations offered by GIM Goa: FINANCE & ACCOUNTING, GENERAL MANAGEMENT & ECONOMICS, IT & OPERATIONS, MARKETING, and OB & HRM. Goa Institute of Management provides PGDM, PGDM (part-time), and FPM programmes. The PGDM program lasts for two years, while the part-time PGDM takes three years and the FPM spans four years. Once you enroll at GIM Goa, numerous recruitment opportunities arise. Various companies come to recruit students. The top recruiter offering the highest salary was Flipkart. Companies from different sectors participate in the recruitment process. Sector-wise placements include: FMCG, IT, Banking & Finance, Healthcare. New recruiters include: Amazon, HDFC, Flipkart, CRIF, Lowe's Inc, Trident Group. Top recruiters: CRIF, Optum, HSBC Bank, Accenture AI, Tata Capital. Prominent roles offered: Management Trainees in Finance, HR, Supply Chain & Operations, Marketing & Sales, Business Analyst, Data Analyst, Data Scientist, Data Architect, Data Engineering, Cloud.

Being at GIM is like being on a thrilling roller coaster. You get to enjoy your time while also growing and improving as a person. Students at GIM learn how to apply what they learn in books to real-life situations and have plenty of chances to develop themselves, getting ready for the business world.

Life on campus is a great mix of fun and learning. You might start your day with a beautiful sunrise at one of GIM's most scenic spots, then go from classes to club activities, gather with friends at midnight for assignments, and end the day with a coffee at SK's. This daily routine shows the lively and dynamic culture of GIM.

People often say GIM is always buzzing with activity, and it's true. With over 25 student groups actively creating a well-rounded experience, there's always something happening. They host a variety of events, like the Basanti Cup, the biggest sports event, Inception for showcasing talents, and Sale Away for practicing marketing skills. The Cultural Club, Razmatazz, organizes amazing festivals to ensure you never feel homesick. GIM also offers many chances to meet industry experts and learn from them during events like Samriddhi, TEDxGIM, and the Grand Alumni Meet.

Campus life at GIM is vibrant and engaging. There are numerous events and clubs that keep things lively throughout the year. The annual fest, Samriddhi, is one of the highlights, and we have a well-equipped library accessible 24/7. The hostel facilities are decent, with good food and a supportive community. Overall, I feel like I'm getting a comprehensive education here, both academically and socially.
When reviewing a particular school, I like to look at five key areas:

Starting with Faculty & Curriculum: While the curriculum at most business schools is similar, what sets them apart is the quality of their instructors. GIM boasts a faculty-student ratio of 17:1, with highly qualified teachers.
Peer Group: GIM's CAT/XAT cutoff is typically between 85-88, attracting talented and diverse students from various backgrounds and age groups. So, you'll find yourself among a great peer group here.
Infrastructure: GIM has one of the most impressive campuses in West India, with state-of-the-art facilities.
Industry Interaction & Placements: The average salary offer is around 9.5 lakhs, with the highest reaching 16.5 lakhs. This suggests that the placement opportunities are quite solid.
Alumni: GIM's alumni network is strong, with graduates working in various industries and roles. This is definitely a plus for the institute.

Other Factors: GIM is AACSB accredited and has international exchange programs with institutions like the University of Antwerp in Belgium, Católica-Lisbon School in Portugal, Warsaw University of Technology Business School in Poland, and Hochschule Ingolstadt in Germany.

GIM also collaborates with the University of Antwerp for an internship program called The Joint International Internship Seminar (JIIS). This is a two-week intensive program in September where students from both Belgium and GIM tackle real management issues in Goa, offering a great cross-cultural experience.

To enhance global perspectives and cross-border engagement, GIM provides basic foreign language courses in French, Portuguese, German, and Spanish. These are offered in partnership with local cultural organizations.
In conclusion, GIM is definitely one of the top Tier 3 colleges in India. Hope this helps!

Student life at Goa Institute of Management is vibrant and full of opportunities. With events happening almost every month, there’s always something to look forward to. The campus is beautiful, and the library is open 24/7, which is a huge plus for late-night study sessions.

There are around 23 clubs that run various activities, from sports to cultural events, ensuring that students are engaged beyond academics. Plus, the student-faculty ratio is great, allowing for personalized attention from professors who are very knowledgeable. Overall, it's a blend of rigorous academics and a lively campus atmosphere.

The placement scenario for the Post Graduate Diploma in Management (Big Data Analytics) at GIM is really strong. Our batch had a 100% placement record, and the highest CTC was 42 lakhs, with many roles related to data analysis and consultancy. The college also has a solid internship program, which helped us gain practical experience through live projects. Companies from various sectors come to recruit, and the support from the placement committee is fantastic. I feel prepared for the job market, thanks to the training and opportunities provided here.

You might not be a fan of math or programming, yet you're thinking about doing an MBA in Analytics. This field definitely involves working with numbers and programming, and it seems like you've chosen it for its job prospects and salary potential. Here's the thing: math and programming are key skills in analytics, especially if you're aiming for high-paying roles. If you're not into math or coding, you'll need to reconsider, because success here means embracing those skills. If that's not your thing, there are plenty of other well-paying jobs that don't require math or programming.

I worked for 4.5 years in HR at HCL Technologies in the IT sector and now I am doing a PGDM in Big Data Analytics at the Goa Institute of Management. Life at GIM is awesome. Even though the Big Data Analytics program is only two years old, the curriculum is well-organized and meets industry standards. The number of seats has already doubled in a year, showing how successful the course is.

GIM uses a case-based teaching method. Students tackle real-world business scenarios and are expected to come up with solutions. Besides these cases, they get access to actual business data, using it to apply different analytical tools and models. For this, we have top-notch facilities, including a fully equipped Data Lab and teaching support. Plus, experienced BDA professionals and industry experts teach parts of the courses to bring real-world insights into the classroom. We also collaborate with SAS India, so instructors from SAS Institute come to teach us analytics topics.

Beyond academics, the Big Data Analytics students have the same opportunities as those in other PGDM programs at GIM. For more details, you can visit the Goa Institute of Management, one of India's leading management schools, located in Goa, India.

I think Goa Institute of Management (GIM) is a better choice than Fore IB for the Post Graduate Diploma in Management. The faculty here is really knowledgeable and experienced, with a student-faculty ratio of around 1:12, which allows for more personalized attention. Plus, GIM has a strong focus on case study learning, making the exams quite challenging but applicable to real-world scenarios. Also, GIM boasts a 100% placement record, with companies like Microsoft and HDFC Bank coming for final placements, which is pretty impressive.

Ques: Does MCC Chennai College offer scholarship opportunities?

Ans: Madras Christian College, Chennai, offers a comprehensive range of scholarship opportunities designed to support students from diverse backgrounds. The scholarship at MCC Chennai focuses on financially disadvantaged students, first-generation graduate students from underrepresented communities, including SC, ST, and MBC students under the sports quota, as well as academically excellent students. There is a dedicated department for extension and facilitating educational loans and part-time employment opportunities for students in need.
Ques: Ques: What is campus life at MCC Chennai?

While I appreciate St. Joseph's College, I have to mention PSG Arts and Science College in Coimbatore as a solid option too. The Bachelor of Computer Applications [BCA] course there offers a well-structured curriculum and the faculty is quite experienced. The college also arranges internships with well-known companies, which is crucial for job readiness. The fees are manageable, making it accessible for many students. They also have various clubs and activities that make campus life enjoyable. Both colleges have their strengths, but the choice really depends on what you're looking for.

If you're all about diving deep into your studies, Loyola College is the place to be. But if you're looking to grow personally and become more well-rounded, Madras Christian College offers that transformation. You might start at MCC as a kid, but you'll walk out as a true Gentleman.

Among these, Loyola College Chennai is the superior college. It has a central location, at the heart of Chennai. Loyola is widely reputed especially for Visual Communication courses. The college has a dedicated pool of faculty. As a student of the institute, you will have access to good learning resources and facilities. It has a good placement record as well. During Loyola College placements 2021, students received an average CTC of INR 5.25 LPA.
You should choose Loyola College. It is considered among the best colleges in Tamil Nadu and offers good academics. The institute has strict rules in place regarding academics and attendance.
Loyola has a well-maintained 99 acres campus in the middle of the city. There are good hangout places near the campus.
Loyola College Chennai placements have been good over the years. During the 2021 placement drive, students received an average CTC of around INR 5.25 LPA.

Madras Christian College doesn’t have a strict dress code. The management instructs students to dress decently. Students are allowed to wear semi-formals. The dress code also depends on the department. Some departments are liberal while some departments are strict. Usually, girls aren’t allowed to wear sleeveless dresses or skirts.

I have friends from all three institutes. According to their experience, I will say St. Joseph College Trichy is a better option. It has good infrastructural facilities and a decent library. The faculties are decent. The college has strict rules regarding attendance. A minimum of 80% subject-wise attendance is necessary.

One of my friends studied at SJC College Trichy. He completed his Post Graduation in Botany from this college. He is still proud of his time as a student at SJC. Here are some facts about the college you should know.

Most of my friend’s classmates became teachers, and they are doing well. The students absorbed not only knowledge but also values. He still recalls and adores his professors because he feels he owes them a debt of gratitude.
There is not much difference when we talk about the course and the subjects but the environment is significantly different for both. Here are some things that you should know about the institutes.

Freedom- MCC offers a lot of freedom to its students in the way they dress and express themselves as compared to Loyola. Even for attendance, it is not as strict as Loyola. Loyola asks its students to pay for condonation and then sit for an exam.
Ragging- It is still very much prevalent at MCC and sometimes it crosses the healthy limit as well. On the other hand, ragging is very rare at Loyola.
Drug scene- MCC is infamous for its drug-related incidents. While enrolling their children, parents are quite worried about this. On the other hand, Loyola does not have such a problem.
Campus- Both the campuses are extremely beautiful with an amazing experience of studying in the college.

College life- When it comes to cultural and extracurricular activities, MCC is more active as compared to Loyola. They conduct a lot of fests and different events which offer its students a lot of opportunities.
Here is a brief overview of the institutes.

Therefore, it depends completely on what you want out of your college. If you want a good college life then you should opt for MCC. But if you want good academics then you should opt for Loyola. MCC has a diversified culture whereas Loyola has students mostly from Chennai.

Hyderabad Institute of Technology and Management (HITAM) is a private, autonomous college established in 2001 in Medchal, Telangana. It was formerly known as the Royal College of Engineering. It is affiliated with Jawaharlal Nehru Technological University (JNTUH) and approved by AICTE, New Delhi. Hitam has been accredited A+ by NAAC and NBA. According to the IIRF ranking, HITAM was ranked 59th out of 173 colleges in 2024. In 2025, HITAM was ranked 70th out of 175 colleges by The Times of India.

HITAM offers UG courses such as B.Tech, B.Tech (Lateral), and the Integrated Twinning Program. B.Tech is the flagship course. The total fee for the 4-year B.Tech program is INR 3.6 Lakh. Admission to the B.Tech program is based on entrance exams like TS EAMCET. Seats are allotted based on the scores in these exams through a counselling process, and students must meet the cutoff set by the college to be eligible for admission.

The Integrated Twining Program is a unique course where the students get to study both B.Tech and MS within five years. Under this program, students will have to study a 3-year B.Tech course in India and complete their final year, followed by one more year to get an MS at a partner university in the USA.

Hyderabad Institute of Technology & Management provides various “Incoming Freshman Scholarships” to students. These scholarships are designed to acknowledge and reward students for their academic accomplishments, leadership abilities, and financial needs, ensuring that a diverse range of deserving students can benefit from the educational opportunities at HITAM.

Ques. Is there any company-sponsored category for admission to FORE School of Management?

Ans. Yes, candidates applying under the Company-Sponsored Category need to download the specified format from the website. After downloading the format, fill it up, get it signed and then submit the form to the college.

FORE School of Management has its pros and cons when it comes to the PGDM program. The course curriculum is well-structured, with a good mix of theoretical and practical knowledge. The faculty is experienced, and getting exposure to real-world applications is a plus. The placement record is impressive, with a reported 100% placement rate and salaries reaching as high as 41 LPA for top performers.

However, I found the campus to be quite small, which limits social life and extracurricular activities. The fees are on the higher side, around 18 lakhs, which might be a concern for some students. If you prioritize placement and faculty quality, it’s a solid option, but the campus experience might leave something to be desired.

I'm currently studying at FORE School of Management, part of the 2015–17 batch. FORE has been around for 25 years, offering a unique approach to management education. Most of the faculty, about 84%, hold PhDs, and 87% have experience in the corporate world. Students and faculty travel to either Singapore or Hong Kong to gain an international business outlook. The college collaborates with Nanyang Technological University in Singapore, and the lectures we attended there for a week were really insightful.

Being located in South Delhi, FORE provides great opportunities for students to connect with companies based in Delhi and Gurgaon. Some of the major recruiters include Deloitte, EY, PwC, Cognizant, Infosys, and Tata Motors, among others.

Besides the International Immersion Programme in Singapore, the college offers a student exchange program during the third trimester. This program allows students to study at ESC Rennes School of Business in France, providing a chance to learn about business practices in different countries and cultures.
Feel free to add anything I might have overlooked.

As a student in the PGDM (Big Data Analytics), I find this program aligns well with current industry demands. The faculty is highly qualified, mostly holding PhDs, which adds immense value to our learning experience. The curriculum is updated regularly, and exams occur every two months, keeping us on our toes.

Placements are impressive with an average package of around 14-15 lakhs, and companies like Deloitte and EY visit frequently. The only downside is the fee structure, which is about 17 lakhs, but I believe the ROI justifies it.

I think going for an MBA from FORE School of Management can be a solid choice despite having bad academics. The Post Graduate Diploma in Management (Big Data Analytics) has a curriculum that aligns well with current industry needs, and the faculty is highly qualified. The placements are impressive, with an average package around 14-15 LPA, and many top companies visit the campus for recruitment.

Even if I had a rough academic background, I would focus on my internships and projects to build my profile. The dual specialization option at FORE would also help me explore different fields, which can be advantageous in the job market.

As someone who graduated from FORE School of Management, I can say it's a pretty solid business school. The placements are quite strong, with a high number of students securing jobs. However, the average salary package might not be as high as some expect; a savvy student might land a package of about 8 lakh per year.

The faculty is a bit uneven, with stronger professors in marketing than in finance. If you're aiming for a hardcore finance job, you might want to adjust your expectations. Overall, it's a good choice for folks with 0-2 years of experience.

I’m on the academic conference council at this institute and also help with admissions. Recently, a parent sent us an email that really hit the nail on the head. The senior management is made up of older folks from government backgrounds who seem out of touch with today's world. They aren’t business leaders and don’t get the corporate scene. The board is more interested in money, and the current director feels powerless, like Manmohan Singh without Sonia Gandhi’s say-so. While the education is top-notch, the school’s corporate ties are weakening each year.

To the Fore Team, I’m happy to say my daughter got into Fore School of Management this year. As a former Naval Officer who served the country, I hope my thoughts are taken seriously. I'm unsure if my daughter should attend Fore. My nephew, an alum, is embarrassed about what the college has become. Here are some concerns from her and her friends, hoping for answers and improvements. Owning mistakes and being ethical is a core management lesson.
Swift action could correct these mistakes if I’ve opened any eyes. After writing this, I’ve decided not to send my daughter to this institute. Best of luck.

For the PGDM in Big Data Analytics, the placement figures are quite encouraging as well. The college claims to have 100% placement, with the average salary around 15 LPA and the highest package going up to 24 LPA. I’ve seen companies like EY and Deloitte coming for placements, which is a solid sign for those in analytics. The curriculum is good and aligns well with industry needs, making it a worthwhile choice for anyone interested in data analytics.

I’m currently pursuing PGDM in Big Data Analytics at Fore, and I find it quite rewarding. The course curriculum is up to date with industry standards, and the faculty are very experienced, mostly PhD holders. The fees are around 17 lakhs, which we pay in four installments.

The placement record is impressive, with an average package of around 14-15 LPA. Companies like Deloitte and EY come for placements, which is a huge plus. Internships are also a key part of the program, and I managed to secure a decent one that pays around 30k per month. Overall, if you're interested in analytics and want a solid return on investment, I’d say it's a good choice.

I think Goa Institute of Management (GIM) is a better choice than Fore IB for the Post Graduate Diploma in Management. The faculty here is really knowledgeable and experienced, with a student-faculty ratio of around 1:12, which allows for more personalized attention. Plus, GIM has a strong focus on case study learning, making the exams quite challenging but applicable to real-world scenarios. Also, GIM boasts a 100% placement record, with companies like Microsoft and HDFC Bank coming for final placements, which is pretty impressive.

Bharati Vidyapeeth's College of Architecture, Pune, under the aegis of Bharati Vidyapeeth (Deemed to be University) is a premier leading institution of architectural excellence and innovation. The college is located at the Dhankawadi Campus on Pune-Satara Road, Both B.V. College of Architecture is approved by the Council of Architecture (COA) and affiliated to MSBTE. The college has a reputation for being progressive and academic, which has resulted in offering a program on Sustainable Interior Design, to inspire architect to be more thoughtful when designing their interior designs.

The institution provides a number of undergraduate and postgraduate programs covering many disciplines of science, design, engineering, law, management and the health sciences, allowing students to choose learning pathways relevant to their career aspirational and self- enhancement pursuits, in a global context.

The admission procedures are regulated through a Common Entrance Test (CET) for undergraduate/ post-graduate/ PhD, with an emphasis on fairness, transparency and honor in selection process for both domestic and overseas candidates.
The Institute offers scholarships, on merit and need basis, for deserving and economical students to support inclusive education and academic excellence.

The institution has received national and international accolades for academic excellence, innovation and sustainable practices, lending to the assumptions that it is top of the class if equated with others in the education sector.

With placement assistance supports in the majority of industries, graduates are receiving offers from some of the highest reputable organizations within the sectors, demonstrating the institution's wonderful industry relationships and the readiness for future careers.

Ans. This will include UG Certificate, UG Diploma, UG Degree and UG Degree with Honors depending on number of year(s) completed.

Chaitanya Bharathi Institute of Technology (CBIT) in Hyderabad, established in 1979, is a well-regarded institution affiliated with Osmania University and approved by AICTE. In the CBIT Ranking 2024, NIRF placed CBIT in the 151-200 band out of 300 institutions in the engineering category. Additionally, India Today ranked CBIT 33rd out of 253 engineering colleges across the nation in 2024.

CBIT offers a BTech program at the undergraduate level, under various specializations. To be eligible for admission, candidates must have completed their 10+2 education with Mathematics, Physics, and Chemistry as core subjects, achieving a minimum of 45% aggregate marks from a recognized board. Selection for the BTech program is based on scores from the TS-EAMCET or JEE Main exams. For 2024, the TS-EAMCET cutoff for popular BTech specializations was 8813 for Artificial Intelligence (AI) and 9565 for Information Technology (IT). The total course fee for the BTech program at CBIT is INR 5.6 lakhs.

Currently in-progress, CBIT Placements 2025 witnessed the placement of 1004 eligible candidates. CBIT highest package was offered at INR 51 LPA by Microsoft PPO. Some of the top recruiters here included Infosys, Accenture, Oracle, Bank of America, Cognizant, and Joyalukkas.

CBIT Hyderabad Placements 2025 are currently ongoing. A total of 1004 jobs have been offered to candidates so far. CBIT highest package stood at INR 51 LPA, offered by Microsoft PPO. The maximum number of jobs have been offered to candidates from the Computer Science & Engineering branch. The leading recruiter, so far, at CBIT Hyderabad is Accenture, recruiting a total of 103 candidates.

Patnam Kamal Basha, a BE CSE student at CBIT Hyderabad reports that students become eligible for the campus placements typically in their third year of the undergraduate program.The placement process is facilitated by the career development center which coordinates with companies to arrange recruitments. Companies that offered jobs at CBIT include Infosys, Wipro, TCS, JP Morgan Chase and Co, Hindustan Unilever, Oracle etc. CBIT Hyderabad average package is around INR 6-7 LPA, approximately.

Ques. Which is better - CBIT Hyderabad or VIT Vellore?

Ans. Students and alumni claim that a local college in Hyderabad would not be able to give one exposure, like an institute like VIT Vellore. VIT is an established college, with good international tie-ups. It provides good exposure at VIP compared to CBIT. Even if you look at placements, the opportunities are better than CBIT Hyderabad. VIT is a better bet than CBIT for Masters too. Chances of enhancing your profile and skillset at VIT is better than CBIT, where it's a struggle to do so.
Ques. How are hostel rooms allotted at CBIT Hyderabad?

Ans. The campus accommodates two students’ residential blocks that accommodate Senior students (II, III, and IV Years, PG) and Junior students (I Years). Both the blocks are separated distantly. The Juniors Block has 20 rooms of equal dimensions with occupancy of 200 students in total. The Seniors Block has 80 rooms with occupancy of 320 students. In a nutshell, 520 students in toto are able to be accommodated in these two blocks. The separation of Juniors Block and Seniors block is due mainly to curb any ragging related act.
Ques. Does CBIT Hyderabad follow a dress code?

Ans. Students at CBIT Hyderabad should come to the institute in a presentable and decent attire. For the workshops and laboratories, they should wear appropriate uniforms as prescribed and should be aware that long and open (unclipped) hair may make them vulnerable for accidents. Male students should wear shirts and full pants in general and they may wear any decent traditional dress with the approval of the authority. Female students should in general wear salwar kameez/chudithar with dupatta /full sari and they may also wear any decent traditional dress with the approval of the authority.

Thus, do not choose the NCR campus of SRM University, especially for the CSE program.

When considering KJ Somaiya, BIM Trichy, and GIM for your higher education, it can be challenging to determine which institute is the best fit for you. Each institute has its unique strengths and advantages that make them desirable options.
Here are some key factors to consider when evaluating KJ Somaiya, BIM Trichy, and GIM:

All three institutes offer high-quality education and a diverse range of programs in various fields. They emphasize practical learning and equip students with the necessary skills to excel in their chosen field.

KJ Somaiya is located in Mumbai, which is one of India's most vibrant and dynamic cities. It provides excellent networking opportunities, exposure to various industries, and access to a vast alumni network. BIM Trichy is situated in Trichy, which is a fast-developing industrial city with access to many prominent companies. GIM is located in Goa, which is a popular tourist destination and has a thriving business community.

All three institutes have a strong reputation for producing highly skilled and competent graduates. They have a robust placement process, with many reputed companies visiting the campuses for recruitment.

Each institute has its unique campus infrastructure and facilities that enhance the learning experience of students. KJ Somaiya and GIM have state-of-the-art campuses with modern facilities, while BIM Trichy has a well-established campus that caters to the needs of its students.

The faculty at all three institutes is highly qualified and experienced, with many members having significant industry experience. They provide excellent guidance and mentorship to students, helping them develop their skills and capabilities. Additionally, each institute has a strong research culture, providing students with opportunities to work on cutting-edge research projects.

When evaluating the above factors, it's essential to keep your personal goals, interests, and financial constraints in mind. While KJ Somaiya may offer the advantage of being located in Mumbai, providing better opportunities, BIM Trichy and GIM may have unique features and advantages that align better with your career aspirations.

In conclusion, while KJ Somaiya, BIM Trichy, and GIM are all excellent institutes, it's crucial to conduct thorough research and evaluation to make an informed decision that aligns with your career goals and aspirations.

XAT or Xavier Aptitude Test is a national-level entrance exam conducted by XLRI, Jamshedpur for admission to management programs offered by more than 150 B-schools across India, including SP Jain Institute of Management and Research (SPJIMR), K J Somaiya Institute of Management Studies and Research, Institute of Management Technology Ghaziabad (IMT Ghaziabad), T A Pai Management Institute (TAPMI), and FORE School of Management.

Each of these B-schools has its own XAT cutoff score based on factors such as the number of applicants, the difficulty level of the exam, and the availability of seats. Generally, the XAT cutoff scores for these B-schools range between the 80 to 90 percentile.

It's important to note that while cutoff scores are an important factor in the admission process, they are not the only factor. Other factors, such as your academic background, work experience, extracurricular activities, and performance in other selection rounds, also play a crucial role in the admission process. So, it's always a good idea to aim for a high score in XAT and prepare well for other selection rounds to increase your chances of admission to the MBA program of your choice.

If you have the financial means to do so, it would be wise to choose Xavier Institute of Management Bhubaneswar (XIMB) over KJ Somaiya Executive Program for a full-time executive MBA. While KJ Somaiya can offer assistance with placement opportunities, they do not provide on-campus placements, meaning you will need to find job opportunities on your own.

XIMB has a strong brand value and has completed 100% placement for its MBA program in 2022 with a 16% increase in average salary, which rose to Rs. 17.54 LPA from Rs. 15.15 LPA the previous year. While KJ Somaiya Institute of Management MBA placements 2023 had a 92% placement rate and attracted 132 companies, the highest and average packages offered stood at INR 22.50 LPA and INR 12.48 LPA, respectively. Sectors such as banking, IT, and financial services were the top recruiting sectors during the placements.

Loyola College Chennai is an autonomous institution founded in 1925. The institute has been awarded the status of “College of Excellence” by UGC and is accredited with an 'A++' grade by NAAC. It is affiliated with University of Madras. Loyola College Chennai is ranked 14th in the College category by NIRF 2025, and placed 5th in Commerce and 6th in Science by Collegedunia.

It offers popular B.Sc and M.Sc programs under a two-shift system. UG admissions are based on 10+2 marks, while PG admissions require a relevant bachelor’s degree followed by GD/PI. Loyola College fees are category-based: UG fees vary by board (HSC, CBSE/ISC, others), and PG fees differ for University of Madras graduates and students from other universities.
For Shift I, M.Sc (Madras University students) costs about INR 13,740-INR 15,150 for the 1st semester, while B.Sc (HSC board) costs INR 14,910-INR 21,040, depending on the specialisation.
Loyola College Chennai reported strong placement outcomes, with the highest package of INR 22.5 LPA and an average package of INR 6.34 LPA, according to the Placement Brochure 2024.
Online application portal for admission to UG programs (2026-27) will open on the day the Tamil Nadu 12th board results are announced. Here is a likely timeline based on the latest available dates.

Note: Students must complete the online registration within 10 days of the Tamil Nadu 10+2 result announcement. For other boards, registration should be done within 3 days of their result announcement.

Loyola College admits undergraduates solely on a merit basis, while PG candidates must take an additional entrance exam consisting of GD and/or PI, administered by the university. The curriculum of the popular Data Science (M.Sc) program is well-rounded with intensive laboratory work, industry talks, and case studies. The other popular courses, such as BCA and BBA, have updated curriculum, aligned with the academics as well as industrial developments in the relevant fields.
For SHIFT 2 Courses and Fees, check: Loyola College Courses & Fees

The college also offers PhD in Economics, Commerce, History, English, Zoology, Physics and Chemistry. There are two active Diploma and PG Diploma programs as well, in the School of Film Studies and Management, respectively.

Loyola College Chennai conducts admissions for UG, PG, and doctoral programs through a fully online process, with the application portal typically opening after the release of Tamil Nadu 10+2 results for UG courses.

Admissions are primarily merit-based. UG candidates are shortlisted based on their Class 12 (10+2) marks, while PG admissions are based on graduation scores and may include entrance tests, group discussions and / or PI for select programs.

To apply, candidates must register on the official portal, choose their course, fill in personal and academic details, upload required documents, and pay the application fee. A unique application number is generated to track the admission status online.

Shortlisted candidates are offered provisional admission, which becomes final after document verification and payment of the admission fee. Applicants required to appear for entrance tests are notified separately after submitting their application.

It offers facilities such as spacious classrooms, well-equipped laboratories, sports complex, library with a reading room and digital database, separate hostel accommodations for boys and girls, and a canteen.

Ques. Are mobile phones allowed inside Loyola College Chennai ?

Ans. No. Electronic gadgets such as mobile phone, ipad, ipod,smart watches are prohibited inside Loyola College campus. Students are also discouraged to travel around the camous in their personal vehicles. Any such vehicle, if used to commute by a student, is to be parked at the parking area inside the campus.
Ques. Is there any dress code / uniform at Loyola College Chennai ?

Ans. While Loyola College Chennai doesn’t require students to wear uniforms, they are needed to dress in a way that’s suitable to the academic environment of the college. Girls are required to wear decenly cut salwaar kameez while boys should sport formals. Neat and tidy appearance is also mandated by the college.
Ques. What are the attendance regulations at Loyola College Chennai?

Ans. Loyola College Chennai mandates an attendance of 75% in each subject in a semester to be eligible for the final examination. Barring special cases such as health issue related absence, absence of a differently abled student caused by any difficulty, no consideration is extented to any defaulter.
Ques. What are the shift timings at Loyola College?

Ans. Loyola College conducts classes in two shifts : Morning Shift (8:15 AM – 1:15 PM) for students working part time after college hours and Afternoon Shift (1:30 PM – 6:30 PM) for students capable of financing their education without any assistance from the college.
Ques. Is Loyola College co-ed?

Ans. Loyola College is a partially co - educational instituition. Some of its courses are co-ed, while others admit male candidates only. For instance, the UG courses at the department of Commerce admit only male students. However, the college has separate hostels for boys and girls to accomodate students belonging to both genders.
Ques. Does Loyola College provide scholarships to differently abled students?
Ans. Yes. Loyola College alumni base lends financial aid to differently abled students under the college’s Student Support Service program.

I'm currently a first-year B.A. (Economics) student at St Joseph’s University in Bangalore, previously known as St Joseph’s College. I've got some insights from my seniors who have graduated. In my opinion, Loyola College in Chennai is one of India's top Jesuit institutions. It's consistently ranked among the top 10 colleges in India by NIRF and offers a wide range of courses in Humanities, Science, and Management. It mainly caters to men, though some courses are open to women.

St Joseph’s University, also a Jesuit institution in Bangalore, has a strong reputation here. It's known for its rich legacy of over 120 years and a strong alumni network. As a co-ed college, it has a balanced mix of male and female students. The university is highly regarded for its Humanities, Science, and B.Voc programs, among other courses. While it may not be as famous outside Bangalore, it remains a prestigious institution in the city and across India.

When it comes to placements, both colleges provide good opportunities. Loyola College, Chennai tends to have a higher placement rate due to its nationwide recognition. St Joseph’s also offers solid placements, although slightly less compared to Loyola, but much depends on individual student performance.

To sum up, both institutions are well-respected Jesuit colleges in India with excellent faculty. Whether you choose Loyola or St Joseph’s, you'll receive not only academic excellence but also holistic development and character building. Both colleges have strong placement records and send their students to top companies.

Loyola College is quite well-known outside Tamil Nadu, especially in major cities like Mumbai and Delhi. Many people regard it as one of the top colleges in India. As a student of the Bachelor of Commerce (B.Com), I've experienced a lot of pride in my college's reputation.

The placement opportunities here are impressive, with companies like Deloitte and TCS recruiting students, which adds to its recognition beyond Tamil Nadu. The college has a strong alumni network that contributes positively to its reputation in other states.

It really comes down to your perspective. Loyola College offers a fair amount of freedom, but they do have a bit of an annoying rule against using camera phones. If you're aiming for courses like chartered accountancy, you might want to consider somewhere else, like Vivekananda, which offers better support for that field. The student community is great, and the faculty is pretty decent too. There are tons of opportunities for club activities and other Co curriculars if that's what you're into. The attendance policy is more relaxed compared to other colleges. Plus, having Loyola on your resume is a nice perk. Hope this helps!

Loyola College is known for its strict environment, particularly concerning academics. In my Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) course, we have a rigorous exam structure where attendance is closely monitored. You need to maintain a certain percentage to sit for exams, and they are pretty serious about ensuring students follow these rules.
It can be challenging, especially if you're juggling extracurriculars and studies, but it helps instill a sense of discipline.

I got 87% in the Tamil Nadu State Board exams and was really eager to study mathematics at Loyola College, even though my math score wasn't the best. I decided to apply for physics, mathematics, and chemistry, hoping to get into at least one of them. To my surprise, I got shortlisted for both physics and mathematics. I was over the moon and joined Loyola in 2016, and I stayed happy throughout my time there. Loyola isn't just a college; it's so much more.
Sure thing! Just include a self-signed copy of your parent's bank passbook when you apply, and you'll be good to go.

Loyola College is particularly notable for its Bachelor of Commerce (B.Com) program, which is designed to prepare students for real-world challenges. The faculty are mostly experienced professionals, and the teaching methods include using modern digital tools. The internship opportunities are robust, with students required to complete internships in their third year, which greatly enhances employability.

The fee structure is also quite affordable, especially for the government-aided shift, making it accessible for many students. Overall, the college provides a holistic experience that balances academics with cultural events and personal development.

If you're all about diving deep into your studies, Loyola College is the place to be. But if you're looking to grow personally and become more well-rounded, Madras Christian College offers that transformation. You might start at MCC as a kid, but you'll walk out as a true Gentleman.

I chose Loyola College for my Bachelor of Commerce (B.Com) degree mainly because of its reputation. The course is rigorous, with a good mix of theory and practical applications, but the faculty is very supportive, which makes it manageable. Regular exams and internal assessments keep us engaged and motivated.

The campus life is vibrant, with plenty of clubs and activities, and the annual fest is a highlight of the year. I've also noticed good placement opportunities, which is a big plus for me as I prepare for my career ahead.

Some negative aspects of Loyola College Chennai, particularly in the Bachelor of Commerce [B.Com] program, include the outdated curriculum. The syllabus often lacks relevance to modern business practices, especially in areas like digital marketing and advanced accounting software. This can hinder students' preparedness for the job market, making it difficult for them to compete with peers from other institutions. Additionally, while the faculty is generally well-qualified, some professors may not effectively engage students, leading to a less interactive learning environment.

Another concern is the high fee structure for the Bachelor of Commerce [B.Com] program. While the college has a reputation for excellence, the financial burden can be significant for many students. Despite the availability of scholarships, the criteria can be stringent, and not all students benefit from them. This can create a financial strain, especially for those from lower-income families.

Lastly, campus life has its downsides too. While events like "Ovations" are engaging, some students feel that there could be more inclusivity in extracurricular activities. The pressure to participate in various clubs and events can sometimes feel overwhelming, detracting from the overall college experience. The infrastructure, although extensive, may not always meet students' expectations in terms of maintenance and facilities, which can affect their daily life on campus.

Caltech isn't very well-rounded. If you think life is all about science and math, you’ll love it. But if you want to meet new people, explore a city, learn about art and culture, or try new things, you might find it lacking. It takes a lot of effort to have those experiences since the environment doesn’t naturally support them. There's a lot more to life than just science and math, but I didn't learn much about that at Caltech.

The network is small and very focused. In the business world, not many people know about Caltech. It’s much easier for a Stanford grad to get hired. Caltech’s network is strong but mostly in academia and research, which means fewer opportunities in other fields.

Social skills are a bit lacking. Caltech folks are a bit different and tend to stay in their own group. This comfort and introversion make for an awkward social scene, and these habits continue into the real world, making it harder to connect with others in business or dating.

Numbers are unavoidable: Many assume they can skip math and accounting in a communications course, but MICA involves lots of number crunching and statistics, especially in quantitative market research.
Embrace diversity: At MICA, you’ll meet people who think, speak, and act differently than you, from socializing to expressing themselves. Be prepared to accept and appreciate these differences.
Sleep will be scarce: Whether due to assignments or the lively nighttime atmosphere filled with long conversations and independence, MICA will keep you up more than you might like.
Stay true to yourself: Peer pressure can be strong, but it’s important to stick to your own beliefs. Even if you’re more reserved, you can still have a great time at MICA (if you catch my drift).

The campus of MICA Ahmedabad is 19 acres of lush green space with Wi-Fi and accommodations for students with disabilities. The campus features state-of-the-art amenities such as computer labs with 24-hour internet access, fully air-conditioned classrooms with contemporary teaching aids, and a well-stocked library that is open around-the-clock.

Along with a canteen, laundry facilities, and round-the-clock internet, the MICA Ahmedabad hostel offers separate hostel facilities for boys and girls that offer twin-sharing and single rooms. Ques. What is the admission process for MICA Ahmedabad?

Ans. Entrance exams such as the CAT, XAT, and GMAT are part of the MICA Ahmedabad admissions process. The MICAT exam, Group Exercise (GE), and Personal Interview (PI) appear next. Candidates are chosen on the basis of how well they perform overall during these phases. These parameters have the following weights: GE (10%), MICAT (25%), CAT/XAT/GMAT (35%), and PI (20%). Candidates must register on the official website, pay the application fee, upload the necessary documents, and confirm their email address and mobile number.
Ques. What courses are offered at MICA Ahmedabad?

Ans. Post Graduate Diploma in Management (PGDM), Post Graduate Diploma in Management Communication (PGDM-C), Post Graduate Certificate Program in Crafting Creative Communication (CCC), and Fellow Program in Management (FPM) are among the programs that MICA Ahmedabad offers. The goal of these programs is to develop innovative and strategic leaders in domains such as digital marketing, brand management, and advertising.
Ques. What is the fee structure for MICA Ahmedabad?
Ans. The entire cost of the PGDM program at MICA, including all applicable fees, is roughly INR 28 lakhs. Depending on the course and program, the cost structure may change.
Ques. What is the placement scenario at MICA Ahmedabad?

Ans. With an average package of INR 19.22 LPA and a maximum package of INR 40.91 LPA, MICA Ahmedabad has a 100% placement record. Google, Amazon, Deloitte, and Cognizant are among the top recruiters. Given the institute's solid industry ties, students are able to land high-paying job offers.
Ques. Does MICA Ahmedabad offer scholarships?

Ans. Yes, Scholarships from MICA Ahmedabad are awarded based on renowned results, family income, and academic standing. For PGDM and PGDM-C, the scholarship pays up to 100% of tuition; for equity scholarships, it offers INR 5 lakhs. Furthermore, FPM students are given a monthly stipend that starts at INR 38,000 and rises to INR 41,000 in their third and fourth years.
Ques. What is the campus life like at MICA Ahmedabad?

Ans. The 19-acre campus of MICA Ahmedabad offers a peaceful and lush environment. Wi-Fi, air-conditioned classrooms, a sports complex, a library, a gym, a cafeteria, a hostel, and medical facilities are among the contemporary conveniences available on campus. Extracurricular activities are encouraged by the institute, and events are planned all year long by a number of student-run committees.
Ques. Is MICA accredited by any recognized bodies?

Ans. Yes, MICA has received approval from the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) and accreditation from the National Board of Accreditation (NBA). According to the Association of Indian Universities (AIU), the institute's PGDM program is equivalent to an MBA degree.

I always felt a bit out of place at Caltech, so I find it easy to talk about its drawbacks.

First off, I don't see how tough Caltech is as a negative. You're picking one of the toughest schools around, and graduating from there means you're pretty impressive. If you think about attending a top university, you'll realize it's not easy to train leading research scientists. Caltech is upfront about how challenging it is, which is probably why its acceptance rate is higher compared to other top schools. People aren't exactly excited to hear about the intense workload. It’s much easier to say, “Come to the happiest place on Earth!”

I know some really smart folks who studied for at least 8 hours a day, and I mean serious studying, not just hanging out. If you consider that, it’s a lot of time spent hitting the books. Honestly, I’m not sure how I graduated. Whenever I meet other grads, I think, “Wow, you must be amazing!” If I were just a regular person, I might say, “Cal Poly? Cool! My cousin goes there!” But I often have to run off, jokingly saying, “Oops, my pool’s on fire again!”

As for dating, it’s not a big deal for me. The male-to-female ratio is about 7:3, and even if no one told you, it's pretty clear dating might be tough. Spending all day in your room or playing video games doesn’t help. It’s just how things are with the numbers and workload. I recall someone asking me my major and joking about it being for the girls. I played along, but it was clear they weren’t serious.
In my view, a downside is something a new college student might not really think about but could affect their growth.
Here are some downsides:
These can be issues, but Caltech teaches us that with enough time, we can tackle any problem. So, you might find a few Caltech grads who are very well-rounded and social...

MICA's PGDM program has a curriculum that’s constantly updated to reflect industry trends. First-year courses focus on marketing and strategic communication, while the second year allows for specialization in areas that align with career aspirations. The faculty are approachable, and the exams are structured to ensure we truly grasp the subject matter.
We also get a lot of hands-on experience through internships, which is super beneficial for our careers. The blend of theory and practice is what makes studying here so valuable.

I really believed MICA was out of reach for me initially, especially after getting rejected from a couple of other colleges. My CAT score wasn't stellar, but I was determined to give MICAT my best shot. After going through the rigorous admission process, including the GE-PI, I was surprised when I received my acceptance letter. Now, I'm enrolled in the PGDM program, and I can say that it was worth every bit of the effort.

MICA is a place that gets mixed reviews from its community. Some folks think it's not worth the hype, while others say it's a unique journey. Here's a straightforward take for those considering spending 20 lakhs to join the 2020 PGDM batch.

Let's talk about the downsides, since most other reviews highlight the good stuff, especially about campus life, which is indeed awesome. This is about the students, job placements, and value for money.

First off, the batch diversity is lacking. It's not just about having a mix of genders, but more about the variety of backgrounds. You'll mostly find students from Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, and Ahmedabad with pretty similar profiles.

The quality of the batch is probably the most disappointing aspect. Only about 20% of students come from prestigious colleges, and they're truly impressive. You'll see a few from places like St. Xavier's Kolkata, DU, and LSR. However, 80% of students are not up to par, and it's rare to find anyone from IITs, NITs, BITS, SRCC, or Stephens. Across my batch, senior, and junior batches, there were just 8 students from these top-tier schools among roughly 600 people.

Most of these 80% come from local colleges with minimal exposure, and their undergraduate degree often amounts to little more than three or four years of not much. Their academic backgrounds typically look like this: BBA, BCom, or BTech from some less-known college, with scores like 80-90% in 10th, 75-85% in 12th, and 65-75% in UG from a Tier 5 college.

I've come across students with a 5 CGPA from engineering schools in places like Mumbai or Indore, showing no creativity over two years in the course, which MICA supposedly emphasizes. Conversations with them can be as dull as talking to a piece of furniture.

While some might have worked hard to get into MICA (though their academic profiles suggest otherwise), it's more of a supply-demand situation where MICA gets tuition fees and students get jobs. Anyone claiming they're deeply passionate about MICA is likely exaggerating. The CCC program is a better fit for those who are truly passionate, creative, and hardworking.

Placements and internships can be hit-or-miss. However, the summer placement season is great for about 60% of the batch. If you manage to secure a good company during this time and get a PPO, your two years at MICA will be much easier.

Final placements can be disappointing. If your summer experience didn’t lead to a PPO, you'll face the same pressures during the final placements. One of the worst things is that your GPA from the first four trimesters isn't included in your CV. So even if you're the top student, it doesn't count much, and MICA tends to level everyone to the same playing field, regardless of GPA.

That said, MICA's placement policies are very student-friendly, unlike many other colleges. You have the freedom to accept or reject offers within a set timeframe. The placement committee treats everyone equally and doesn’t pressure you into accepting random jobs. If you don't want to go through the VIVO process (inside joke), it's entirely your decision. Big props to the placement team for that.
If you're thinking about trying your luck at MICA, aim for a good CAT percentile along with a decent MICAT score, and you might end up in a place full of surprises.
I'll try to share my positive experiences soon to give you a complete picture. Peace out.
Sri Venkateswara University is a great place to start your academic journey, with its peaceful environment and spiritual vibe. Here are some friendly tips for newcomers:

While education is important, remember that many successful people, about 90%, became millionaires without a degree. Focus on gaining skills like communication and computer literacy, as these are often more valuable in today's world.

Make use of the SVU library to read books and articles. Develop leadership skills and emotional intelligence too. Knowledge holds more value than just marks, as seen with Amartya Sen, the Nobel laureate in economics, who emphasized the importance of knowledge over mere grades.

Travel to gain fresh perspectives and maybe start a new venture. Remember Jack Ma's advice about finding opportunities in problems. Government jobs are becoming scarce, so consider self-employment or the private sector.
Live your life doing what you enjoy, ignoring unnecessary drama and negativity. Be true to yourself and avoid copying others, as this doesn't honor who you are. Build a team with shared goals.

Read newspapers to stay informed about societal happenings. Turn your savings into investments to tackle future inflation. Avoid the rat race and choose your own path. Spend weekends learning new skills, as they are your future financial tools. During tough times like recessions, these skills will support you. Best of luck, friends!

Before joining MICA’s PGDM-C, I wish I had realized just how much knowledge was waiting for me in the MICA Library. For two years, it’s like being near a gold mine of information. Ignoring the library while you’re there is like being thirsty next to a full well and not taking a sip. Take the time to dive into and explore the treasures within. The collection is carefully curated and well-maintained, and honestly, the MICA library could be studied as a subject on its own. Looking back, I wish I had made more effort to uncover the valuable resources it offers.
But since everyone has different expectations, here are a few things you might want to know before signing up for MICA:

From my experience with the PGDM (Communication) at MICA, the online courses are pretty good overall. The curriculum is fast-paced and updated regularly based on industry input, which I appreciated. Classes are interactive, and the faculty is approachable, making it easier to grasp complex concepts. The assessment structure is rigorous but manageable, so if you stay on top of your studies, you should be fine. Plus, the placement opportunities are robust, which adds to the course's value.

Honestly, MICA is a fantastic place, but whether it's worth 20 lakhs depends on your perspective. The Post Graduate Diploma in Management (Communication) gives you a unique blend of marketing and communication skills, which is great. The faculty is very approachable, and the curriculum is relevant to industry needs.

However, the hostel facilities could be better, especially in the second year. The high fees might feel a bit overwhelming, but the average final package of around 19 lakhs does provide a decent return on investment. If you’re passionate about this field and willing to put in the work, it could be worth it for you.

Though I've never been in the CCC program at MICA myself, I've heard from many folks who have gained a lot from it. A common thing I hear from CCC graduates is that the program really broadened their creative thinking. I get why you might be worried about job placements, but I've been informed that both the course content and the job placement situation have improved a lot recently.
To make the best choice, I'd suggest reaching out to some recent graduates on LinkedIn to see if the course aligns with what you're looking for professionally.

The college establishes 100% Summer and Final placements every year. Leading companies visit campus and recruit students regularly. Roles revolve around marketing and related functions. There are ample opportunities for every student, and after joining the college, one should be assured of getting a job.

Sri Ramakrishna College of Arts and Science (SRCAS) is a private autonomous college in Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu. Established in 1987, the college is affiliated with Bharathiar University. SRCAS is approved and recognised by UGC and AICTE. NAAC has accredited the institute with an ‘A+’ grade. SRCAS is one of the best arts and science colleges in India, especially in Tamil Nadu. In 2025, Collegedunia ranked SRCAS at 156 out of 259 best colleges in India, while, as per NIRF 2025, the institute achieved 76 overall rank among the best colleges in India.

Of the 30 UG, 10 PG, and PhD programs at SRCAS, B.Sc. is the flagship course, offered in 10+ specialisations with fees ranging from INR 52,000 to INR 92,000 in the first year. To be eligible, candidates must have passed 10+2 in science, and the college admits them directly based on their qualifying exam scores.

SRCAS’ 2025 placement data is unavailable as of now. According to the college’s released data for 2023-24, the highest package secured was INR 12 LPA, the average was INR 4.6 LPA, and the placement rate was 93%. Top recruiters include Amazon, Airtel, TCS, HCL, Infosys, Zoho, and more.

SRCAS has successfully concluded its 2025 admission period. Candidates seeking admission in 2026 can follow the tentative important events and dates for that year.
SRCAS is often ranked among the best arts and science colleges, especially in Tamil Nadu.
Collegedunia.com in 2025 ranked SRCAS as 96th out of 280 best science colleges in India, and 156th out of 259 arts colleges in India.
NIRF in 2024 ranked SRCAS as 56th out of 300 best colleges in India, which is an improvement from 86 in 2023.

SRCAS Coimbatore offers a wide spectrum of Undergraduate (UG), Postgraduate (PG), and Research (PhD/M.Phil.) programs across Arts, Science, Commerce, Management, Computer Science, and Social Work. At the UG level, students can choose from multiple specialisations in programs like B.Sc, BCA, B.Com, BBA, and BA, with eligibility primarily based on 10+2 scores.

SRCAS offers M.Sc., M.Com, MBA, MSW, MA, and M.Phil as PG courses, with eligibility typically requiring a Bachelor’s degree in a relevant discipline with at least 50% aggregate, along with merit or entrance scores depending on the program. The details for SRCAS Courses & Fees are mentioned in the table below.

Sri Ramakrishna College of Arts and Science admits students to its UG programs based on the 10+2 qualifying exam scores. For the B.Sc. program, candidates must have completed 10+2 in the science stream, while for BBA, B.Com, and BA, a 10+2 pass in any stream is accepted. Similarly, SRCAS admission to the PG programs is based on graduation scores in relevant disciplines; M.Sc. candidates must hold a B.Sc. degree, while M.Com and MA (Eng) candidates must hold B.Com and BA (Eng) degrees to be eligible. MBA candidates at SRCAS must have secured a minimum of 50% in graduation to be eligible and can apply via TANCET scores for admission.

SRCAS accepts TANCET scores for its MBA program. Although the 2025 cutoff has not been announced yet, aspirants can estimate it based on the 2024 cutoffs. The table below provides the SCRAS TANCET 2024 cutoff for the OC category:

Sri Ramakrishna College of Arts and Science has yet to release its 2025 placement statistics. Students at SRCAS have a high chance of securing placement offers, with 93% in 2024. The 2023-24 official data reports a package of INR 12 LPA as the highest of the year, with an average of INR 4.6 LPA.

Selva Venkatesh, a current student pursuing a B.Sc., claims that students can attend the SRCAS placement interviews at the end of the 3rd semester, where companies such as Infosys, Wipro, and TCS visit for recruitment. He claims the maximum salary package per year is approximately INR 24 LPA, and the average salary per year is INR 6 LPA. A student with a 9 CGPA or about 60% in semester exams is eligible for a campus interview.

Sri Ramakrishna College of Arts and Science offers comprehensive scholarship programs designed to support meritorious and economically disadvantaged students. Students who achieved excellence in academics and sports are granted financial assistance, as well as students with financial constraints. The college administration assists students during the application process.
Sri Ramakrishna College of Arts and Science operates on 16 acres of land, with a mix of nature and modern infrastructure. The campus is situated in the heart of Coimbatore city in Tamil Nadu.

Sri Ramakrishna College has fully furnished hostels for boys and girls, providing comfortable and safe housing to all its students. Hostellers have access to gyms, playgrounds, and indoor gaming facilities. The SRCAS hostel fee ranges from INR 76,000 to INR 90,000 per year, according to student testimonials on Collegedunia, as the college has not stated the fees on its website. Ans. SRCAS is among the best colleges in Tamil Nadu, and its rankings by reputed agencies support the notion. Similarly, Collegedunia ranked SRCAS as the 9th and 13th best science and arts colleges in Tamil Nadu, respectively.

Ques. How can one reach the RCAS campus?
Ans. SRCAS can be accessed by air, where the nearest airport is just 8 km from the campus, by rail, and by road.

Ans. Students have largely praised the faculty of SRCAS for being supportive and approachable. Teachers are known to emphasise practical knowledge and help students with their queries anytime during college hours.
Ques. How is the campus life and extracurricular activities at SRCAS?

Ans. Students describe the campus life at SRCAS to be fun and memorable. Students can engage in multiple clubs present at the college, such as theatre, music, photography, entrepreneurship, and environmental conservation.
